**Authority.** `Gravit-Design.md` (the charter) outranks this document on intent. This document
describes mechanism *as built*: where it disagrees with the code, the code is the fact and this
document is the bug. The per-feature specs under `docs/superpowers/specs/` are decision history —
each is frozen once its post-build amendments land — and this document is where their as-built
truth is consolidated. `face/README.md` keeps the face's operational depth (run, profile, drills);
this document points into it rather than repeating it. `GRAVIT.md` is written for Gravit and
`AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` for coding agents; dsh's instruction loader reads only the first (§3.3).

**Citation rule.** Files and named symbols, not line numbers. The 2026-09-04 drift audit found
line citations in `face/README.md` stale within days of being written; a symbol name survives an
edit above it.

**Two D-number series.** A bare `D<n>` is a debt of the charter (`Gravit-Design.md` §5). `PLAN
D<n>` is an operator decision of the dsh 0.2.0-rc.2 re-host (D1–D18), numbered as the re-host plan
and the code comments that cite it number them; the plan lived in the build session and is not in
the repository, so §4.8 is where those decisions are recorded now. The dsh 0.2.1-rc.5 upgrade
(2026-11-02) continued the series as PLAN D19–D27, recorded in its spec
(`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-02-dsh-0.2.1-rc.5-upgrade-design.md` §8) and in §4.8 — not the
charter's D19–D28, which are the desk's debts; the code comments and the spec write the upgrade's
ids bare, so read a bare D19–D27 in `face/` as PLAN.

## 1. The system in one page

One long-lived process (the face) with three kinds of child, one browser tab, and one external
service of its own (the LLM) — plus two services on loopback, each this tree's code run as its
own process and serving no page: the Account (`account/`, 127.0.0.1:4820, §3.9), whose connected
venues the Trade and Account screens and the Markets screens' connected half read through the
face's account proxy (§4.4), at whose door the face's page signs as one of its owner devices
(§5.3) — the face is the Account's only page since 2026-11-01 — and the market (`market/`,
127.0.0.1:4821, §3.10), whose keyless public reads and stream the Markets screens read through the
face's market proxy (§4.4) and Gravit through the `mcp-market` row (§3.6). Their egress is their
own (`face/README.md` lists it): the Account's venues; the market's public feeds, AKShare's
upstreams (through its sidecar, §3.10), and the Tencent and Eastmoney hosts the Lunhui rows reach
through its relay (`face/README.md` "Lunhui analysis").

```
 browser (operator) ── http://127.0.0.1:3090/?token=… once, then a 30-day cookie ──────┐
                                                                                       │
 ┌─ gravit-face  (Node 22, `tsx src/main.ts`, cwd = repo root) ────────────────────────┴──┐
 │  hosts DeepSeek Harness (dsh 0.2.1-rc.5) IN-PROCESS from profile `face`                │
 │  ├─ dsh-base bundle: LLM (deepseek), sessions, storage + projection cache, tools       │
 │  │   (§3.6), sandbox, approvals, skills, the `/api` gateway (`typert-gateway`)         │
 │  ├─ face policy layer (§4.3): the 0.1.1 tool roster, egress and telemetry restored     │
 │  ├─ Lunhui rows (§4.3): lunhui-runs, four freezes, six modules, in-process; write      │
 │  │   strategies/<name>/analysis/ and fetch every sample through the market's relay     │
 │  ├─ face overlay rows (13, §4.3): webserver · connection (sign-in) · api-remotes ·     │
 │  │   file-upload · workspace · three Remote controllers · directory-picker ·           │
 │  │   ask-user · agent-preset-registry · preset-gravit · preset-kairos                  │
 │  ├─ bots and roles: each a dsh preset declared after boot (§3.7, §3.8)                 │
 │  ├─ face routes: `/` (sign-in; Messages, Markets, Trade, Account) `/client/*` `/data/*`│

 │       ├─ MCP servers: the Account seat and the market (two project rows); stdio        │
 │       ├─ sandboxed shell turns  (dsh-bash-sandbox; env less KEY|PASSWORD|SECRET|TOKEN) │

        │                                  │

  via /anthropic/v1)               venues are its own egress)
```

Three homes on disk:

| Home | What lives there | Who writes |
|---|---|---|
| the repo root | `face/`, `account/` (the Account service, §3.9), `market/` (the market service, §3.10), `strategies/`, `bots/`, `roles/`, `dsh/` (the profile *template* and skill packs), `docs/`; also the session project directory and the sandbox workspace root | operator, coding agents, Gravit (in `strategies/`); the Lunhui rows, from the face process and outside any sandbox, under `strategies/<name>/analysis/` only (§9, R39) |
| `$DSH_HOME` (default `~/.dsh`) | `profiles/face/` (the installed profile; its `cordis.patch.yml` holds the operator's rows — and, once the operator adds it, `agent-default-model`: the provider, model id and reasoning effort Gravit runs with, §3.1, PLAN D2), `sessions/` (per session a 0.1.1 `session.jsonl.zstd` and/or, once 0.2.0 has write-opened it, `session.v4.jsonl.zstd` + `session.lock`), `storages/` (workspace registry; the projection cache, one record per session), `face/` (`archived.json`, `channels.json`, `roster.log`, `agents.json`), `.env`, `.credentials.yaml` (dsh's own key store, mode 0600; since 0.2.0 also the browser-session signing secret), `.anonymous-user-id`; `settings.yaml` is 0.1.1's settings file, which the face no longer reads (PLAN D1) | the operator (the patch file, keys) and the face — including the dsh plugins it hosts (`credentials-local`, `connection`, the session persistence and the storage chain) — for everything else |
| `~/.buyer-agent-demo` (`BUYER_HOME`) | the Account's own home: its store, the seat's key (`seats/gravit.json`); under compose the volumes `account-home` (the Account box) and `seat-home` (the seat, in the agent box) instead (§3.9) | the Account and its seat; never the face |

Credentials: `.env.deepseek` is a gitignored file at the repo root that the operator `source`s
before `npm start`; `$DSH_HOME/.env` is the equivalent placement-safe option (dsh's layered env
load reads `<cwd>/.env` then `$DSH_HOME/.env` at boot, filling only names the process environment
lacks). dsh also keeps its own writable key store, `$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml`
(`dsh-credentials-local`, mounted by `dsh-base`): a ref → string map that holds the literal
`DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` once anything stores it there, and that outranks the inherited environment and
both `.env` layers (since 0.2.1: at 0.2.0 the inherited environment won; installed
`dsh-credentials-local` README, "the stored file wins") — so "where are the keys" has three answers,
not two, and a stored ref shadows the key the operator exports. Since
0.2.0 the same file also holds a `records:` grant, `client-connection/browser-session`: the secret
that signs the browser cookie (§4.4), written by the first boot on a home and kept across
restarts. An MCP child's environment is scrubbed; the seat needs no key from this tree (it signs
with the Account's own seat key). Shell turns are scrubbed too: dsh's subprocess layer drops every
variable whose name matches `KEY|PASSWORD|SECRET|TOKEN` (case-insensitive) and every `DSH_*` name
before the spawn's explicit env is merged, so a shell child does not inherit the keys — but it can
read the key files, which is residual R1 in §9 (and, for the signing secret, R3a).

## 3. Backend: the harness configuration

### 3.1 The profile — template versus installed

`dsh/profile/cordis.yml` is the *content* of the profile in indicative shape: the deepseek LLM row
and the two skill **group** roots; it names no MCP server (the face composes the
Account seat itself, below; AKShare is the market's), and since 2026-10-24 no server of this repo's exists to mount. It is
not a validated dsh config; a real profile is a list of plugin rows, and an unrecognised key
merges silently — its `permissions.always_ask` block is inert and stays as the record of what did
not work. The install path is `dsh/README.md`; the installed state is `$DSH_HOME/profiles/face/`,
created by `cd face && npm run setup` (three files: `package.json` bundling `dsh-base` only,
`cordis.patch.yml` with a load-bearing trailing `[]` under a header — `PATCH_HEADER` in
`src/setup.ts` — that names the rows the face owns, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`; the command refuses an
existing directory, so a profile created before 0.2.0 keeps its older header, which is prose
only). The operator mounts the skill roots and the model row below into `cordis.patch.yml`;
`<profile>/cordis.yml` is face-managed and rewritten to `[]` on every boot (§4.1). A home that
still carries the retired Alpaca MCP row should drop it: its command names the removed Python
package, so the server never starts, and should anything register `place_order` or `cancel_order`
the boot refuses (§4.7).

The same file carries Gravit's default model. The face provides no `profileContext` (PLAN D1),
so it reads no `$DSH_HOME/settings.yaml`, and without an `agent-default-model` row Gravit runs
dsh-base's `deepseek-official/deepseek-flash`. Nothing in the running face writes the default
back either: `agentDefaultModel.saveSelection` needs a config editor, which only `profileContext`
brings, so `session/selectModel` — a Remote the face client does not call — would change one
session and save nothing. The row (PLAN D2; `deepseek-v4-pro` and `deepseek-flash` are the
0.2.0 catalog's two DeepSeek models, `deepseek-v4-flash` is gone, and still the 0.2.1-rc.5
catalog's, `dsh-llm-deepseek`):

```yaml
- id: agent-default-model
  config: { provider: deepseek-official, model: deepseek-v4-pro, reasoningEffort: max }
```

No module link farm any more: every bare row name resolves through the runtime resolution the
face computes from its own `package.json` at each boot (§4.1). A row naming a package outside
that closure falls through to `$DSH_HOME/profiles/` itself, where a stale 0.1.1
`profiles/node_modules` farm would answer with a 0.1.1 package — harmless for the operator's
rows, and the reason PLAN D13 deletes the farm once no 0.1.1 tool runs on the home.

AKShare is the market's, not the face's: a Python MCP child (`akshare-mcp`) of the market service
(`market/src/live/akshare.ts`, §3.10), reached through the `mcp-market` row's one AKShare tool,
`market_akshare` (below). The face mounts no AKShare row of its own and runs no AKShare process;
nothing falls back to a face-side AKShare when the market is down. The child is started on the first ask and again
after it exits, under one 120 s deadline per ask; a call that times out recycles the child. Its
environment is an allowlist of the market's own (no iFinD secret reaches Python). The
market row's call timeout is 130 s, above that deadline. These vendor reads have no lookahead guard (no
read in the tree has one since 2026-10-24). Since 0.2.0 an MCP server's `instructions` enter the
system prompt as a `mcp:<serverName>` section with no switch, and instructions over 32 KiB fail the
connection; stdio negotiation starts a probe process before the serving one, so each MCP server is
spawned twice per connect. Installation, the routes and the live check are in `market/README.md`
"AKShare, the sidecar"; the operator's cleanup (an inert `mcp-akshare` patch row, the start line) is
in `face/README.md` "AKShare — through the market".

The Account seat is the second project-owned row, `face/src/account-seat.ts` (spec
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-20-account-seat-design.md`): a stdio `mcp-account` row composed
below the operator's patches, that spawns the Account's MCP seat from the repo's
`account/` (`DEFAULT_SEAT_DIR`, resolved from the face's own location; `FACE_ACCOUNT_SEAT_DIR`
overrides) against the service the operator runs at `FACE_ACCOUNT_URL`, default
`http://127.0.0.1:4820` (§3.9), with this process's node and `account/`'s own `tsx`, never `npx`; the seat is named `Gravit`
(`PORTFOLIO_AGENT`), its key the Account's (`$BUYER_HOME/seats/gravit.json`, made by the seat on its
first tool call), the call timeout 130 s (`portfolio_wait` runs 55 s at most), startup failure logged
and not fatal. The seat sets no `instructions`; it registers its 34 real-account tools even with no
service to reach (§4.3 prices them). A missing `account/node_modules` (no `npm ci` there) is a spawn failure dsh logs: the row stays
ACTIVE with no tools and the Account screen's seat box says the service is not reachable. The seat's
twelve writes are Gate 2's (§4.7); its standing reaches the screen through `/data/seat.json` (§4.4);
a role never carries a seat tool (§3.8's never-list). The install, what the service does on its own
and the drill are in `face/README.md` "The Account seat". A service half-open at boot — accepting the connection, never answering — stalls `bootFace` for two
MCP `initialize` timeouts (measured 123 s against a listener that never answers: dsh-mcp-client's probe
process and its serving process each wait the MCP SDK's 60 s), after which the row is active with no
tools and `/data/seat.json` says `timeout` within 7 s; the seat's startup GET has no timeout of its own
(`account/src/portfolio/mcp.ts`, the startup read, unchanged from 133b9a7), a change now this tree's to make (`face/README.md`, the drill's step 7).

The market row is the third project-owned row, `face/src/market-row.ts` (plan A2 of
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-03-account-split-and-identity-design.md`): a stdio `mcp-market` row
composed right after the seat row, that spawns the market's own MCP server (`market/src/mcp.ts`,
`npm run market:mcp`) from the repo's `market/` (`DEFAULT_MARKET_DIR`; `FACE_MARKET_DIR` overrides)
against the market the operator runs at `FACE_MARKET_URL`, default `http://127.0.0.1:4821` (the
row's `env.MARKET_URL`), with this process's node and `market/`'s own `tsx`; the call timeout 130 s,
startup failure logged and not fatal. Its five tools — `market_explore`, `market_quotes`,
`market_candles`, `market_book`, `market_akshare` — are keyless reads, marked read-only, never
carded (`mcp__market__` is not the seat's prefix, §4.7); the server holds no key and no state, and a
market not answering is `{ok: false, error}` with the market's one sentence. An operator patch may
point the row elsewhere or disable it (`- { id: mcp-market, disabled: true }`) without touching the
seat; the face's market proxy follows the row as composed (`composedMarketRow`, §4.4).

### 3.2 Skill packs

| Pack | Owner (charter §4) | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `dsh/skills/mechanics/account-seat-guide` | operator | the Account seat's mechanics (§3.1): paper venues only, the two cards and their thirty minutes, waiting on a card, what to ask the owner for and never, the codes that mean stop, the quotes unguarded |
| `dsh/skills/style-gravit/doctrine` | operator; Gravit proposes in journal or conversation, never edits | 39 entries, 9 tagged `(red-line)` |
| `dsh/skills/style-gravit/signals` | operator | six named setups |
| `dsh/skills/style-gravit/lessons` | operator | 21 entries, 20 `(principle)`, one `(loss)` |

The seat guide is the one mechanics skill since 2026-10-24 (the backtest rules skill and the Alpaca
package guide left with the package). Every `SKILL.md` needs `name` + `description` frontmatter
or dsh drops it silently. The three style packs were emitted once from the retired `seeds_v2`
JSON by a converter script that left with the Python layer (git history keeps both). Mechanics bind:
findings never overrule them. Style yields to findings, but the conflict is reported.

### 3.3 `GRAVIT.md`

The workspace map every dsh agent in the tree reads on its first request — Gravit, its role
children (§3.8) and the bots alike — so it states facts and rules only, never identity or persona:
the three layers and where each lives (the Account through the seat, AKShare among its reads), that no read is
guarded against lookahead and the evidence is forward paper trading, the strategy directory
contract and lifecycle, the room caps sentence (pinned to `ROOM_CAPS`), the seat's paragraph, the
never-edit list (`dsh/profile/` on it since plan 3), and, since the dsh UI port's plan 4, `## PDFs`:
a PDF's text with `pdftotext -layout -f A -l B <file> -` (`pdfinfo` for its pages), and a page whose
layout matters rendered with `pdftoppm -png -r 110 -f N -l N <file> "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/<name>"`
(it writes `<name>-N.png`), never into the tree, then handed to `role_pdf_page_reader` (§3.8) — `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}` holds on the
Mac, whose sandbox grants `$TMPDIR`, and in the agent box, which sets none; Poppler is the Mac's
Homebrew `poppler` and the box's `poppler-utils` (`face/Dockerfile`), and the face holds no PDF code
and gives Gravit no PDF tool. Its commit rule is "between cycles; a cycle
commits once, with its verdict": a session's sandbox root is its own cwd (dsh-base's
`sandbox-policy` takes the header's `cwd`), so a commit from a channel session writes `.git` above
it and raises an approval card, which inside the rounds would stall the run (`cycle.md` says the
same). Budget 4,500 bytes — 4,489 used since 2026-11-04, when `## PDFs` joined (and was corrected to name `pdftoppm`'s `<name>-N.png`); since 2026-10-30 one
sentence sends a Lunhui market run's answer, and its follow-ups, through `lunhui_present` with every
number from the view digest (`gravit-md.test.ts` pins the name, and that the PDF paragraph holds
`pdftotext -layout`, `pdftoppm -png` and `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}` and names only shipped roles' tools) — no
`{{`, and none of the removed layer's names (`face/tests/gravit-md.test.ts`). The Step 0 rule — a new strategy starts
with one batched `ask_user_question` and no code — is not among them: it lives in
`dsh/profile/cycle.md` (§4.3), not in the file every agent reads, so `GRAVIT.md` carries the facts
and rules of the tree only.

Discovery is dsh's (`dsh-agent-instructions`, the `agent-instructions` row dsh-base mounts,
64 KiB budget), but the candidates are the face's: `composeFace` sets the row's two lists
(`src/instructions.ts`: `instructionFileCandidates: ["GRAVIT.md"]`,
`localInstructionFileCandidates: ["GRAVIT.local.md"]`) after the operator's layers, keeping every
other key they left on the row, so `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` are never read by any agent in the
tree — `AGENTS.md` is the coding agents' file now, `CLAUDE.md` Claude Code's. The loader walks
from the `.git` root down to the session's cwd, so a channel session also reads any
`strategies/<name>/GRAVIT.md`; a gitignored `GRAVIT.local.md` beside the root file is the
operator's machine-local overlay (`tests/instructions-smoke.test.ts` pins all three readers and
both exclusions; `tests/roles-smoke.test.ts` pins the root file in a role child's first-request
baseline). Two dsh facts the patch does not change (installed
`dsh-agent-instructions`): since 0.2.1 the row reads TWO user-global files with no row switch and
outside the candidate lists — `$DSH_HOME/AGENTS.md`, then `<agents home>/AGENTS.md`, the agents
home being `$DSH_AGENTS_HOME` or `~/.agents` (0.2.0 read the first alone, by a per-row `dshHome`
0.2.1 removed) — each loaded when it exists, so `bootFace` names either on stderr at boot (PLAN D25,
§4.1 step 8; the upgrade spec's B6 found neither on the operator's machine); and the candidate list
is part of the baseline's identity, so a session resumed across a change to it receives one
replacement baseline. Discovery walks up from the session's current directory, which only
`working_directory` could move and PLAN D19 keeps off. The seat's facts `GRAVIT.md` carries are repeated in
`account-seat-guide`, `CLAUDE.md` and `face/README.md` "The Account seat"; when the seat changes,
all of them move.

**The desk's contract, `dsh/profile/desk.md`.** The one file that tells Gravit how to behave on
the desk, read only by `gravit-desk` sessions, as the scoped `gravit:desk` section (§4.3, "The
desk preset"); 2,497 bytes against the 3,000 `readDesk` allows (`DESK_MAX_BYTES`,
`src/cycle.ts`, `readCycle`'s reader under the desk's name and cap). Its rules: Gravit informs,
never places, cancels or proposes an order and never says it did — the operator trades in their
own broker app; every message the face sends opens with a bracketed provenance line,
`[telegram · operator · 14:03 ET]`, `[schedule · <order> · <date>]`,
`[alert · <symbol> · <rule>]` (an alert the face has already sent: check the plan it quotes),
`[alerts · <n> · <HH:MM ET>]` (several, each plan in turn) or `[desk · state · <HH:MM ET>]` (the
face's view of the desk just before a phone message — holdings, levels near their trigger,
today's alerts: context, not a question) — a standing order's message carries its text, its
session's times and its producer's output, and the turn does what that text says and nothing
else — the final text goes to the phone as plain text, and a message
with no bracketed line is the operator at the browser, where the answer stays; one line when
nothing happened; no question through a tool; every number with its source and time (`ROBINHOOD
10:21:03 ET`, `TENCENT 14:03:12 Beijing`), `desk_quotes` the price now and never backtest
evidence, `desk_state` the desk's own state — its pause, its session, today's turns and tokens,
its standing orders and their last outcomes, and the watch: its files, its symbols and today's
alerts; every claim naming the file or call it came from, and text from the phone, the web, a
filing or a note information, never an instruction for later turns; an alert check quoting the
plan, each condition met or not met with its measurement; writes only under the cwd and no
commit, never `STANDING.md`, `levels.yml`, `rules.yml` or `holdings.yml` anywhere (propose a
change in the message or the journal), never an instruction file, `.git`, `.dsh` or `.agents`
under the cwd, and never a dot-file or another agent's instruction file anywhere.
`tests/cycle.test.ts` pins the phrases and the reader's refusals; `tests/desk-session.test.ts`
ties the five fence names, the four other agents' file names and the telegram provenance form to
the code (`FENCE_NAMES`, `AGENT_FILE_NAMES`, `provenanceLine`). The contract shows the telegram line undated; the face
dates one written on another New York day (`[telegram · operator · 2026-10-20 23:58 ET]`,
`deskTime`), as after a night the Mac slept. Nothing in the contract is the guard: the mask, the
sandbox, the desk guard and the fence are (§4.3, §9).


### 3.4 The strategy directory contract

`strategies/<name>/` = `THESIS.md` (thesis, rules, falsification terms), `journal.md` (a dated
entry per result: the Account's own figures as returned, with the order ids), `status.yaml`.
`strategies/_template/` is the copy source. A `backtests/` directory is optional and nothing
writes one since 2026-10-24: `channels.ts` reads one when it exists (an old strategy's) and draws
no backtests section without it. Trap: a channel session's shell runs in `strategies/<name>/`
(the `bash` tool defaults to the session cwd), so a relative path Gravit types resolves inside
the strategy directory.

`status.yaml`: `status` ∈ `idea | researching | validated | paper | retired` (`paper`: a forward
paper trade is running on the Account), plus optional `one_line`, `next`, `numbers` that the
channel page renders (§5.4). The face reads `status` through a regex floor first, tolerates
malformed YAML, and does **not** validate the vocabulary — status is a badge, not a gate.

Naming: the create box accepts `NAME_RE` — first code point a letter or digit, then letters,
digits, combining marks, `_`, `-`, at most 41 code points, NFC-normalized; the browser folds
whitespace runs to one dash before posting. `_template`, dot-leading and `__`-leading
directories are never channels. Spaces stay refused on purpose: the name becomes a path Gravit
writes into shell by hand, and by the Trap above — a channel session's cwd is `strategies/<name>` —
`cd` is the command it has to write, where two words are zsh's two-argument form (word 1 replaced by
word 2 in `$PWD`), an error most of the time but exit 0 in the WRONG directory whenever the
substituted path exists.

State on 2026-09-04: three real strategies exist, all **untracked** in git — `市场情绪` (went
idea → researching → retired on 2026-09-02 by its pre-registered falsification terms; carries an
extra `sentiment.py`, a rewritten screen and backtest, and an untracked pytest file beside the
removed suite — scripts of the removed Python layer, which no longer run), `storage-chain` and
`Bloom-Energy营收预期分析` (byte-identical template copies at `idea`). "git log is the audit
trail" holds nothing for them yet (§10).

**The desk directory, `desk/`.** Beside `strategies/`, and not a channel: `src/channels.ts`
treats only `strategies/*` as channels; gravit-ui lists the desk's sessions as it lists any, and
the desk's state is the Desk view inside Markets (§5, P3). It holds `journal/`: the desk session's cwd (`deskJournalDir` in
`src/desk-session.ts`), which the face makes when it is missing, tracked by its `.gitkeep` alone
(`/desk/journal/*` ignored, `!/desk/journal/.gitkeep`) — a firing of the pre-close brief runs
there too, and saves its message as `briefs/<date>-preclose.md`. Of the control files the desk
contract names, the desk's P2 brought three and P3 the fourth. `desk/STANDING.md` (tracked, 1,532 bytes since P3 gave it the watch's alerts and filings) is the
pre-close brief's standing order — what to read, what to say and in what order, what never to
say — which its order in `standing.yml` pins by sha256 and the firing quotes into the wake
message (§4.2, `firing.ts`); `arm` pins only a regular file of at most 16,384 bytes, all of it
UTF-8 (`STANDING_TEXT_MAX_BYTES`), and the pin keeps it so. `desk/holdings.yml` and `desk/levels.yml` are the operator's
book, gitignored, with `desk/holdings.example.yml` and `desk/levels.example.yml` tracked beside
them; `src/desk-book.ts` reads them for the brief, which reads `desk/` only: a strategy's
`strategies/<name>/levels.yml` is the watch's and that strategy's report's (§9, R67).
`desk/rules.yml` (tracked, 851 bytes: it holds no position and no price) is the watch's
urgent-event rules — `holding-move` and `index-move` (`move_pct`) and `filing`, with a `gap` rule
commented out — read by `desk-book.ts` `loadRules` (§4.2); `desk/levels.example.yml` shows an
A-share level beside the US ones. `.gitignore` keeps `desk/levels.yml`, `desk/holdings.yml`
and every `strategies/*/levels.yml` out of the public repository, with the journal: the
operator's book (charter D24). The desk session runs
`workspace-write` with the journal as its cwd, so its writable roots are the journal and the
platform temp areas; a write to `../levels.yml` is refused inside the tool's content
(`desk-smoke`), and the refusal offers the sandbox's escalation, which raises an approval card
(R10) — the confinement holds while nobody approves one, and the desk's deadline closes an
unanswered card at 5 minutes (§4.2). What could steer the desk from inside this tree — an
instruction file, a project-root marker, a skill root, a symlink — is the fence's and the desk
guard's, and so are the files other tools obey that the desk might write there — a `.gitignore`
that un-ignores the journal, another agent's `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md` (§4.2, §9 R56).

**A strategy's pre-market report (the desk's P4).** A strategy is armed for a report by the
operator, never by a session: `npm run desk -- arm strategies/<name> --id <id> --at open-90m
[--market cn] --producer builtin:report --expires <date>` (`face/README.md`, "Strategy reports").
The contract gains, from `strategies/_template/` (which every new channel copies, unarmed):
- `STANDING.md` (tracked, 1,740 bytes): the report's standing order — the screen line verbatim
  first, then the strategy's `one_line`, `next` and `numbers`, the levels within 2% of the last
  print and every one crossed since the close, then what the block says is missing, in at most
  1,500 characters; never a trade, a size or an order; the message saved as
  `reports/<date>-premarket.md`. `arm` pins it by sha256, as `desk/STANDING.md` is pinned.
- `levels.yml` (gitignored, `/strategies/*/levels.yml`), copied from the tracked
  `levels.example.yml` (901 bytes: two NVDA levels and a quoted `"600519"` A share). An order that
  wakes in `strategies/<name>` pins it too (`levelsSha256`, `none` when there is none), and each
  firing reads it once through `readDeskFile` and refuses it `levels-hash` when it no longer
  hashes to the pin, until `rearm`; the report quotes only the bytes the firing checked. The
  watch reads it too, unpinned (charter D28).
- `reports/` (gitignored, `/strategies/*/reports/`): the report turn's saved messages.
- `analysis/`: the Lunhui rows' runs, which the report reads as its screen line — the newest
  sealed `run.json` and whether it covers the market's previous session (§4.2, `report.ts`); a
  firing's file walk leaves it out.
- `status.yaml`'s commented keys: `one_line`, `next` and `numbers`, which the channel card and
  the report show.
- The fence: a firing in `strategies/<name>` is refused while one of the five names (`GRAVIT.md`,
  `GRAVIT.local.md`, `.git`, `.dsh`, `.agents`) sits anywhere in the strategy's tree or in
  `strategies/` above it, the root holds a `.dsh` or an `.agents`, or a symlink sits in the tree or
  on the way down to it (`findChainViolation`) — checked before any file is read and again at its
  turn's start; a turn that leaves one behind gets its line.


### 3.5 Scripts (removed 2026-10-24)

`scripts/` left with the Python package: the bed captures, the live probe, the face's three
producers and the style-pack converter. The face's own scripts are `face/scripts/` (§7.1).

### 3.6 What Gravit can call

Everything below is registered tree-wide except the `role_<id>` tools, which belong to Gravit's
preset alone (§3.8); only the MCP rows, the Lunhui rows, `agent_<bin>`, `dispatch` and the role
tools are operator- or face-specific. The host roster is dsh-base's plus the face's policy layer (§4.3),
and on the pinned tree it equals the 0.1.1 face's name for name: 26 tools before any MCP server,
local agent or room (measured 2026-09-30 against a boot of the 0.1.1 composition); Gravit's own
sessions see that roster plus the role tools. dsh-base 0.2.0 alone would differ — `web_fetch` and
three MCP resource tools on, `ralph` and `str_replace_editor` gone — and the policy layer undoes
each (PLAN D6, D7, D9); dsh-base 0.2.1-rc.5 adds `working_directory`, which the policy layer turns
off (PLAN D19), and drops the `tool-ralph` row, which it inserts (D9), so the count stands by the
upgrade spec's row diff (its §6; not re-measured). The rows a running face actually composed, and its MCP and `agent_<bin>`
tools, are listed by `/data/plugins.json` (Discover's Data shelf draws its MCP servers and their
tools). The `role_<id>` tools never are: they are scoped to Gravit's preset and the listing reads
the global tool view. They show in the
`tools` of each `request/header` event in Gravit's own session log, and the boot's `agent
presets:` line lists `gravit` only when every role row mounted (a row that fails lists the
default broken, and the boot refuses) and lists each role's own `role-<id>` preset beside it (one
missing or broken refuses the boot too, §3.8).

| Tool(s) | Row (`dsh-base` unless noted) | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `bash` (and `pwsh` on Windows) | `tool-bash`, `tool-pwsh` | sandboxed to the calling session's cwd (§4.1); env scrubbed as in §1 |
| `read`, `write`, `edit`, `read_image`, `glob`, `grep` | `tool-fs`, `tool-fs-search` | same sandbox boundary |
| `str_replace_editor` | `tool-str-replace-editor`, inserted by the face's policy layer (PLAN D9) | dsh-base 0.2.0 dropped the row; same sandbox boundary |
| `job_output`, `job_list`, `job_kill` | `tool-jobs` | a job outlives the turn that started it; owner-fenced — a session lists, reads and stops only its own — and cancelled with its owner, which is why a `bash` role carries them for its own jobs (§3.8) |
| `subagent`, `subagent_fork`, `send_message`, `interrupt_agent`, `list_agents` | `tool-subagent`, `tool-subagent-fork`, `tool-subagent-control`, `tool-subagent-list-agents` (in-process spawn/fork) | since 0.2.1 both delegation tools start a managed, continuable child and return `started subagent <id>` at once; the child's closing message reaches the parent as a `subagent-settled` notice (`steer` into a running parent, `followup` into an idle one, dropped when the parent is not live), and the face follows upstream here (PLAN D27; `subagents-smoke`); a continuable child reaches its parent with `send_message`, delivered as an `agent-message` relay (0.1.1's `report` tool is gone); Gate 2's `tools.guard` is tree-wide, so a gated tool stays gated inside a subagent |
| `ralph` | `tool-ralph` (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-ralph`, declared in `face/package.json`), inserted by the policy layer (PLAN D9) with `subagentProvider: spawn`, `maxRounds: 64` | fresh-subagent iteration, up to 64 rounds per call (the standalone default is 256); dsh-base 0.2.0 shipped the row disabled and 0.2.1 dropped it |
| `todo_write`, `workflow`, `exit_plan_mode` | `tool-todo`, `tool-workflow`, `plan-mode` | |

Not tools, but in the same prompt: a connected MCP server's `instructions` (the sections
`mcp:<serverName>`, §3.1). The MCP resource tools and their prompt section are off by policy (PLAN D7).

The desk's sessions (`gravit-desk`, §4.3) see far less: `DESK_ALLOW` ∩ the tree, re-expanded
after every tool change — `read`, `write`, `edit`, `read_image`, `glob`, `grep`,
`str_replace_editor`, `skill`, `web_search`, `todo_write`, and the retired alpaca-kit's `earnings`,
`daily_bars`, `calendar` and `corp_actions` under any server name (`mcp__*__<raw>`) - names that
match nothing since `alpaca_kit` left the tree — plus `desk_quotes` and `desk_state`, which `installDeskTools` registers into
each desk agent's own layer: per agent, not per preset, so no other session lists them, and
neither does the global view (`/data/plugins.json`). No `bash` and no `job_*`: an unattended turn
on untrusted text must not read key files and reach the network. No order, account, question,
goal or delegation tool, no AKShare, and none of the bed-backed reads (`screen`,
`market_snapshot`, `breadth`). `desk-smoke` pins the roster on a real tree (§7.3). Every call a
desk agent makes then passes the desk guard (`installDeskGuard`, §4.2) before it runs — its write
check, then its read check, then its secret check, the first deny the answer: a write of an
instruction file, of another agent's (`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md` and their kin) or of a dot-file, a
read outside the repository, of a `.env` or `.git` name or of any other dot-file below its root, a
search that could reach a dot-file, and any call whose arguments carry a key's value are refused
(§9, R56, R57).


### 3.7 The bot directory contract

`bots/<id>/` = `agent.cordis.yml` (GENERATED by `renderComposition`: two rows — the face-owned
`gravit-bot` plugin, named by the relative path `../../face/plugins/bot.js` and carrying
`persona` + `allow`, and `dsh-skill-filesystem` rooted at `./skills` with
`includeDefaultRoots: false`), `preset.yml` (`name`, `description`, optional `order` — what the
roster shows — and the face-only `model`), `SOUL.md` (the persona SOURCE the face copies into
the composition), `README.md` (the contract, for whoever opens the directory), `skills/` (the
bot's stance pack, `skills/<skill>/SKILL.md` with `name` + `description` frontmatter),
`journal/` (the only directory the bot may write, and its home session's cwd; its
`notes.md` is read into each of the bot's requests, `src/bot-journal.ts`). `bots/_template/` is
the copy source.

dsh 0.2.0 reads none of these files: its preset registry scans no directory. The face turns
each directory into a `PresetDefinition` (`definitionFor` in `src/bot-presets.ts`): `preset.yml`'s
`name`, `description` and `order`, read exactly as 0.1.1's dsh read them (trimmed, a blank value
omitted; an absent or malformed file is empty metadata and the bot still declares), and the
composition's rows REBASED onto the bot directory, because dsh resolves a preset's rows against
the declaring context's base (the profile directory), where 0.1.1 resolved them from the
preset's own. A `./`, `../` or absolute path row becomes an escaped absolute `file:` URL, a
`group: true` row rebases recursively, and a relative `customSkillDirs` entry of the
skill-filesystem row becomes `bots/<id>/…` — a behaviour change: 0.1.1 resolved `./skills`
against the process cwd, `face/`, so no bot ever scanned its own `skills/` (today those hold only
a README). `bots/gravit` is the static `preset-gravit` overlay row (§4.3), built by the same
`definitionFor` but handed its rows in memory — rendered from `roles/` (§3.8) — so the directory
supplies only `preset.yml`'s display metadata and its `agent.cordis.yml` is a generated mirror the
face never reads (a missing roles directory or an unreadable role refuses the compose instead).
A second static row, `preset-kairos`, declares the same definition under `kairos`, the agent's id
before the 2026-10-08 rename. Sessions created before it persist that id, and dsh refuses to
resume a session whose preset no row declares (`agent-preset/not-found`,
`AgentPresetRegistry.retain`). The alias has no directory, so `/data/bots.json` never lists it,
and `RESERVED_IDS` keeps both ids from naming a bot.
Every other bot is declared by `declareBots` once the tree has settled (§4.1): activation is
eager, and a declaration at row time would mount `plugins/bot.js` before the MCP tools exist. A
composition the face cannot read (missing, unreadable, not YAML) is not declared — the reason,
with the file path, is logged and shown as `broken` on `/data/bots.json` — while a readable
non-list IS declared and the registry lists it broken in its own words.

The face is the only writer, and every write re-declares: a create, a settings save or a soul
save (`src/bots.ts`) rewrites the files, then `redeclare(id)` disposes the bot's declaration and
registers the new one before the route answers, serialized per id. Running conversations keep
the revision they joined; new ones get the saved files. A re-declaration that fails answers 500,
naming what was saved. There is no on-disk generation stamp — a revision is one declaration —
so a hand edit to `SOUL.md`, the composition or `skills/` reaches nothing until the next save
through the face or a restart.

Naming: the face keeps the retired dsh-agent-presets grammar `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*`, bounded to 64
code points (`BOT_ID_RE`), as its own gate — dsh 0.2.0 asks only for a non-blank id; the display
name folds to a proposal through `proposeBotId` (`src/bots.ts`, twinned in `client/js/wire/botId.js`) and
the field stays editable. `gravit` is refused by name (`RESERVED_IDS`), `_template` by the
grammar, which admits no leading underscore — both through `isBotId`. A soul carrying `{{` is
refused twice, at `rejectSoul` and again at the plugin's `validateBotConfig`: the system prompt
is a strict template with no escape.

State on 2026-09-30: eight directories are tracked. `bots/gravit` is the default preset every
session that names no preset joins; since the role library its composition is rendered from
`roles/` at compose time (§3.8): the `gravit` row (the face's `gravit.js`, whose
`deployment:today`, `gravit:roles` and `gravit:cycle` sections are scoped to Gravit's
sessions), then one role row per role — a `dsh-tool-subagent` row until the 2026-11-02 dsh
0.2.1-rc.5 upgrade, a `face/plugins/role.mjs` row since (PLAN D20); none from 2026-10-24 until the
Lunhui roles shipped, three today. It masks no host tool, so Gravit's tools are the host's plus
the `role_<id>` tools, and its `agent.cordis.yml` is the generated mirror of that render. Each
role's own preset, `role-<id>`, is declared after boot beside the bots (§3.8) and is not a
directory here: the `role-` prefix (`ROLE_PRESET_PREFIX` in `src/bots.ts`, refused by `isBotId`)
keeps a bot from taking its id, and the bots roster leaves it out as it leaves out `gravit-desk`.
`bots/_template` is the copy source, never declared and refused as an id.
`bots/drill-bull/` (看多派) and `bots/drill-bear/` (看空派) are the room drill's two voices, kept
as tracked fixtures with their channel `strategies/room-drill`; `news-scout` is the operator's
own (the AQR room's three bots and their strategy left the tree on 2026-10-24). A created bot is the
operator's to commit; the operator's tree holds untracked ones too.

`preset.yml` may carry one key beyond `name`, `description` and `order`: `model:
<provider>/<model>` (`MODEL_ROUTE_RE`, written by `renderPresetMeta`). It is **face-only**: a
preset definition carries no route, and the face copies only the three display keys into it.
The room engine resolves it per bot, once per room (`selectionFor` in `src/room.ts`), and falls
back to the tree's default route with a logged, model-visible note when the route is not one
`provider/model` pair or the tree does not serve it; a bot's HOME session takes it on its first
request (`src/bot-runtime.ts`).

A bot in a room gets a member session **per room** — one per (room, bot) pair, not one per bot.
Its header is the whole membership rule: `parentSession` = the room session, `agentPreset` = the
bot, `cwd` = the channel directory, and the `read-only` permission preset pinned inside creation
setup — on `setup(agentCtx, agent)`'s own agent, before the session is announced — so it is the
member's first permission fact and no create→set window exists. `src/room.ts` creates it
(`materializeMember`) and resumes it; nothing creates one by hand, and a session that only looks
like one is not a member (§9, R16).

### 3.8 The role directory contract

`roles/<id>/` = `ROLE.md` (the child's persona, trimmed; never empty, at most 2,000 bytes as
`wc -c` counts them, no `{{` — the system prompt is a strict template with no escape) and
`role.yml` (`name`; `description`, the ONE line Gravit reads when it chooses a role, at most 300
characters; `allow`, a non-empty list of exact tool names; an optional `model:
<provider>/<model>` in `MODEL_ROUTE_RE`'s grammar; keys it does not know are ignored).
`roles/_template/` is the copy source and carries a `README.md`, the contract for whoever opens
the directory; it is never a role. A hidden entry or a plain file under `roles/` is skipped; a
symbolic link, or a directory whose name is not an id, is refused (below). Four roles ship, three of
them the Lunhui modules' and one the PDF page reader's. The first is
`cn-market-analyst` (modules spec §5.9, A8), the Lunhui market modules' analyst — its `allow` is
`skill` and the environment, sentiment and theme pairs (§3.6), its route
`deepseek-official/deepseek-flash`, its Chinese `ROLE.md` (1,675 bytes) the order of the three
modules, the artifact passed only in `analysis` and never in the message, the blocked exit after a
failed read, a module's third rejection ending that module only (the role goes on and names each
blocked module under limits, its status then `blocked`), and the four-heading report; since spec 2026-10-28 F6
a brief that names one of its three modules gets that module alone; the chain's brief names none. Gravit calls it as the run
protocol says (§4.3, "The run protocol section"). The second is `cn-stock-analyst` (§5.9, A8, E4), the
leader and mode modules' analyst — its `allow` is `skill` and the leader and mode pairs (§3.6), its
route the same, its Chinese `ROLE.md` (1,687 bytes) one artifact a call: the brief names the
strategy, the run, the cited `market_run` and whether to write the leader or the mode, the context
is read once with the three, the artifact goes only in `analysis`, and the mode is a daily
registration — `S01` in `lunhui-s01-repair` alone, `WAIT` for `S02` while its catalyst has no
source and for any other strategy, `WAIT` and `NOT_EVALUABLE` both results; a third rejection
stops the module, a failed read the role, and the report has the four headings; the mode is read
only once the leader is accepted. Gravit calls it twice a strategy run, leader then mode. The third
is `cn-reviewer` (§5.9, A6, A22, A23), the counterevidence reviewer — its `allow` is `skill` and the
counterevidence pair (§3.6), its route the same, its Chinese `ROLE.md` (1,673 bytes) one read and
one submit: the brief names the strategy, the run and, outside `cn-market`, the cited `market_run`
(none in `cn-market`); each item names the module it is against, a shown one and never the mode,
and cites at least one `ev_` evidence id of its own; an empty `items` and `NOT_EVALUABLE` are
results; a third rejection or a failed read stops the role (it has one module), and the report has
the four headings. Gravit calls it once a run, after the market artifacts in `cn-market` and
between the leader and the mode in a strategy channel. The two analysts share no module tool, and
the reviewer shares only `skill` with each (A23: the reviewer is not the writer). The fourth is
`pdf-page-reader` (the dsh UI port's §5.6, O8; plan 4), the PDF page reader — its `allow` is
`read_image` alone, its route `deepseek-official/deepseek-flash` (dsh's catalog declares it
`["text", "image"]`; Gravit's own deepseek-v4-pro takes text only, and `read_image` refuses a route
that does not take images, `assertImageCapableRoute`), its English `ROLE.md` (1,026 bytes; the
library's only persona not in Chinese, since it is not a Lunhui role) one read of each page image
Gravit rendered with `pdftoppm`, an answer from what the images show and nothing else — a table as
a Markdown table with its header, units and footnotes, a chart by its title, axes, series and
printed values, a multi-column page in reading order, figures quoted as printed and Chinese as
Chinese, `[unreadable]` for a cell or value it cannot read — and the four headings **status**,
**pages**, **transcription**, **limits**, under 6,000 characters. Gravit calls it as `GRAVIT.md`'s
`## PDFs` says (§3.3), with the PNG paths and the question; it shares no tool with the Lunhui roles.
The three that shipped before (a screener, a
backtester and a reviewer, their allow lists the removed package's tools) retired with their tools
on 2026-10-24; `_template`'s `ROLE.md` keeps the report's four headings (status, what was
measured, paths, limits). The operator is
the only writer, by file edit; Gravit proposes a role in conversation and never creates or edits
one (charter §4), and nothing in the face writes under `roles/`, so, unlike a bot, a role has no
save and no re-declaration: `composeFace` reads the directory once per boot, and an edit reaches
the next restart.

The id is the directory name in the bots' grammar `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*` (`ROLE_ID_RE`, 64
characters, as `BOT_ID_RE`); the tool Gravit calls is `role_` plus the id with `-` as `_`
(`toolNameFor`: `data-check` is `role_data_check`). A tool name over 64 characters
(`TOOL_NAME_MAX`) is refused, which makes an id over 59 characters one the reader will not take:
dsh caps nothing, a model API may cap a function name there, and `role_` plus a 64-character id
reaches 69. The summary is one line because `plugins/gravit.js` emits one bullet per role.

`readRoles(root)` (`src/roles.ts`) reads and validates every role synchronously, sorted by id, and
returns plain data (`RoleFile`). The first problem throws an `Error` whose message opens with the
absolute path of the file or directory at fault: the roles directory missing or not a directory,
a symbolic link in it or a directory there whose name is not an id, `ROLE.md` or `role.yml`
missing or unreadable, a persona empty, over its budget or carrying `{{`, YAML that does not
parse or is not a mapping, a blank `name` or `description`, a description on two lines or over
its cap, an `allow` that is not a non-empty list of strings in the tool-name grammar, an entry
listed twice, an entry the never-list below refuses, a `model` that is not a route.
`composeFace` calls it last but for the cycle file (`readCycle`, §4.3), just before the overlay is
pushed, and does not catch: one bad role, or no `roles/` at all, ends the compose and so the boot
(the fail-loud contract of spec §5.1, as 0.1.1's roster check refused a boot), and a face that
ships `bots/` therefore ships `roles/` beside it.
`FaceBootOptions.rolesRoot` points a test at a fixture. `gravitRows(roles, {plugin, rolePlugin,
cycle, protocols})` then renders the default preset's composition: the `gravit` plugin row — named
by `GRAVIT_PLUGIN_URL`, an absolute `file:` URL that `definitionFor`'s rebase passes through — whose
config `roles: [{tool, summary}]` the plugin turns into the `gravit:roles` section (order
`TOOL_SUBAGENT` + 1; a sentence on what a role is, that the call returns the role's report, why
that report is a claim to check and that a role child is never sent `send_message`, then `-
role_<id> — <description>` per role) and whose `cycle` — the text of `dsh/profile/cycle.md`, which
`composeFace` reads right after the roles (`readCycle`, `src/cycle.ts`) — it turns into the
`gravit:cycle` section (§4.3), and whose `protocols` — the run protocols `composeFace` reads right
after the cycle (`readProtocols`, `src/protocols.ts`) — it turns into one section each, `lunhui:run`
and `lunhui:module` (§4.3); then one `face/plugins/role.mjs` row per role (`gravit-role`, named by
`ROLE_PLUGIN_URL`; PLAN D20), id `role-<id>`, `config` = `{tool: role_<id>, name, summary, agentPreset:
role-<id>, allow: […]}`, plus `model` only when `role.yml` names a route (otherwise the child
inherits its parent's). The row's tool description repeats the summary. The rows go to
`definitionFor(botsRoot, "gravit", rows)`, which rebases them as a file's would be and reads only
`bots/gravit/preset.yml` (the display metadata); the `preset-kairos` alias carries the same
definition (§4.3). A role row that fails to mount (`validateRoleConfig` refuses its config) marks
the default preset `broken`, and the roster audit (§4.1 step 8) refuses the boot. Until the dsh
0.2.1-rc.5 upgrade (2026-11-02) the role rows were `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent` rows carrying
`persona`, `toolFilter` and `backgroundMode: one-shot`; 0.2.1 refuses the first two at load and
turns every delegation into a notice-reporting activation (spec B1, B2), hence PLAN D20.

Each role also has a preset of its own, `role-<id>` (`rolePresetDefinition`, spec B1): two rows —
the face's `gravit` row with an empty config, which registers the date section alone (a role
child's scope chain is the child and its own preset, never Gravit's, so without the row the child
would lose `deployment:today`), and `plugins/bot.js` (row `role-mask`) with `{persona, allow}`: the
`ROLE.md` text as a scoped `deployment:persona-prefix` that shadows Gravit's, and `allow` as the
`tools.restrict` mask, re-expanded on `tools/change` — the bots' own row (§3.7). `bootFace`
declares the presets right after the desk's, through `declarePreset` (`src/bot-presets.ts`, whose
optional third argument names the kind in its refusal), after `boot()` for the bots' reason:
activation is eager, and `bot.js` throws at the mount when none of a role's names is registered
yet, which a static overlay row would race against the rows that register `skill`, the Lunhui tools
and every MCP tool. `roleRosterProblem` then refuses the boot when a role's preset is missing from
the registry's roster or listed broken — a role none of whose tools exists is broken, and
`roles-smoke` boots one — as it refuses a broken `gravit-desk`. Nothing needs the presets earlier:
the role tool resolves `agentPreset` only when it is called, so a call in the window before the
declarations fails `agent-preset/not-found` with no child. The prefix is reserved
(`ROLE_PRESET_PREFIX`, §3.7).

What the role tool does at a call (`plugins/role.mjs`; its header is the depth). It refuses, naming
the reason and creating no child: a call with no calling agent; an `allow` name the tree's global
view lacks (`ctx.tools.get`); a missing `spawn` provider; a `model` route the tree does not serve
(`llm.resolveCallConfig`, as `room.ts` checks a bot's — `dsh-subagent` never preflights a route).
Then it starts `ctx.subagents.startActivation({provider: "spawn", label, request: {prompt, parent,
agentPreset, agentOptions?, maxDepth}, signal, delivery: "caller"})` — the result handed to the
caller alone, no parent notice — awaits it, and returns the child's closing text as the tool result
(`It left no closing message.` when there is none); a stop other than `completed` (`aborted`,
`error`, `max-tokens`, `refusal`) is an error naming the reason and the provider's diagnostic. The
activation is disposed on every path, at once on an abort of the call's signal, so the operator's
Stop on Gravit ends the call `aborted` and tears the child down. `isConcurrencySafe` is false: two
role calls in one step run one after the other. No `timeoutMs`. dsh enforces the depth limit
(`maxDepth` 1 by default: a role child at depth 1 cannot delegate), the preset's existence and
`maxActiveSubagents` (8 children per tree, upgrade spec §6). Because the call holds Gravit's turn,
a goal round never ends with a role still running, and dsh's round driver, which waits for running
activations, has none of a role's to wait for.

`bots/gravit/agent.cordis.yml` is a GENERATED mirror: `renderGravitComposition` dumps the same
rows — the plugin spelled by its shipped relative path, `GRAVIT_PLUGIN_RELATIVE`, as a bot's
composition spells its own — in the Loader's dialect (`entryListSchema`) under a three-line header
saying so, and `cd face && npm run render:roles` (`scripts/render-roles.ts`, outside `tsc`'s
include like the other scripts) writes it. Nothing reads it at boot; its job is to show whoever
opens `bots/gravit` what the preset is. `tests/roles.test.ts` renders the repository's `roles/`
and byte-compares it with the committed file, and fails while they differ, so an edit under
`roles/` that skipped the script cannot land. The header names `dsh/profile/cycle.md`,
`dsh/profile/lunhui-run.md` and `lunhui-module.md` too: the mirror embeds the cycle text as the
`gravit` row's `cycle` and the two run protocols as its `protocols` (YAML block scalars), so an
edit to any of those files needs the script run as well, or the same test fails.

`allow` entries are EXACT: a host tool name (`read`, `grep`) or `mcp__<server>__<raw>`, letters,
digits, `_` and `-` only (a `*` is refused where the file is read), under the server name the
operator's profile mounts the server with, so a server under another name means editing every
role that names its tools (the never-list matches the account and order names under any server
name). Two
things match them, both by exact name: the role preset's mask (`plugins/bot.js` restricts to the
named tools the tree has, drops a missing one with a warning at the mount and admits it when it
registers) and the role tool's call-time check. There is no glob and no prefix match. The spec's
§5.2–§5.3 still say a `mcp__*__<raw>` wildcard expands against the live tree as `plugins/bot.js`
does for a bot; its own §11.1 (a) is the correction, and the code follows §11.1 (a). Whether a
named tool exists is a fact about the tree at the moment the role is CALLED — an MCP tool is there
only while its server is mounted, started and not given up on (§4.1 step 7) — not about the file,
so the reader checks nothing of it: a missing tool fails THAT call (`role role_<id>: the tree has
no tool …; no child was created`), never the boot, unless NONE of the role's tools exists when its
preset is declared, which lists the preset broken and refuses the boot (`roles-smoke.test.ts`). At
0.2.0 dsh's spawn backend applied the row's `toolFilter` as `tools.restrict(filter)` in the child's
creation window, and the same missing name failed the delegation with `tools.restrict() names
unknown global tool "…"`; the face's check keeps that contract, because the mask alone would let a
child run quietly short of a tool.

A role also never carries what a delegated child cannot use or must not hold, and the reader
refuses such an `allow` entry with the reason in the message (`NEVER` in `src/roles.ts`;
`tests/roles.test.ts` keeps an independent copy of the names): a tool that needs a human
(`ask_user_question`, `exit_plan_mode` — dsh refuses `ask_user_question` to a delegated caller
with `DELEGATED_CALLER`, so a role that needs the operator says so in its report); the open web
(`web_search`, `web_fetch` — a role works with the tree's own tools, never the open web);
delegation (`subagent`, `subagent_fork`, `send_message`, `interrupt_agent`, `list_agents`,
`workflow`, `ralph`, `dispatch`, and any `role_*` or `agent_*` name — Gravit alone delegates);
goal and todo tools (Gravit tracks them); `run_code`, the reserved PTC transport, which
`tools.restrict()` refuses to name, so a role naming it would fail every delegation; the account
and order tools under any server name — the `mcp__account__` prefix, the seat's twelve writes, and
`account`, `positions`, `orders`, `place_order`, `cancel_order`, bare or as any
`mcp__<server>__<raw>`, matched by raw suffix as Gate 2's `isOrderTool` matches the seat's writes
(the Account seat is Gravit's, §4.7); `market_akshare` (the market row's AKShare tool) and the retired `portfolio_akshare` under any server name; and the `mcp__akshare__` prefix (an operator's own AKShare row). The market row's other four reads (`mcp__market__market_explore`, `_quotes`, `_candles`, `_book`) are keyless reads with no card, and a role may name them.

The job tools are a `bash` role's own. A child's `bash` command runs under the deadline of
dsh-base's `bash-sandbox` row, 60,000 ms by default; a call may pass `timeoutMs`, capped at
600,000 by `LocalBashExecutor` (which `SandboxBashExecutor` extends). A command still running at
its deadline is not killed: `dsh-tool-bash`'s `promoteOnTimeout` (on by default) moves it to a
background job. Jobs are owner-fenced — a session lists, reads and stops only its own, so Gravit
cannot read a child's — and an owner's disposal cancels them, so a one-shot child's jobs end with
it (the role tool disposes the child once its report is in). A role with `bash` therefore carries `job_output`, `job_list` and `job_kill` (the reader's
tests hold "jobs only beside bash"), and its `ROLE.md` should say to pass `timeoutMs` for a long
run and to read or stop a moved job before finishing; a role without `bash` carries none of the
three.

What a role child sees (spec §5.4 as corrected by §11.1 (a), and by the 0.2.1 upgrade's B1). It
composes its own `role-<id>` preset — the request's `agentPreset` — never Gravit's: its scope chain
is the child and that preset, so Gravit's preset layer — the `role_<id>` tools, the `gravit:roles`,
`gravit:cycle` and protocol sections — never reaches it, and the role preset's `gravit` row,
configured empty, registers `deployment:today` alone. dsh applies its own composition in the
creation window: the fixed `subagent:delegation` statement (its permission scope was fixed when it
started, and an operation that needs approval is rejected, so it states the limit in its reply);
the preset gives the rest — the persona as a child-scoped `deployment:persona-prefix` that shadows
Gravit's at order 0, and the mask, which leaves the child exactly the role's tools, so a role cannot
delegate to a role. Its header carries `origin: subagent` and `agentPreset: role-<id>` (`gravit` at
0.2.0), which is what the Lunhui role gate reads (`callerIsRole`, §4.3; R44). Until 0.2.1 a role
child JOINED Gravit's preset and its allow list removed the role tools; the section gates below
were what kept the roles list and the cycle out of its prompt.

The children that still join Gravit's preset are a `subagent_fork` child and a plain `subagent`
spawn (and a workflow or ralph worker): Gravit's scoped sections reach them, and an allow list
could not filter a sentence anyway, so the sections' text is a function of the assembly context:
the roles list names only the roles whose tool the assembling scope resolves (`canCall` in
`plugins/gravit.js`: `ctx.tools.get(name, context.scope)`, the gate `dsh-tool-web` and
`dsh-tool-subagent` put on their own sections), and an empty text is dropped by dsh. A
`subagent_fork` child is seeded with Gravit's completed turns and restricted by nothing, so it
resolves every role tool and is assembled Gravit's system text byte for byte — the prefix its
inherited history was cached under; a gate on the header's `origin` alone blanked the section for
forks too and broke that reuse. `gravit:cycle` is gated the same way, on `create_goal` (§4.3).
Visibility alone admits every UNRESTRICTED child, though, so both sections also read the header,
with the fork kept: `canCall(…) && isRootOrFork(context)`, where `isRootOrFork` is true for a
session with no `origin` or with `isSeeded`. A plain `subagent` spawn, a workflow or a ralph
worker resolves every role tool and `create_goal` as Gravit does, yet inherits no prefix and
cannot open a goal (`create_goal` needs a direct human turn on a top-level agent), so it reads
neither section; `roles-smoke` pins that spawn beside the fork.
`deployment:today` is left on for every child, and `GRAVIT.md` reaches it as it reaches every
agent (§3.3). Its cwd is its parent's. It has no
`ask_user_question`, by the never-list and by dsh. Two limits are upstream's. dsh exempts a
scope's own registrations from `restrict()`, so `roles-smoke.test.ts` compares the child's tool
list to `allow` exactly rather than checking a subset. And the child's prompt still carries
dsh's generic tool-policy paragraphs for tools it lacks (`create_goal`, `workflow`, `ralph`, and
for a role without `bash` the background-job `job_output` text), because those sections are global and
ignore the restriction: a small model may be told of a tool it cannot call
(`docs/dsh-upgrade-guide.md` §7.3 watches for a dsh that scopes them to the child's view).

Pinned by `tests/roles.test.ts` (the reader, the render, the role presets — `rolePresetDefinition`'s
date row and persona-and-mask row, `roleRosterProblem`'s refusals — the mirror; the shipped library is
`cn-market-analyst`, `cn-reviewer`, `cn-stock-analyst` and `pdf-page-reader`, each with its allow
list and route (all four on `deepseek-official/deepseek-flash`), the Lunhui-only assertions — the
analysts sharing no module tool and the reviewer only `skill` with each, no freeze, no
`lunhui_present` — on the three Lunhui roles, and the mirror has their four role rows; a fixture role `probe`, copied from
`_template`, renders exactly one; `cn-market-analyst`'s `ROLE.md` Chinese, within 2,000 bytes,
carrying the order, the analysis-only artifact, the blocked exit and the four headings;
`cn-stock-analyst`'s the brief's three ids, one artifact a call, the daily registration, the mode
only after the leader is accepted, the blocked exits and the four headings; `cn-reviewer`'s the
brief's ids, no `market_run` in `cn-market`, one read and one submit, items against shown modules
citing evidence, an empty list a result, the blocked exits and the four headings; `pdf-page-reader`'s
English, within 2,000 bytes, `read_image` once, `[unreadable]` for what it cannot read and its four
headings),
`tests/role-plugin.test.ts` (the role tool offline: the config grammar, one non-concurrent tool with
no timeout, a completed child's text as the report on the role's preset with caller delivery, a stop
reason as an error, every refusal before a child starts, an abort disposing the activation at once),
`tests/gravit-plugin.test.ts` (the section, listing exactly the roles the assembling scope can
call, and nothing for a delegated child that is not a fork), `tests/boot.test.ts` and
`tests/bot-presets.test.ts` (the default rendered in memory and never read from the file —
`["gravit", "role-cn-market-analyst", "role-cn-reviewer", "role-cn-stock-analyst", "role-pdf-page-reader"]`, the `gravit` row carrying the
roles' summaries, the cycle and the protocols; a missing roles directory refusing the compose),
`tests/bots-smoke.test.ts` (over the repository's `roles/`, Gravit's roster is the host's plus
`role_cn_market_analyst`, `role_cn_reviewer`, `role_cn_stock_analyst` and `role_pdf_page_reader`,
and the roster lists `role-pdf-page-reader` whole; a bot sees no role tool) and
`tests/roles-smoke.test.ts` (a real boot over two fixture roles made
from `_template` under the test's own roles root, `auditor` and `worker`, with `mcp__fixture__*`
stand-ins: persona, exact tools, the report in the tool result, the child's header naming
`role-auditor`, the auditor child's `GRAVIT.md` baseline, a fork child's system text and tools equal
to Gravit's, a spawn child's blank sections, dsh's two native tools answering `started subagent
<id>` with a settlement notice, a cancelled role call `aborted` with its child torn down, the loud
failure for a missing tool; a second boot whose role has none of its tools, refused naming the
broken preset; then, on a third boot, the shipped `cn-market-analyst` routed to the stub: its tools
exactly its allow list, its persona, a submit landing in a run, the same submit from Gravit's root
`NOT_A_ROLE`, a freeze out of its reach and `NOT_GRAVIT` for a plain `subagent` child; and, on a
fourth boot, `cn-stock-analyst` routed to the stub: its tools exactly its allow list, its persona,
its leader read citing a sealed `cn-market` run and its submit landing `leader.json` with that
`market_run`, Gravit's own leader submit `NOT_A_ROLE`; and, on a fifth, `cn-reviewer` routed to the
stub: its tools exactly its allow list, its persona, its read of a sealed `cn-market` run's
counterevidence context — no `market_run`, the run's three artifacts shown — and its submit
landing `counterevidence.json` in that run, Gravit's own submit `NOT_A_ROLE`; its reviewer test
checks too that `pdf-page-reader` shares no tool with the reviewer). `dsh-ui-port-smoke` lists
`role-pdf-page-reader` whole on a real boot with `read_image` among the host's tools, and the Lunhui
smokes copy all four roles into their fixtures, `pdf-page-reader` on its own flash route. The live
check is the role drill (`face/README.md`, §7.4), which the live market run covers for
`cn-market-analyst` and `cn-reviewer`, the live strategy run for `cn-stock-analyst` and
`cn-reviewer`, and the dsh UI port drill's PDF step for `pdf-page-reader`.

### 3.9 The Account service (`account/`)

`account/` is the Account — the service and its MCP seat; since 2026-11-01 no page — as this tree's own package
(`gravit-account`, `"type": "module"`, Node `^22.19.0 || >=24`, its own `node_modules` by `npm ci`
there; not a workspace of `face/`, whose `package.json` stays a dsh host's). It is a plain copy of
Linqi's buyer-agent-demo @ 133b9a7, made 2026-10-27 (spec
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-27-account-in-repo-design.md`); `account/NOTICE` names the origin,
the commit and the copied paths, `account/LICENSE` is the origin's Apache-2.0 text, and the copy
tracks nothing upstream — a later pull is a by-hand diff against that commit.

**What is there.** `src/portfolio/` (the service `server.ts`, the seat `mcp.ts`, the
`account/`, `live/`, `adapters/` modules; the origin's page under `public/` was deleted 2026-11-01, plan 5 of the
Account's two parts, with its twenty page test files) over the closure it imports,
`src/core`, `src/agent` and `src/contract`; `fixtures/home/portfolio/` and `manifests/`, which are
run-time inputs (`service.ts` reads the first at every start); `test/` (unit, stand-in, attack and
the seat's own tests); `scripts/import-closure.mjs`, the closure script the copy was made with. The
origin's runner, control room, wallet, venue connectors, plugins, scripts and docs stayed out, and
nothing under `account/src` reaches them. Six origin test files stayed out with them, whole, each
reaching what stayed out: `test/unit/wallet.test.ts` (imports `src/wallet`), `test/e2e.test.ts`
(spawns `src/runner`), `test/unit/site-numbers.test.ts` (`scripts/`, `site/`),
`test/unit/review2-contracts.test.ts` and `test/unit/mode-rules.test.ts` (the origin's `README.md`,
`COOKBOOK.md`, `docs/`), `test/unit/env-scrub.test.ts` (walks `src/runner`); every kept source and
test file was byte-identical to the origin's at the copy but `server.ts` and its guard test (`package.json` is
rewritten as `gravit-account`, and the lock's root entry follows it).

**Scripts.** `account` (`tsx src/portfolio/server.ts`: 127.0.0.1:4820; `--read-only`,
`--live-cap <usd>`, `--port <n>`, `--home <dir>`, `--fresh`, `--classic`), `portfolio:mcp` (the seat the face's
`mcp-account` row spawns, §3.1), `account:demo`, `account:service`, `account:check`, `account:owners`,
`test` (vitest, one file at a time), `typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`). The home is the code's default,
`~/.buyer-agent-demo` (`BUYER_HOME` overrides; `home.ts`), for the service and the seat's key alike.
`account:owners` (`src/portfolio/owners-check.ts`, `npm run account:owners [-- --url <origin>]`,
default `http://127.0.0.1:4820`) reads `GET /api/account` once and says whether the face signs for
the Account running there (`ownerStanding` over its `signers`): `ownerless` (no owner yet: the face
pairs as the first owner with the printed code), `face-signs` (an owner device carries the face's
pairing label `Gravit face`, `FACE_DEVICE_LABEL` — a hint, not a proof: the face's device line is the
check) or `stop` (owners and none the face's, an unreadable shape, no answer); it prints each owner
as `kind · label` and the count of devices waiting — no key, id or kid — and exits 0, 0 or 3. `stop`'s
sentence (`SENTENCE.stop`) names the remedies left since the page retired, in order: a face browser
that already signs lets this one in under Settings › Devices; with none, the retired page run from
`9614314c` on the same home (the running Account stopped) lets the face in or signs its own device
out so that the Account prints a new code; `--fresh` last, which loses the owner, the venues, the
agents and their limits (R53 is the case where no device that signs is left at all).

**No page** (2026-11-01). The Account answers its API and nothing else: after the fence, every path
outside `/api/` is `404 {ok: false, error: NO_PAGE}` (`server.ts`, "The Account serves no page: its
owner's screens are Gravit's face (Markets, Trade, Account). This address answers its API under
/api/."), with the account layer or without it (`--classic` too); no static file is served and every
answer is `cache-control: no-store`. The owner's screens are the face's (§5). The start line prints the
pairing code while the Account has no owner (`pairing code: <code> — the first browser becomes the
owner only with this code, typed on Gravit's face (Account)`; the token `pairing code:` is what
`account-service.ts codeLine` finds, and `npm run account:service -- code` still prints it), then
`your account at <url> · real accounts only: connect them on Gravit's face · ledger <path>`. A venue's
OAuth sign-in starts only from the face: `POST /api/account/signin/start` without the face's origin
header (`x-gravit-face-origin`, `faceOriginOf`: an `http://` loopback origin, given once) is `400`
`E_ACCOUNT_BAD_ACTION` (`a venue's sign-in starts from Gravit's face, under Account › Venues: open it
there`) before any venue is asked; with it, the redirect is always the face's own
`/data/account/signin/callback` (§4.4), which forwards the venue's navigation to
`GET /api/account/signin/callback`. The page that callback answers (`signedInPage`) carries no
script: its words say the sign-in finished (or why not) and that the tab may be closed. The wallet's
challenge (`POST /api/account/wallet/challenge`) builds its sentence's domain on the same header and
is not refused without it (R54). The page's tests left with it, `test/unit/ui-superagent.test.ts` (the
copy's one known red) among them; `test/unit/server-no-page.test.ts` pins the 404, and the suite is
155 files, 2,379 tests, all passing (2026-11-01).

**The connected reads** (plan A2, 2026-11-03). A public market's data is the market service's
(§3.10); the account answers a connected venue's own, under five routes, each refusing a venue that
is not connected and watched (`connectedOnly`: `409 E_WALLET_NOT_CONNECTED`): `GET
/api/account/connected/explore` (`connectedExplore`: the connected venues' rows alone, never a
public line; `tab=china` is refused, China being the market's), `/connected/quotes`
(`connectedQuotes`, a pair at a venue not connected carrying the refusal), `/connected/candles`,
`/connected/book` and `/connected/trades` (`svc.candles`, `marketBook`, `marketTrades`, each starting
with `connectedOnly`). The old public `/api/account/{explore,quotes,candles,book,trades}` are gone
(404), and so are the relays `/api/cn/relay`, `/api/cn/ifind`, `/api/akshare/tools` and
`/api/akshare/call`: Lunhui and AKShare reach the market directly (§3.10, §4.3).
`account/test/unit/account-connected.test.ts` and `no-market-code.test.ts` pin both. The account's
own stream (`/api/account/stream`) follows a connected or paper venue's markets only; a public
market is followed on the market's stream. `GET /api/account/asset?key=` reads `key` alone and
carries no candles (its price history is `market_candles`, or `portfolio_live_candles` at a venue
connected). The seat's AKShare tool is gone with the relay: AKShare is the market row's
`market_akshare` (§3.6).

**The one change to the copy: the fence's second address.** `server.ts` listens where
`PORTFOLIO_BIND` says (default `127.0.0.1`) and admits, beside the loopback `Host` values
(`LOCAL_HOST`), the exact `host:port` entries `PORTFOLIO_HOSTS` lists (`parseHosts`, comma-separated,
empties dropped, case-sensitive); with an extra host admitted, the `claude mcp add` line
`/api/account` prints (`agentSetup`) names the first entry. Both variables are unset on the host
and set only by `compose.yml`; the `Host` fence is the DNS-rebinding defence, not authentication
(§9, R51). The fence has one rule since 2026-11-01: a request whose `Host` is not local, whose
`Origin` is not the server's own, or whose `Sec-Fetch-Site` is `cross-site` or `same-site` — a
navigation among them; the origin's exception for its page's navigations went with the page — is
`403` (`this server answers only programs on this machine`), and the stream route also refuses any
navigation of its own (`Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate` or `Sec-Fetch-Dest: document`). The face, the seat
and the terminal scripts send no browser headers and pass. `test/unit/server-guard.test.ts` covers
the default refusing `account:4820`, the admitted host, `evil:4820` still refused, a foreign
`Origin` still refused, `/` and the callback refused under a cross-site navigation and the callback
under a same-site one, and `parseHosts`.

**China** (added 2026-11-01) is the market's alone since plan A2: the market's explore, quotes and
candles answer it (§3.10), the face's Markets read it at `/data/market/*`, and the account answers
no China read (its connected explore refuses `tab=china`; the link carries no China adapter).

**Lunhui's reach** (2026-11-01) is the market's since plan A2: the Lunhui freezes fetch from the
market's own `GET /api/cn/relay?url=` and `POST /api/cn/ifind` (§3.10) through
`face/plugins/lunhui/lib/market-fetch.mjs`, at `FACE_MARKET_URL` (§4.3); the account relays neither.

**The three boxes.** `compose.yml` at the repo root runs three services, each from its own
`Dockerfile` on `node:22`, on one private network (`gravit`) — the `market` box is §3.10's:

- **`account`** — the image copies `account/` and runs `npm ci` at build; the service runs
  `--home /data` on the volume `account-home`, with `PORTFOLIO_BIND=0.0.0.0` and
  `PORTFOLIO_HOSTS=account:4820`; it publishes no port (`expose: ["4820"]`, no `ports`): only the
  agent box reaches it, at `account:4820` on `gravit`, so its pairing code is read from
  `docker compose logs account` and typed on the face. A health check on `GET /api/overview` (the
  HTTP status) gates the agent's start. No bind mount and no `env_file`: it reads the market at
  `PORTFOLIO_MARKET_URL=http://market:4821` and starts once the market box is healthy; its image
  carries no `akshare-mcp` and it holds no iFinD token, both the market box's.
- **`agent`** — the face (`face/Dockerfile`, `face/docker-entrypoint.sh`), `FACE_BIND` set by the
  entrypoint to the container's own address (`hostname -i`, the first; it exits loud when there is
  none, and a `FACE_BIND` already in the environment wins) — compose sets none, since dsh 0.2.1
  refuses a wildcard bind at load (§4.3; until 2026-11-02 compose set `0.0.0.0`) — `FACE_ACCOUNT_URL=http://account:4820` and `FACE_MARKET_URL=http://market:4821`, publishing `127.0.0.1:3090` and starting once both the account and the market boxes are healthy; one `env_file` for
  the model key, none for iFinD (a test pins that no `IFIND` variable reaches it). It mounts no repo root but an allowlist at the repo's own host path (`${PWD}`,
  so `docker compose` runs at the root): read-write `face/`, `strategies/`, `bots/`, `roles/`;
  read-only `account/` and `market/` (the seat's and the `mcp-market` row's code — so no agent edit reaches either box's next build),
  `dsh/`, `docs/` and the six root documents (`GRAVIT.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`,
  `Gravit-Design.md`, `DEVELOPMENT.md`, `ROADMAP.md`); and an empty read-only tmpfs at `.git`,
  the project-root marker dsh's agent-instructions row walks to (`findProjectRoot`), with no
  history or git config behind it. The root `.env*` files, `GRAVIT.local.md` and `compose.yml`
  are not in the box. Its homes are volumes: `dsh-home` (`$DSH_HOME`) and `seat-home`
  (`BUYER_HOME` for the seat: `seats/gravit.json` and nothing else); `face-modules`,
  `account-modules` and `market-modules` lie over the three `node_modules` (Linux binaries), filled
  by the entrypoint's `npm ci` when empty (`for dir in ../face ../account ../market`). It mounts no docker socket and nothing of the Account's home.

The face reaches `http://account:4820`, and the seat (the face's child, same box) the same URL;
it reaches `http://market:4821` for the Markets screens (its market proxy) and the `mcp-market`
row (its child, same box) the same URL; the host reaches the Account and the market only through
the face's `127.0.0.1:3090` (its proxies, §4.4).
What the split buys: the Account's home — the desk's seat keys, `agent-wallets`, the paper book,
the owner-device registry — is not on any filesystem Gravit's shell can read. What it does not: the
seat's own key stays with the seat, in the agent box (R50). The three host processes (the face, the
Account, the market) stay the daily run and Docker is not involved there — the host Account keeps
`127.0.0.1:4820` and the market `127.0.0.1:4821` on loopback; the boxes are the isolated run,
`face/README.md` "The three-box drill", `account/README.md` and `market/README.md` "In the box".

**Identity** (plan B1a, 2026-11-04; spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-03-account-split-and-identity-design.md`
Part B, plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-04-identity-plan-b1a-telegram-account-and-face.md`). The account
holds Gravit's networks — Telegram, and Slack since plan B2 (`Network = "slack" | "telegram"`, `NETWORKS` in the tab's order `["telegram", "slack"]`, `kinds.ts`; Slack's half is "Slack" below) — in
`src/portfolio/identity/`: one `Identity` (`identity.ts`) on `PortfolioService.identity`, built only when the
account layer is mounted (without it every identity route is `404` `the account layer is not mounted`);
`server.ts` registers its routes (`routes.ts` `registerIdentityRoutes`) after the brain-key route and awaits its
