`dispose` on close, and `service.ts` hands it every fill (`onFill`, beside both `fill` emits) and every ledger row
(`onLedgerRow`, at `toldRow`), which it phones and never throws on. The face's desk reaches the phone only
through it (§4.2 `phone.ts`, `phone-bridge.ts`). The modules:

- `kinds.ts` — `PhoneKind` (`chat`, `alert`, `urgent`, `brief`, `report`, `card`, `fill`, `watchdog`); the five
  routing rows in their order (`chat` Chat with Gravit, `alerts` Watch alerts, `brief` Pre-close brief, `cards`
  Cards waiting, `fills` Fills and reports; `rowOf`: `urgent` → alerts, `report` → fills, `watchdog` in no row,
  every connected network); the signed routing string (`parseRouting`, `formatRouting`: rows in that order,
  networks sorted, `chat=telegram;alerts=telegram;brief=;cards=telegram;fills=telegram`); `quietHolds`, on the
  America/New_York wall clock (`from > to` crosses midnight, `to` exclusive), never holding `chat`, `urgent` or
  `watchdog`.
- `store.ts` — `identity/state.json` (`loadIdentity`, field by field, a fresh or unreadable file the default;
  `saveIdentity`): the bindings (`network`, `speaksAs`, `botId`, `talksOnlyWith`, `operatorId`, `since`, the
  signed `fingerprint`), the routing, quiet hours and `blocked` (at most 200, `BLOCKED_MAX`); `writeIdentityFile`,
  every file under `identity/` — `0600` in a `0700` folder, temp file, fsync, rename, refused through a link at
  the folder or the file; `Strangers` (`strangers.json`, ruling 9: `{network, sender, masked, count, last}`,
  `sender` the first 12 hex of `sha256("<network>:<id>")`, `masked` `…` and the id's last three digits, at most 50,
  the oldest `last` dropped first — never a name, a handle or a text).
- `secret-file.ts` — `credentials/networks/telegram.json` (`{token, botId, username, operatorId,
  operatorHandle}`), written and removed as `brain-keys.ts` writes a brain key, read only as a plain `0600` file
  with no link on the way.
- `bot-api.ts` — `BotApi` (`getMe`, `getUpdates` with `allowed_updates: ["message"]`, `sendMessage` with
  `reply_parameters` and `allow_sending_without_reply`; 15 s, a poll its timeout plus 15 s), `splitMessage`
  (4,000 UTF-16 units, from the face's retired bridge), `redactorOf` (every spelling of a token, the URL-encoded
  `%3A` and `%3a` among them, longest first) and `telegramApiBase` (ruling 12: `https://api.telegram.org`, or
  `ACCOUNT_TELEGRAM_API` only when it is exactly `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` — any other value ignored with one line
  that does not repeat it; the only file under `account/src` that names `api.telegram.org`).
- `pending.ts` — `PendingConnections`, Connect's sheets 1–3: one pending connection at a time, `PENDING_MS` ten
  minutes (ruling 2, the brain key's ten), the token in memory only; getMe, then a long poll until the first
  private message (`waiting` → `heard`; a 409 `conflict`, retried after 5 s); Not me counts the sender in Not you and
  waits again; drop, expiry and a second Next forget the token and the Bot API client (an expired connection is a
  tombstone whose view says `expired`); a blocked sender is neither heard nor counted.
- `telegram.ts` — `TelegramConnector`, the connected poller (the face's retired bridge's loop): `getUpdates` long
  polls of 50 s; the bound operator's text in their private chat (`from.id` and `chat.id` both theirs) goes to the
  inbox when the Chat with Gravit row ticks Telegram — else it is answered `Chat with Gravit is off on Telegram:
  Account › Identity turns it on.` and kept nowhere (ruling 5), save a text whose first word is one of the phone's
  five commands (`/status`, `/pause`, `/mute`, `/new`, `/stop`, as the bridge parses them, `PHONE_COMMAND`), which goes
  to the inbox whatever the row says, so the phone may always pause or mute (D19); the operator's message that is not text is answered
  `text only, please` and not stored (ruling 4); any other private sender is counted in Not you unless blocked, never
  answered, and everything else is dropped; `identity/telegram.offset` moves past an update only after the inbox
  has it; a 409 waits 30 s, any other failure backs off 5 s doubling to 60 s (`pollFailing`), each said at most once
  a minute and cleared by a poll that answers; an update with no numeric `update_id` is never handled; a 403 on a
  line to the operator marks the network `blocked` until one goes through.
- `inbox.ts` — `InboxRing`, `identity/inbox.json`: the operator's last 500 messages (`INBOX_MAX`, ruling 3), each
  `{id, network, messageId: "telegram:<id>", replyTo?, text, at}`, `id` the account's own number, only growing and
  never reused; a message already kept from the same bot is not appended twice (the bot is kept in the file, not
  on the wire), so an update re-read after a restart is stored once and a reconnected bot's renumbered messages are
  new; a failed write changes nothing and the poll re-reads it; `after`, `last` and `wait` never write.
- `outbox.ts` — `Outbox`, `identity/outbox.json`: what a network could not take yet, at most 100 (`OUTBOX_MAX`),
  each with its kind; flushed in order before each poll and each send, the first part of one written more than
  2 minutes earlier opening with `(written <time> ET, sent late)`; at the flush an entry quiet hours would hold now,
  or one older than 12 hours (`OUTBOX_MAX_AGE_MS`), is dropped with one line, and so is a refused head; a network's
  queued messages are dropped at its disconnect and at its connect (entries carry no chat id).
- `notices.ts` — the account's own notices: `fillNotice` (`Filled · Buy 10 NVDA at 183.00 · Paper · Alpaca`, kind
  `fill`, every venue's fills) and `cardNotice` (a Guard card waiting, `Your call · <reason> — waiting in Gravit`,
  kind `card`), both one line through the link scrub, `scrubLinkText` in a `LINK SCRUB BEGIN … END` block
  byte-identical with the face's `card-notice.ts` (a test compares them, §4.7): NFKC and the look-alike dots
  (U+3002, U+FF0E, U+FF61, U+2024) to `.` first; every scheme link (`[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*://…`) and every `//host`
  becomes `<link>`, then every dotted quad; then every `.` not between two ASCII digits becomes `·` (U+00B7), so no
  client can make a host of what is left (`evil.com` → `evil·com`, `NVDA.US` → `NVDA·US`; `183.00`, `3.5%` and
  `v1.2.3` unchanged). No notice carries a button.
- `identity.ts` — `Identity`: `view()`, `apply()` (the four owner types), `problem()` (the check prepare and the
  door share), `inbox()`, `send()`, `flush()`, `onFill`, `onLedgerRow`, `phoneStatus()`, `dispose()`; at
  construction it resumes the poller of every binding whose token file reads and matches it; a read-only account
  (`--read-only`, `--classic`) polls nothing and may still send.
- `routes.ts` — the seven routes below and `IDENTITY_WORDS`, fixed sentences none of which repeats what was sent.

The four owner types (`account/sign.ts`, in `OWNER_TYPES`, none a money or steer type, none replayed by
`restore.ts`: the state file is the record), each prepare → What you sign → `POST /api/exchange`:

- `connectNetwork` (`AccountIdentity:Connect`: `network`, `pending`, `botId`, `speaksAs`, `operatorId`,
  `talksOnlyWith`, `routing`, `keyHash`, `salt`). The token's one trip is sheet 1's Next (ruling 1); the signature
  names its fingerprint (`keyHash = hex sha256(salt ‖ token)`, the brain key's recipe) under `BRAIN_KEY_TTL_MS`. The
  door peeks the pending connection and checks the fingerprint, the bot, the operator heard and the routing; only
  then does it take it, check the fingerprint again, write the token file and then the state (a failed save
  removes the file) and start the poller; a refused connect leaves the pending connection as it was. The ledger row
  keeps the fingerprint (`keyless`) and no salt; the summary is `Telegram connected: Gravit speaks as @x and talks
  only with @y · token <8 hex>`.
- `disconnectNetwork` (`network`) — the state saved first, then the poller stopped and the token file removed; a
  failed save changes nothing.
- `setRouting` (`routing`, `quietFrom`, `quietTo`) — `HH:MM` in America/New_York, default `23:00`–`07:00`; both
  `""` store quiet hours as `null`, off, and they stay off after a restart; one end empty, a value not `HH:MM` or
  equal ends are refused.
- `blockSender` (`network`, `sender`, `masked`) — the ref into `blocked`, out of Not you.

A bot-token-shaped value in any signed field of the four is refused at prepare and at the door
(`IDENTITY_WORDS.tokenInField`), before the hash-chained ledger could hold it; an agent's key signing any of them is
`E_ACCOUNT_OWNER_ONLY`. The routes are unsigned and behind the account's fence, like its reads (spec §5.5: the
account, not the caller, decides who receives each message):

| Route | Does |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/account/identity/telegram/token` `{token, keyHash, salt}` | sheet 1's Next, on its own reader (the JSON parser skips it in every spelling express routes to it, `isIdentityTokenPath`), at most 1,024 bytes of `application/json`: the shape, the fingerprint, no binding already, then getMe; `{ok: true, pending}`, else a fixed sentence — 400 malformed or not token-shaped, 413, 415, 409 a fingerprint that does not match, Telegram's refusal or a network already connected, 502 Telegram not answering. The token is in no answer, no log line and no ledger row |
| `GET /api/account/identity/pending?id=` | sheets 2 and 3: the pending connection (`bot`, `link` — `https://t.me/<bot>` —, `qr`, `expiresAt`, `state` `waiting` · `heard` · `conflict` · `expired`, and the `sender` once heard — `id`, `name`, `handle`, `masked`, `text`); 404 with none |
| `POST /api/account/identity/pending/not-me`, `POST /api/account/identity/pending/drop` `{id}` | sheet 3's Not me; the sheet closed, the token forgotten at once |
| `GET /api/account/identity` | the Identity tab: each network (`speaksAs`, `talksOnlyWith`, `since`, `fingerprint`, `polling`, `lastPollAt`, `conflictAt`, `blocked`, `pollFailing`), the routing, `quiet` (or `null`) and Not you — never a token, a salt, the full `keyHash`, the bot's or the operator's numeric id |
| `GET /api/account/identity/inbox?after=<n>&wait=<s>` | the face's desk: the messages numbered above `n` (default 0), waiting up to `s` whole seconds (0–25, default 0) only while `n` equals `last`, the wait ending when the request closes; `{ok, messages, last, status}`, `status` the phone's (each network's poll, `queued`, `strangers`); 400 otherwise. Not proxied by the face |
| `POST /api/account/identity/send` `{kind, text, replyTo?, network?}` | the face's desk and watchdog: exactly those keys (nothing can name a chat), a kind in `PHONE_KINDS`, `replyTo` `<network>:<id>`, at most 65,536 bytes (413). The account picks the networks — a `chat` its own network when connected, `watchdog` every connected network, every other kind its routing row among the connected — and holds what it will not send, `{ok: true, held: "nothing connected" \| "not routed" \| "quiet hours"}` (ruling 7); takes its own tokens out (`<token>`) and every loopback link (`<local link>`: the face's URL carries its token); splits it and sends it to the bound operator's chat alone, the first part replying to `replyTo` when it names that network: `{ok: true, sent: ["telegram:<id>", …]}`, `queued: true` beside it when a network failed and its part waits in the outbox, `{ok: true, queued: true}` when nothing went yet, `502 {ok: false, error}` when every network refused it outright (Telegram's 400 or 403). Not proxied by the face |

The files, under the account's home (`~/.buyer-agent-demo`, `BUYER_HOME`): `credentials/networks/telegram.json`
(and Slack's, below); `identity/state.json`, `inbox.json`, `outbox.json`, `strangers.json` and `telegram.offset` — all `0600` in `0700`
folders, written atomically, none read through a link. Tests: `test/unit/identity-store`, `identity-pending`,
`identity-sign`, `identity-inbox` and `identity-send.test.ts`, over `test/identity-fakes.ts`'s `fakeBotApi` on
loopback (token-shaped made-up tokens; no test reaches Telegram): the suite is 146 files, 2,245 tests. The face
signs the four types from Account › Identity and its four Connect sheets since plan B1b
(`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-04-identity-plan-b1b-identity-tab.md`; §5.2–§5.4), and `pending.ts` makes the
connection's QR there (`qrOf`, `qrcode` 1.5.4 pinned: `data:image/svg+xml;base64,…`, made once when the connection
begins, `""` if it throws) and, since that plan, carries the heard sender's numeric `id` in the pending view, for the
owner's page to sign as `operatorId` (drawn there only masked).

**Slack** (plan B2, 2026-11-04; `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-04-identity-plan-b2-slack.md`, the same
spec's Part B as it applies to Slack). Slack is a second network beside Telegram, through the same `Identity`,
the same four owner types, inbox, outbox, routing, quiet hours, notices and Not you; only its listening and its
sending are its own. The seams (`1287e2ce`, Telegram unchanged by them):

- `PendingSource` (`pending.ts`) — one network's side of sheets 1–3: `network`, `secrets` (what every line has
  taken out), `check(signal)` (sheet 1's Next), `listen(ctx)` (sheet 2: `admit`, `stranger`, `heard`, `conflict`,
  `log`) and `resume()` (where the connector starts once taken). `PendingConnections.begin` (Telegram) and
  `beginSlack(appToken, botToken, keyHash, salt)` each make one; one pending connection at a time either way.
- `Transport` (`identity.ts`) — one network's sending: `network`, `secrets`, `partMax`, `send(part, replyTo?)` → a
  wire id, `classify(err)` → `retry` · `refused` · `blocked` · `auth`, `dispose()`. `TelegramTransport`
  (`telegram.ts`) and `SlackTransport` (`slack.ts`).
- `Connector` (`identity.ts`) — one network's listening once connected: `start()`, `status()`,
  `setBlocked(b)`, `dispose()`. `TelegramConnector` and `SlackConnector`.
- `WIRE_ID` (`kinds.ts`) — the one wire id rule, `^(?:telegram:\d{1,16}|slack:\d{9,12}\.\d{6})$` (Slack's
  `slack:<ts>`, no channel in it: Gravit has one DM there), read by the account's `send` and route and redeclared
  byte for byte in the face's `phone.ts` (a test ties them); `SLACK_TOKEN_ANYWHERE`
  (`/\bx(?:ox[abposre]|app)-[A-Za-z0-9-]{10,}/g` → `<token>`), taken out of every text sent and every line logged
  on top of each network's exact-spelling redactor; `chatOffLine(network)`.
- `secret-file.ts` — `SecretOf<N>`: `credentials/networks/slack.json` is `{appToken, botToken, appId, channel,
  botId, username, operatorId, operatorHandle}` (`SlackSecret`), under the same rules as Telegram's file;
  `secretsOf` gives both tokens.

The modules:

- `slack-api.ts` — `SlackApi`, seven Web API methods (`auth.test`, `bots.info`, `users.info`,
  `apps.connections.open`, `conversations.history`, `conversations.replies`, `chat.postMessage`) over `fetch`,
  each a `POST` of `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` to `<apiBase>/<method>` with the token in
  `Authorization: Bearer` (never in a URL), 15 s, cut when the caller's signal aborts; `apps.connections.open`
  with the app-level token, the rest with the bot token. An answer not `ok` is a `SlackApiError` (the HTTP
  status, Slack's `error` code, a 429's Retry-After), its message redacted. `slackApiBase(env, log)`:
  `https://slack.com/api` (`SLACK_API`), or `ACCOUNT_SLACK_API` only when it is exactly
  `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` (or that and `/api`) — any other value ignored with one line that does not repeat
  it. `socketUrlOk(url, apiBase)`: the socket URL `apps.connections.open` answers is taken only as
  `wss://<name>.slack.com/…` (no port, no credentials), or under the override as `ws://127.0.0.1:<that same
  port>/…`, so no answer steers the app token's socket elsewhere. `escapeSlack` (`&`, `<`, `>`),
  `slackAppLink(appId, teamId)` (Slack's `app_redirect`, sheet 2's link) and `SLACK_MANIFEST` (ruling 11: Socket
  Mode, a bot user named Gravit, the Messages tab, the bot scopes `chat:write`, `im:history`, `users:read`, the
  event `message.im`; carried as `slackManifest` in `GET /api/account/identity`, no route of its own). The only
  file under `account/src` that names Slack's host.
- `slack-socket.ts` — `SlackSocket`, one Socket Mode link over Node's own global `WebSocket` (no dependency):
  asks `apps.connections.open`, opens the URL only if `socketUrlOk`, and hands over `hello` first — no envelope
  is handled before its handler finishes (the connector's backfill runs there); a hello handler that throws
  closes the socket and backs off with the cursor unmoved, and a socket with no hello within 30 s
  (`HELLO_DEADLINE_MS`) is closed the same way. Envelopes go one at a time, in order, across sockets; the handler
  answers `ack` (the link sends `{envelope_id}`) or `hold` (nothing sent, so Slack sends it again; a throw
  holds). `disconnect`: `refresh_requested` reopens at once, `warning` does nothing, `link_disabled` stops the
  link with `pollFailing: "Socket Mode is off for this app"` (`LINK_DISABLED`). A close backs off 5 s doubling to
  60 s, reset by a hello; a socket silent 30 minutes is reopened (`SOCKET_REFRESH_MS`); a frame over 64 KiB,
  binary or not JSON is dropped with a line a minute at most. The link always closes its own socket, waiting up
  to 5 s (`CLOSE_WAIT_MS`), before it opens the next, so its own sockets are never two at once.
- `slack.ts` — `SlackPendingSource`, `ConflictWatch`, `SlackConnector`, `SlackTransport`:
  - **sheet 1's check** (ruling 7), in order: `auth.test` (the bot, its team), `bots.info` (the bot's app),
    `apps.connections.open` with the app token, the socket and its hello within 10 s (`HELLO_WAIT_MS`), whose
    `connection_info.app_id` must be the bot's app. Shapes first (`SLACK_APP_TOKEN_SHAPE`
    `^xapp-[0-9]-[A-Z0-9]{8,14}-[0-9]{6,16}-[a-f0-9]{32,80}$`, `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN_SHAPE`
    `^xoxb-[0-9]{6,16}-[0-9]{6,16}-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,40}$`); refusals `refusedBySlack`, `slackNoSocket`,
    `slackPairMismatch`, `slackUnreachable`, each one fixed sentence naming neither token nor URL. Both tokens
    live in the pending connection's memory for its ten minutes and nowhere else.
  - **sheets 2 and 3**: on that same socket, the first `message` event in a DM (`channel_type: "im"`, no
    subtype but `thread_broadcast`, no `bot_id`) of this team and app; everything else is acked and dropped. `memberKind(users.info,
    team)`: a bot is dropped; only a full member of the bot's own team is heard — another team's member, a guest
    (restricted or ultra-restricted) or a deactivated account is a stranger, counted in Not you, and the
    sheet waits on. The sender view carries the display name (else real name, else username), the handle
    `@<user.name>` (the username, which the person cannot change), the full user id (`userId`, `U…`, drawn on
    sheet 3), the `<team>:<user>` id masked to `…` and its last three characters, and the text; the DM's channel
    and the message's ts are kept as `resume`.
  - **the signed ids**: `botId` = `<team id>:<bot user id>`, `operatorId` = `<team id>:<user id>`, `speaksAs` =
    `@<bot user name>`, `talksOnlyWith` = `@<user.name>`; the fingerprint is `keyHash = hex sha256(salt ‖ appToken ‖
    0x00 ‖ botToken)` (`keyMatches(salt, appToken + "\u0000" + botToken, keyHash)`, neither token able to hold a
    NUL); the summary `Slack connected: Gravit speaks as @x and talks only with @y · tokens <8 hex>`.
  - **ConflictWatch** (ruling 8, for the pending source and the connector alike): a hello's
    `num_connections` > 1 is another holder of the app's socket, Slack spreading events across them — the
    pending state `conflict`, the connected status `conflictAt` with a line a minute — except that a reading
    within 30 s (`CONFLICT_RECHECK_MS`) of the owner's own close is taken only when the next hello, or a recheck
    on a fresh socket 30 s later, still reads > 1 (Slack can still count the closed socket).
  - **SlackConnector**, once connected (rulings 1, 2, 5): at every hello, before any live envelope (which waits
    unacked in the link), the backfill — `conversations.history(channel, oldest = cursor, inclusive = false,
    limit = 100)` page by page, and the replies after the cursor of each thread whose `latest_reply` is after it
    (`conversations.replies`; its parent among those rows or in the last 24 h of history, `THREAD_LOOKBACK_MS`, at
    most 5 pages, one line when that bound is hit), at most 500 (`INBOX_MAX`; over 500 waiting, the newest 500
    with one line), oldest first, each read as the event it would have been. A backfill that fails throws, so the
    link backs off and the next hello backfills from the cursor where it stayed. Each message: the bound
    operator's text in the bound DM (this app, this team, the operator's user id, no bot, no subtype — a
    `thread_broadcast`, a thread reply also sent to the DM, is taken as a plain text with its thread's `replyTo`,
    live and backfilled, and stored once though the backfill sees it in the history and the thread alike) has a
    leading `!status`, `!pause`, `!mute`, `!new` or `!stop` rewritten to `/` (`normalizeCommand`), is redacted
    (Slack token shapes and the bound tokens), and — with Chat with Gravit ticking Slack, or a command — is
    appended as `slack:<ts>` (`replyTo: slack:<thread_ts>` in a thread), and only then acked and the cursor
    (`identity/slack.cursor`) moved past it; with the row off and no command it is answered `Chat with Gravit is
    off on Slack: Account › Identity turns it on.` and kept nowhere. A text the inbox cannot store is held (not
    acked) and ends its socket, so the cursor never passes it and the next hello reads it again. A live text is
    skipped (acked) only when the inbox already holds it, or when it is Slack's retry of one at or before the
    cursor. The operator's file (`file_share`) gets `text only, please`; anyone else who DMs the app, by `memberKind`
    (a bot dropped), is a stranger, counted unless blocked, never stored or answered; a channel, group or mpim, a
    bot, an edit or deletion, another team or app, a slash or interactive envelope is dropped. Everything is acked
    at once but a held text and a stranger whose `users.info` did not answer (held too, so Slack sends it again). A read-only account writes no cursor. `invalid_auth`, `token_revoked`,
    `account_inactive` and `not_authed` read as `pollFailing` with that code until a call goes through.
  - **SlackTransport** (rulings 3, 4, 10): `chat.postMessage` to the bound DM alone, `mrkdwn: false`,
    `unfurl_links: false`, `unfurl_media: false`, top level (never `thread_ts`: `replyTo` is taken and not sent),
    each part (`splitMessage` at 4,000 units, `SLACK_PART_MAX`, before escaping) escaped; a part's wire id is
    `slack:<ts>`. A 429, a 5xx, `ratelimited`, `service_unavailable`, `request_timeout`, `fatal_error` or a network
    failure is `retry` (queued in the outbox); the four auth codes `auth` (the status's `pollFailing`, the message
    dropped); every other code `refused` (dropped with one line). Slack has no `blocked`.
- `identity.ts` — a Slack-only outbox flush timer: a queued Slack message is tried again 30 s later
  (`SLACK_FLUSH_MS`), or after Slack's Retry-After when that is longer, since Slack has no poll to flush before;
  Slack rows an earlier run left in the outbox (or queued before a connect) are flushed at once at boot and when
  Slack's transport starts, with no send needed (a read-only account flushes nothing).
  Every log line has every running network's tokens and every Slack token shape taken out.
- `routes.ts` — `POST /api/account/identity/slack/token` `{appToken, botToken, keyHash, salt}` (`SLACK_TOKEN_PATH`,
  `parseSlackTokenBody`), on the same own reader, 1,024-byte limit and fence as Telegram's
  (`isIdentityTokenPath` covers both), answered in Slack's own `IDENTITY_WORDS` (`slackMalformed`,
  `slackTokenShape`, `refusedBySlack`, `slackNoSocket`, `slackPairMismatch`, `slackUnreachable`, `slackMismatch`,
  `slackBotMismatch`, `slackTokenInField` — a Slack token in any signed field of the four types); 400, 409 and
  502 as Telegram's. The pending view gains `workspace` and the sender's `userId`.

Slack's files, under the account's home: `credentials/networks/slack.json` and `identity/slack.cursor` (the last
stored ts, the analogue of `telegram.offset`), under the same rules as the rest. The rulings the plan made (its
"This plan's rulings", not reopened): 1 ack after the inbox append; 2 the backfill at every hello; 3 no threads;
4 plain text; 5 the `!` prefix; 6 the scopes (`chat:write`, `im:history`, `users:read`, the event `message.im`, the
app token's `connections:write`; no `im:write`); 7 the pair check; 8 the conflict; 9 the socket's life; 10 the Web
API's calls and their failures; 11 the manifest from the account; 12 the phone's records keep their name (the desk's
source kind stays `telegram` and gains `network`; §4.2 `phone-bridge.ts`); 13 the watchdog (§4.2
`scripts/watchdog.ts`). Tests: `test/unit/identity-seams`, `identity-slack-api`, `identity-slack-pending`,
`identity-slack-inbox` and `identity-slack-send.test.ts`, with Slack's cases in `identity-sign` and
`identity-send`, over `test/identity-fakes.ts`'s `fakeSlack` (a Web API and Socket Mode server on loopback;
made-up tokens built by concatenation at runtime, and a walk of the tracked files for any literal of a Slack
token's shape); no test reaches Slack.

### 3.10 The market service (`market/`)

`market/` is the Market part's keyless public data as its own service on 127.0.0.1:4821: the
public sources and their stream hub, China (Tencent), the AKShare sidecar, Lunhui's relay and
iFinD, the public reads and stream the face's Markets screens read (`/data/market`, §4.4), and its
own stdio MCP server, `market:mcp`, which the face's `mcp-market` row spawns for Gravit (§3.1). It is its own package (`gravit-market`, `"type": "module"`, Node `^22.19.0 || >=24`, its
own lockfile and `node_modules` by `npm ci` there), moved out of `account/` on 2026-11-03 (plan A1
of spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-03-account-split-and-identity-design.md`). Its code is
still Linqi's buyer-agent-demo @ 133b9a7 by way of this tree's `account/`: `market/NOTICE` names
the origin and lists the files, `market/LICENSE` is a byte copy of the account's Apache-2.0 text.
It holds no wallet, no home and no key file, imports no `viem/accounts`, and writes nothing to
disk; `test/unit/no-wallet.test.ts` pins all of it (no `home.ts`, `credentials.ts`, `keystore.ts`,
`sign.ts`, `paper.ts`, `metamask.ts`, `writes.ts`, `earn.ts`, `polymarket-clob.ts`,
`wallet-bridge.ts` or `ed25519.ts`; no fs write call outside `market-service.ts`, the operator's
installer; no `BUYER_HOME`).

**What came from the account.** *Moved* with `git mv` (history follows) into `src/live/` from
`account/src/portfolio/live/`: `akshare`, `china`, the eight `cn-*` modules, `public-markets`,
`public-rwa`, `public-stocks`, `us-quotes`, `stream-hub`, `prices` and `history-stocks`, with their
eighteen unit tests, `live-public-markets-fixtures.ts` and `test/fixtures/fake-akshare-mcp.mjs`.
*Copied* at `20ead850`, the account keeping its own: `src/core/errors.ts`, `src/refuse.ts`,
`src/calendar.ts`, and into `src/live/` `trade`, `types`, `history`, `history-crypto`,
`categories`, `preipo`, `hl-rules`, `icons`, `compare`, `explore`, `exchange`, `kalshi`,
`polymarket-us`, `robinhood`, `dex` and `chain` — seven of them (`types`, `exchange`, `kalshi`,
`polymarket-us`, `robinhood`, `dex`, `chain`) trimmed to the exports the market uses, each copy
marked under its header ("Copy of …" or "Trimmed copy of … at 20ead850"). `exchange.ts` carries a
local `type KeyFile = Record<string, string>` in place of the account's `credentials.ts` import.
`src/server.ts` mirrors the account server's fence, no-page answer, JSON parser and unread-body
answer. The account's tests still import `market/src` and `market/test`, so its suite needs
`cd market && npm ci`; `account/src` imports nothing of the market's.

**Listening and the fence** (`src/server.ts`, `startMarketServer`). It binds `MARKET_BIND`
(default `127.0.0.1`) on `--port` (default `MARKET_PORT`, 4821), and an address in use is one
sentence and exit 1. It admits the loopback `Host` values plus the exact `host:port` entries of
`MARKET_HOSTS` (`parseHosts`, comma-separated), and refuses a foreign `Origin` and a
`Sec-Fetch-Site` of `cross-site` or `same-site` with `403 {ok: false, error: "this server answers
only programs on this machine"}`. Every path outside `/api/` is `404 {ok: false, error:
MARKET_NO_PAGE}` ("The market serves no page: its screens are Gravit's face (Markets). This address
answers its API under /api/."), and every answer is `cache-control: no-store`.
`account/test/unit/market-fence-parity.test.ts` drives the same cases at both servers so the two
fences cannot drift. `GET /api/health` is `{ok: true, service: "market", sources, china, akshare,
ifind}`, naming no token. The start lines say the address, whether iFinD is configured, and the
AKShare command (started on first use).

**The core** (`src/core.ts`). `realMarketCore()` builds the public sources (`publicSources()`),
one hub (`joinHubs` over a `StreamHub` that answers from REST and the venue feeds), `chinaSource()`,
`publicPrices()`, the Lunhui relay and iFinD, and the AKShare sidecar; nothing opens until asked.
**The read cache** (`src/read-cache.ts`, the account service's `ReadCache` copied) keeps each
source's reads (`keptSource`: listings, stats and events `PUBLIC_KEEP_MS` 20 s, a line
`LINE_KEEP_MS` 3 s, up to `HISTORY_KEPT` 64 histories of `HISTORY_KEPT_BARS` 250,000 bars), holds a
refusing source back under `public:<id>`, and gives every kept source a `reset()`.

**China** (`src/live/china.ts`, `chinaSource({http, clock})`, added to the account on 2026-11-01
and moved here) stands beside the public sources, not among them: the public sources feed paper
pricing, the candles and book routes and the venue checks, none of which may meet a CNY market.
Only `realMarketCore()` builds it, so a core made anywhere else, tests included, never asks
Tencent. Its parsers are the face's old ones, moved with their limits: `cn-session.ts`
(`readCnSession`, the Shanghai-clock phase), `cn-quotes.ts` (`parseTencentQuotes`, `decodeGbk`),
`cn-rank.ts` (`parseTencentRank`, `mergeMovers`), `cn-history.ts` (`gridIndex`, `parseDayQuery`,
`parseKline`, `CN_BARS`) and `cn-search.ts` (`parseTencentSearch`, Tencent's smartbox).
**`CnHttp`** (`cn-http.ts`) is its network, a GET that returns the body's raw bytes (the shared
`Http` decodes every body as UTF-8 and keeps 2,000 characters, which would mangle Tencent's GBK
names and cut a ranking short); `cnHosts` guards it, after `fixedHosts` in `public-markets.ts`:
https, the default port, no user, GET, and one of four hosts (`CN_HOSTS`: `qt.gtimg.cn`,
`smartbox.gtimg.cn`, `proxy.finance.qq.com`, `web.ifzq.gtimg.cn`); no key is held. It answers the
day's top 20 by volume or movers (`ExploreItem`s of kind `ashare`, key `cn:<6 digits>`, `currency:
"CNY"`, `turnoverCny`, `canTrade: false`), search hits, a `ChinaMarket` per code carrying `cn`
(`ChinaFacts`: market cap, P/E TTM, turnover rate, limit up and down, amplitude, `phase`,
`quoteStatus`) and a `ChinaHistory` — 1D and 5D as Shanghai sessions of minutes, the longer ranges
as forward-adjusted day, week and month bars. Reads are kept a short while (`RANK_TTL_MS` 10 s,
`QUOTES_TTL_MS` 5 s, `MINUTES_TTL_MS` 30 s, `BARS_TTL_MS` 600 s, `SEARCH_TTL_MS` 60 s) and shared per
key; a failure is never kept, and a ranking that fails is answered from the last good one for up to
`STALE_KEEP_MS` (10 min), flagged stale; a refusal carries its own words, never Tencent's text or a
URL. Traps carried with the code: STAR shares (688…) report volume in shares, the others in lots;
Tencent answers GBK with a trailing `~`. There is no lookahead guard and no fallback source: when
Tencent does not answer, China says so (`ChinaStatus`). The market's own reads answer it (below);
the protocol's `/api/china/*` routes still serve it, though no account reads them since plan A2.

**The source protocol** (`src/protocol.ts`, `mountProtocol`) is how the account reads the market.
Every answer is 200 `{ok: true, value, readAt?}` or `{ok: false, refusal}` (a top-level Map goes
out as `[key, value][]`, `readAt` is the value's read stamp or a parallel list of them); a bad or
doubled parameter is 400, an unknown source or a read it has no method for 404.

| Route | What it answers |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/sources` | each source's `id`, `name`, `kind`, `connectTo`, `connector`, `readOnly?`, `historyApart?`, `sessions?` (its clock's zone) and `has` (which reads it serves) |
| `GET /api/source/:id/listings` · `line` · `stats` · `events` · `candles` · `book` · `trades` · `settlement` · `funding` | that source's read, through the read cache; `candles` also takes `range` and `own`; book depth 1–50 (default 20), trades 1–100 (default 30) |
| `POST /api/source/:id/reset` | the forced re-check: lets the source's hold go |
| `GET /api/china/rank` · `search` · `quotes` · `history` · `status` | China's reads, each answer carrying China's `status` |
| `GET /api/price?asset=` | a coin's price or `null` |
| `GET /api/hub/covers` · `GET /api/hub/confirmed` | whether the hub streams a market (and prices only), and a quote confirmed within `maxAgeMs`, waiting at most `HUB_WAIT_MAX_MS` (5 s) |
| `GET /api/hub?client=` | the hub's events as SSE: `quote`, `book` (to a book hold only), `trades` (the ring after the last seq sent, `evictedSeq`, the recent trades) and `live`, coalesced 100/100/250 ms per market, a heartbeat every 15 s; a hold taken, or a stream opened by a client that holds, gets the current state at once |
| `POST /api/hub/hold` · `POST /api/hub/want` | `{client, source, symbol, book?, held}` holds or lets go (the same hold twice is one); a want pushes that market to the client for `IDLE_MS` (60 s) |

A client's last stream closing lets every hold go; a client that holds with no stream open is let
go after `IDLE_MS`, and a market with no hub keeps no client.

**Lunhui's reach and AKShare** (`src/routes-cn.ts`, `mountCn`, the account's four route bodies
moved; the account relays none of them since plan A2: the Lunhui freezes and the `mcp-market` row
ask the market directly). `GET /api/cn/relay?url=` (`live/cn-relay.ts` over `CnHttp`) forwards one GET to an
allow-list (`RELAY_HOSTS`: `qt.gtimg.cn`, `web.ifzq.gtimg.cn`'s `fqkline/get` and `day/query`,
`push2ex.eastmoney.com`'s four `getTopic…`/`getYesterdayZTPool` pools, `push2`/`push2delay`
`clist/get`; https, the default port, no user, no fragment) and answers the upstream's status,
content type and bytes unchanged, plus `location` on a 3xx, with `x-content-type-options: nosniff`;
no decoding, no caching, no redirect followed; three request headers pass (`accept`, `referer`,
`user-agent`); 7 s and 512 KiB per read, 4 s for `day/query`, a 16-slot queue (`RELAY_IN_FLIGHT`)
with a 64-waiter cap (`RELAY_WAITING`), an abandoned ask leaving it. `POST /api/cn/ifind` (`live/cn-ifind.ts`) runs the boards
stand-in's one query (`IFIND_QUERY`) with `IFIND_REFRESH_TOKEN` or `IFIND_ACCESS_TOKEN` from this
process's environment, held in memory and never in a reply, log line or refusal, re-exchanged
once on a rejected token, under one 15 s deadline and a 4 MiB cap.
Refusals are `{ok: false, relay|ifind: <word>}` with `x-cn-relay`/`x-cn-ifind`. The AKShare
sidecar (`live/akshare.ts`, `createAkshare`) runs `akshare-mcp` (`akshareCommand()`:
`MARKET_AKSHARE_BIN`, else `~/.local/bin/akshare-mcp`; argv only) as an MCP child over stdio,
started on the first ask and again after it exits, one 120 s deadline (`AKSHARE_CALL_MS`) per ask,
recycled on a timeout, an allowlisted environment (no iFinD secret reaches Python), 4 MiB replies
and 16 KiB arguments; `GET /api/akshare/tools` and `POST /api/akshare/call` answer `{ok: false,
akshare: <word>, message}` refusals (`off`, `unknown-tool`, `bad-arguments`, `unavailable`,
`timeout`, `too-large`). Install and limits: `market/README.md`.

**The public reads and the stream** (`src/reads.ts`, `src/stream.ts`, `src/follows.ts`), the face's
Markets reads since plan A2 (proxied under `/data/market`, §4.4) and `market:mcp`'s. `GET
/api/explore`, `/api/quotes`, `/api/candles`, `/api/book` and `/api/trades` are the account
service's old public reads with the connected-venue branches deleted — the same query limits and
body shapes; the account's copies are gone (§3.9), so nothing pins the two alike any more. The
refusals are the market's own words: a question the market's checks refuse is `409
E_MARKET_BAD_REQUEST` ("the market does not take this request as written"), an unknown source
`E_MARKET_UNKNOWN_SOURCE` (`"<id>" is not a public market source: Markets names each source by its
id`), a non-China pair in `quotes` `E_VENUE_RAIL_CLOSED` (`"<venue>" is priced in explore: the
market quotes A shares only (venue "china")`), China absent `China is not read by this market`, a
venue that publishes no trades `<name> publishes no trades the market can read`;
`market/test/unit/reads.test.ts` pins each, and `no-wallet.test.ts` that the reads say nothing of
an account. `GET /api/stream` and `POST /api/stream/markets` are the account's bus without account
events (`MarketStream`: `quote`, `trades` and `book` for the markets a page follows, `MAX_FOLLOWS`
16, coalesced, a `snapshot` frame on every new stream), the face's `/data/market/stream`.

**`market:mcp`** (`src/mcp.ts`, `npm run market:mcp`, stdio, server name `market`). Five tools,
each `readOnlyHint`, each one or two loopback fetches at `MARKET_URL` (default
`http://127.0.0.1:4821`) with no key, no signing and no state: `market_explore` (`GET /api/explore`,
`tab`, `q`, `sort`, `limit` 30 by default), `market_quotes` (1–12 `venue|symbol` pairs, `GET
/api/quotes`), `market_candles` (`GET /api/candles`, interval 1h when nothing else is given),
`market_book` (`GET /api/book` and `GET /api/trades` together, the seat's old answer shape) and
`market_akshare` (`POST /api/akshare/call`, a tool's own error passed on as an answer). A failed
fetch is `isError` with `{ok: false, error: MARKET_DOWN}`. `market/test/unit/mcp.test.ts` spawns it
over an in-process market.

**The account's one link** (`account/src/portfolio/market/`). The account reads the market through
`connectMarket` (`link.ts`), built only by `server.ts`'s main and `account-check.ts` from
`PORTFOLIO_MARKET_URL` (default `MARKET_URL_DEFAULT`, `http://127.0.0.1:4821`); a service made
anywhere else reaches no market unless one is handed in. The link is the transport (`client.ts`:
answers kept per route, shared in flight, a refusal kept at most 2 s, no Origin sent, redirects
manual; two ways to ask, no raw pass-through) and three adapters, the three things `service.ts`
takes as options: `remoteSource` (`sources.ts`, one per `/api/sources` row, defining exactly the
reads it `has`, plus `reset`), `RemoteHub` (`hub.ts`) and `remotePrice` (`price.ts`, the last price
of up to 2,000 assets remembered); the public sources price the paper venues, the twins and the
desk, never a public read of the account's own. `shapes.ts` holds the types and pure functions copied from the
market. The source list is asked every 5 s until the market answers, then every 60 s, so an
account started first fills in with no restart; the main's start line says `market: <url> ·
answering` or `not answering yet`. The account relays none of the market's routes (§3.9).

**The hub mirror and its reconnect** (`hub.ts`). `RemoteHub` counts local holds per key and POSTs
the first and the last, sends wants at most every `WANT_EVERY_MS` (10 s), and mirrors the stream's
last quote, book and a trades ring (`RING_SIZE` 200) per market. When the stream drops every quote
and book goes `live: false`, `confirmed` answers nothing, and it reopens after a wait doubling from
`BACKOFF_MIN_MS` (500 ms) to `BACKOFF_MAX_MS` (30 s); a stream silent for `SILENT_MS` (45 s) is taken
for dropped. Each stream is an epoch: on every open the seqs it says are rebased above every seq
given out before, every ring, recent list and `evictedSeq` is cleared, trades stamped before the
stream opened are marked `snap` (paper counts them only if stamped after it last judged), and every
hold and want is sent again — so a restarted market's trades can never fill a resting paper order
on an older price.

**The market is down** (`MARKET_DOWN`, "The market service is not answering, so prices here are
not current."). `MarketLink.marketOld()` is defined while the client is stale or the hub stream is
down with nothing answered since. Then holdings keep their last price and carry `marketOld`
(`{since, message}`), a prepare refuses with the sentence ("Paper account: The market service is
not answering, …", `E_VENUE_REJECTED`), paper waits — it never fills on a price older than the
market's last answer — and `snapshot()` takes no net-worth or paper point. A market-down refusal
carries `native: {market: "down"}` and is held only `MARKET_DOWN_HOLD_MS` (2 s), in the source's
hold and the read cache alike, and while the market is old the link asks the
source list every 5 s and pokes the hub, so recovery takes about 2 s.

**`market:service` and the box.** `npm run market:service -- install|status|restart|logs|uninstall`
(`src/market-service.ts`) is the LaunchAgent `com.gravit.market`, the operator's to install, never
an agent's: the plist runs `node --env-file-if-exists=<repo>/.env.ifind …/tsx/dist/cli.mjs
src/server.ts`, so the token is read from the file at each start and the plist carries only its
path; it keeps `PATH`, `HOME` and `MARKET_AKSHARE_BIN`, logs to `~/Library/Logs/gravit-market/`, and
`status` asks `/api/health`. The `npm run market` script is `tsx --env-file-if-exists=../.env.ifind
src/server.ts` (`test/unit/market-script.test.ts` pins that tsx hands the flag to node). The account's
`account:service` keeps `PORTFOLIO_MARKET_URL` when it is set. Under compose the `market` box
(`market/Dockerfile`: AKShare's pinned install layer, `MARKET_AKSHARE_BIN=/usr/local/bin/akshare-mcp`,
then `npm ci`; `market/.dockerignore`) runs `npm run market` with `MARKET_BIND=0.0.0.0` and
`MARKET_HOSTS=market:4821`, `expose: ["4821"]` and no port published, no volume, the optional
`env_file` `.env.ifind`, and a health check on `/api/health` that the account and agent boxes wait on;
`face/tests/compose.test.ts` pins it. `MARKET_BIND` and `MARKET_HOSTS` are for the box only.

**Suites** (2026-11-03, `feat/account-split-a2`, plan A2's docs commit): `market/` 30 files, 325
tests, all pass; `account/` 141 files, 2,163 tests, all pass; the face 3,031 tests, 2,998 pass +
33 skipped, 3,032/3,032 with `FACE_SMOKE=1` (§7.4). Before them (2026-11-03, `feat/account-split-a1`): `market/` 29 files, 284 tests, all pass;
`account/` 143 files, 2,188 tests, all pass (its one clock-dependent case, `ui-standin.test.ts`
"prices move every few seconds…", can fail on the real clock); the face 2,993 tests, 2,960 pass +
33 skipped, and with `FACE_SMOKE=1` 2,994, all pass; each package's typecheck clean.

---

## 4. Frontend: the face server (`face/src`)

Some 26,800 lines of TypeScript across 58 files (26,795 measured on 2026-11-02), run directly by
`tsx` — no build step, plus two plain `.js` files outside `src/` (`face/plugins/bot.js` and
`face/plugins/gravit.js`, §3.7–§3.8 — a composition names each by a path the loader reaches as an
absolute `file:` URL, which the face rebases from a relative one for a bot, and each must import
nothing), the role tool `face/plugins/role.mjs` (§3.8, PLAN D20; it imports `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`
only) and the Lunhui rows' plain `.mjs` files under `face/plugins/lunhui/` (§4.3: twelve row files
and their `lib/`, which import `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`, pinned exactly in `face/package.json`,
and each other, never `src/`). Pins: `DSH_PIN = 0.2.1-rc.5` (every `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*`
dependency — 38 since the dsh UI port declared its four host rows' packages (34 after the 2026-11-02
upgrade declared `dsh-tool-ralph`), 40 `@deepseek-ai/*` packages with the two cordis ones — declared exactly and installed), `CORDIS_PIN = 4.0.5` (`@deepseek-ai/cordis` rides its own 4.x track; the dsh packages
peer it with a tilde range) and `CORDIS_INCLUDE_PIN = 1.0.10` (the one cordis plugin the face
imports itself); all three are asserted by `tests/version.test.ts`, which also refuses the three
package names 0.2.0 retired. Until 2026-11-02 the pins were 0.2.0-rc.2, 4.0.4 and 1.0.9. `face/README.md` carries the run table, the profile rules, the instruments,
channels, Discover, bots, roles, the upgrade order, and the drills. Beside the server,
`face/scripts/` holds four operator tools — `check-home.ts`, the go-live dry run that boots the
face on a COPY of a harness home and read-opens every session (it refuses the live home by
device and inode, and a copy without its `DRY-RUN-COPY` marker), `validate-fixture.mjs`
(`npm run check:fixture`, §6.7), `render-roles.ts` (`npm run render:roles`, §3.8), which
regenerates the mirror `bots/gravit/agent.cordis.yml` from `roles/`, and `schema-sizes.ts`
(§4.3), which boots a COPY with its MCP rows as the copy mounts them and prices a Gravit
request's tools one by one (it refuses the default live home, `~/.dsh`, by device and inode; a
live home set elsewhere is not detected) — and, with `face/landing/`, the static
product landing page (`npm run build` → `face/dist/`) and its demo-asset tooling; nothing there
runs in the face process.

### 4.1 Boot sequence (`main.ts` → `boot.ts`)

`boot.ts` mirrors the dsh 0.2.1-rc.5 CLI's `runProfile` (the `@deepseek-ai/dsh` chunk
`lib/profile-boot-C14i-8IN.js`, also published as `@deepseek-ai/dsh/profile-boot` — a reading
aid, not a dependency; at 0.2.0-rc.2 the chunk was `lib/profile-boot-BZ2ZjNWi.js`, and the
2026-11-02 re-diff found `runProfile`, `composeProfile` and `createAppReady` unchanged up to line
shifts, no new `provide`, required service or readiness rule) with ten divergences, each stated in the file's header: no `--patch`
files; no `profileContext` (PLAN D1 — with it dsh-base's `settings` row would import and rename
the operator's shared `settings.yaml`, and `config-editor`, `plugin-manager` and `dsh-hmr` would
recompose the live tree from files that do not carry the face's layers); no proxy policy (PLAN
D10 — `installProxyFromEnvironment` would reroute the face's own Account fetches too);
no signal handlers, shutdown controller or fail-loud inside `bootFace`; `appReady` committed
last; the face's own `package.json` as the install anchor; a skipped bundle refused; a strict
row audit; and the policy layer.

1. Read `FACE_PORT` (default 3090) and `FACE_PROFILE` (default `face`) with `||`, so an empty
   export means the default rather than a moving port or the profiles root itself. Resolve the
   client directory module-relative.
2. **`process.chdir(<repo root>)`** before boot: `SessionController`, which replaced 0.1.1's
   `ApiProxyService`, takes every session's default project directory from `process.cwd()` and
   offers no config key, and dsh-base's `sandbox-policy.workspaceRoot` is `!!js process.cwd()`.
   The client directory and boot's `INSTALL_ANCHOR` are module-relative; the channel root, the session-delete fence root and the panels' cwd are read
   from `process.cwd()` after this chdir, so they are the repo root only because of it.

   `process.cwd()` is only the *fallback* boundary. `dsh-sandbox-policy` resolves the writable
   root per call from the calling session's `cwd`: a channel session is fenced to
   `strategies/<name>/` (plus platform temp areas), and a write outside it — `face/`,
   another strategy, `docs/` — is denied and escalates to a card; a root session (`+ new` with
   no folder chosen) is fenced to the whole repo, where `face/`, `dsh/skills/` and `roles/` are
   all writable with no card (§9, R9).
3. Install SIGINT (exit 130) / SIGTERM (exit 0) handlers and app-boot's own `installFailLoud`,
   before the boot it guards. It covers `unhandledRejection` and `uncaughtException`, skips the
   rejections boot's startup audit already reported, prints one labelled diagnostic, releases
   the room engine, the quote and search routes, the tree and then the Account proxy under a 2 s bound, and
   exits 1; a signal's shutdown releases the same four in the same order.
4. `bootFace({profileName, port, deferReady: true})`: dsh's layered env load
   (`$DSH_HOME/.env`, `<cwd>/.env`) → `composeFace`: resolve `$DSH_HOME`, load the profile
   anchored on the face's own `package.json` (a bundle `loadProfile` could not load is now
   skipped, not thrown — the face refuses the compose), **rewrite `<profile>/cordis.yml` to
   `[]`** (the loader's write-back would otherwise bake composed rows in and double every
   bundle insert next boot), stack the patches — bundle layers (`dsh-base`) → the face policy
   layer (§4.3) → the Account seat → the Lunhui rows (§4.3) → the profile's
   `cordis.patch.yml` → the home's
   `cordis.patch.yml` → a caller's in-memory `extraPatches` (`main.ts` passes none;
   `scripts/check-home.ts` disables a home copy's MCP rows with it) — apply the guarded
   switches (`session-telemetry-otel` disabled when `DSH_TELEMETRY_DISABLED` is non-empty and
   the row is composed; `hmr` disabled whenever composed), patch Gravit's persona into
   `system-prompt` (`personaPrefix` only, §4.3), set the `agent-instructions` row's two
   candidate lists after it (`instructionsPatch`, §4.3), then push **the face overlay last** — its
   default preset rendered here, in memory, from `roles/`, `dsh/profile/cycle.md`,
   `dsh/profile/lunhui-run.md` and `lunhui-module.md` (`readRoles`, `readCycle` and then `readProtocols` run as the very
   last steps before the push; a missing roles directory, a role the reader refuses, a cycle file
   that is missing, unreadable, empty or over 3,300 bytes, or a protocol file that is missing,
   unreadable, empty, over 3,000 bytes or carries `{{` ends the compose with that path, and a face
   that ships `bots/` ships `roles/` beside it, §3.8). This
   inverts the CLI's layering deliberately: loopback-only binding must survive an operator
   patch, so face rows win silently; the policy layer is the other way round and yields to an
   operator row with the same id.
5. Compute the runtime module resolution (`createRuntimeResolution`, anchored on
   `face/package.json`, pure) and boot. `prepare` provides the launch environment, installs
   `PluginPackages` with that resolution before any row imports — without it a fresh home
   resolves no dsh-base row, and it needs the native `node-addon-require-builtin` — and provides
   the command line (`args: []`) with the face's own `appReady`. Nothing writes
   `$DSH_HOME/profiles/node_modules` any more. A required dsh entry that does not activate
   throws dsh's `StartupError`, whose grouped diagnostic `main.ts` prints before exiting 1.
6. Audit the settled tree, disposing it and throwing on the first failure: **every enabled
   Loader entry ACTIVE** (dsh 0.2's own boot fails only on its required ids and merely warns on
   the rest; the face refuses a partial tree, naming each `id (package): state`); the services
   `approval`, `userQuestions`, `typertGateway` and `permissionPresets` present, each refusal
   naming its consequence; an ACTIVE `@deepseek-ai/dsh-api-remotes` entry — the answerer: a
   tree without it boots clean and passes every other check while every order is denied "no
   approval channel is available" and every question rejects `NO_PROVIDER`; and
   `ask_user_question` in the **live** tool registry (service and tool fail independently — that
   was the 2026-08-31 → 09-02 silent outage).
7. Audit Gate 2 (§4.7) — it was ARMED inside `prepare`, before any row mounted, by
   `armOrderGate`: two `hostCtx.inject` fibers, the guard waiting on `tools` and the prepended
   `tools/pre-execute` listener on `approval`, so both exist the moment their service does and
   re-arm exactly once if that service restarts. That is the tenth divergence, added 2026-09-30
   after a review proved the window it closes: dsh-base's `typert-gateway` activates DURING
   `boot()` and its unary `/api` is not readiness-gated (only the mux upgrade waits on
   `appReady`), so a slow row let `session/create` + `session/prompt` run, and an order tool
   dispatch, seconds before a post-boot registration existed (`order-gate-midboot-smoke` pins
   the closed window). The audit refuses the boot if either fiber is not ACTIVE, then runs
   `auditOrderTools` and logs `order gate armed for …` or refuses — when a server carries the
   seat's tools and the gate covers none of its writes (`uncovered`), or when any server
   registers a retired order tool, `place_order` or `cancel_order` (`retired`; the refusal names
   the tool and says to remove its MCP row). A third outcome is silence: `dsh-mcp-client`
   defaults `failOnStartupError: false`, so a seat child that cannot start (no `npm ci` in
   `account/`, or a `FACE_ACCOUNT_SEAT_DIR` naming nothing) leaves the row ACTIVE and the tree healthy with no
   `mcp__account__*` tools, no `order gate armed` line and no error from the face — only
   `mcp-client(account): connection failed … no tools were registered` on stdout; reconnect
   exhaustion unregisters the tools for the life of the process. Check the server's page on
   Discover (Data → the server: its tools), the seat box, or that stdout line; the fix is the
   install and a restart.
8. The preset roster: the registry present and its default `gravit`; every other bot declared
   (`declareBots`, §3.7) — a bot that cannot be declared does not fail the boot, its reason is
   kept for `/data/bots.json`; then the desk's `gravit-desk` and one `role-<id>` preset per role
   (§3.8), each declared from memory through `declarePreset`, a refused declaration refusing the
   boot; the default listed and not broken, and so the `kairos` alias, `gravit-desk`
   (`deskRosterProblem`) and every role preset (`roleRosterProblem`); every declared bot listed. Log `agent presets: …` (with `N bot(s) not
   declared, see above` when a declaration failed). Then the global-instructions audit (PLAN D25): one
   stderr line for each user-global `AGENTS.md` that exists — `$DSH_HOME/AGENTS.md` and
   `<DSH_AGENTS_HOME or ~/.agents>/AGENTS.md` (`globalInstructionFiles`), the two files dsh
   0.2.1's `agent-instructions` reads with no row switch — saying it would enter every agent's
   instruction chain; a warning, not a refusal, and the face never moves `DSH_AGENTS_HOME`,
   because `skill-filesystem` resolves its default roots from it.
9. `main.ts` mounts the routes (§4.4): `/` behind `ctx.connection.authorizeIndex` and
   `/client/*`; the quote routes (`registerQuoteRoutes`) and the search route
   (`registerSymbolSearchRoute`), both behind the `/data` fence from `http.ts`; the Account proxy and the seat
   route, both on the `mcp-account` row as composed and the second reading through the first's
   `account` reader; channel routes; session
   routes; bot routes (every save re-declares); the bot runtime; the room engine; and panel
   routes (awaited, because their registration runs `syncAgentTools`, so every connected agent
   that has an exec recipe — `claude`, `codex` — becomes an `agent_<bin>` tool before the face
   reports up; a connected bin without a recipe stays a roster row and gets no tool).
10. `booted.commitReady()`: only now does the gateway register `/api/remote.mux`. A tab still
    holding its 30-day cookie reconnects the moment the upgrade is admitted and must find every
    route mounted. It re-checks that the root is still active and throws otherwise — into
    `installFailLoud`, never a face that would not stream.
11. Print `gravit-face: http://<host>:<port>/?token=… (profile: …)` from the bound service —
    the per-process launch token that mints the browser cookie (§4.4) — then one line
    explaining it, and the room caps.

One `bootFace` per process: given a `dshHome` (as the tests do; `main.ts` passes none) it sets
`process.env.DSH_HOME` permanently, which is why the real-boot tests (32, §7.3) live in files of their own
(`roles-smoke.test.ts`'s five boot one after the other, each into a fresh home). Without `deferReady` it commits `appReady` itself as its last step, which is what every
smoke that boots without `main.ts` relies on.

**The desk at boot.** desk (`installDesk`): `/data/desk/status`, `POST /data/desk/pause`, the two desk tools over
the desk's quote source - `marketQuotes({ explore: marketProxy.explore, quotes: marketProxy.quotes })` (`src/market-quotes.ts`, §4.2): the market's reads through the market proxy's caches (`registerMarketProxy` returns both), a US share by its `explore` read and an A share by its `quotes` read, at most six in flight - and the desk
guard, always; and, unless `FACE_DESK=0`, the ledger's `boot`, the sleep watch, the desk
conversation — its route resolved first from `FACE_DESK_MODEL` (`resolveDeskRoute`), started
without being awaited, so the desk session is ensured and supervised from boot — and, with a
phone client (`createPhoneClient`, `phone.ts`, at the `mcp-account` row's URL as composed — the
proxy's — or `seatUrl()` with no row; none when the row is disabled), the phone bridge
(`phone-bridge.ts`) over the account's inbox and send (§3.9 "Identity"; the face reads no
`TELEGRAM_*` name since plan B1a); and, with the conversation, the standing
orders' clock (`schedule.ts`), loaded on first use once the bridge has set the conversation's
outlet; its calendar is the builtin XNYS rules, and a `.py` script producer runs under
`FACE_PYTHON` (read by `desk.ts`), else `python3`; and, in the same chain once the clock row is
made, the watch (`watch.ts`, P3), given `watchRow` (`main.ts` passes `{}`) and a quote source
that is not `unavailable`, on the desk's two calendars (`deskCalendars`: XNYS by New York date,
the XSHG table by Beijing date), with SEC's filings only once `ALPHA_EDGAR_USER_AGENT` is set. The desk comes after `bootFace` has bound the
port, so a face that could not bind writes no `boot`; its `ready` is not awaited, so the
ledger never delays readiness. `main.ts` prints `desk: ledger at <dir>` or `desk: rows
disabled (FACE_DESK=0)`.

### 4.2 Module table

| File | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `main.ts` | entry: chdir, signal handlers and `installFailLoud`, boot with `deferReady`, the sign-in route and every route family (the room engine, the bot runtime and the Account proxy included — the proxy's `dispose` runs after the tree's at shutdown, once the web server has stopped), `commitReady`, the tokenized URL; the market proxy (`registerMarketProxy`, on `composedMarketRow(seatLoader.entries())`: the `mcp-market` row's URL as composed, or 503 `disabled` with the row disabled; its `dispose` beside the account proxy's on both exits); the desk's `installDesk`, with `quotes: marketQuotes({ explore: marketProxy.explore, quotes: marketProxy.quotes })` — the one source for both markets — and `watchRow: {}`, the watch on its production defaults (the wall clock, the face's two calendars, SEC's fetch only once `ALPHA_EDGAR_USER_AGENT` names a contact) and, since plan B1a, `phone` (`createPhoneClient` at the `mcp-account` row's URL as composed, or `seatUrl()` with no row; none with the row disabled), the same client the Gate 2 notice uses (`onCardAsked: announceCard(cardPhone, …)`, passed to `bootFace` only when `FACE_DESK` is not `0`, ruling 10; `deskEnabled` is read before the boot for it) |
| `boot.ts` | the mirror of the dsh CLI's `runProfile` (§4.1): `composeFace` (its last step renders the default preset from `roles/`, `dsh/profile/cycle.md` and the run protocols; `FaceBootOptions.protocolsDir` points a test at a fixture), the runtime resolution, the strict row audit, the required-service and answerer checks, `ask_user_question` in the live registry, Gate 2 registration, `declareBots`, the desk's and the role presets' declarations, the preset-roster checks, the global `AGENTS.md` audit (`globalInstructionFiles`, PLAN D25), `commitReady`; since plan B1a `FaceBootOptions.onCardAsked(name, args)`, which `armOrderGate` calls, unawaited, when Gate 2's decision is `ask` — never for a deny, a read or a retired tool; a throw is one `console.error` line and the card is asked either way (§4.7) |
| `overlay.ts` | the seventeen host rows `dsh-base` does not mount (§4.3), `satisfies`-checked against each plugin's own config type; `BOTS_ROOT`, `DEFAULT_PRESET`, `GRAVIT_PLUGIN_RELATIVE`, `presetRowId` |
| `policy.ts` | the policy layer (§4.3): `POLICY_ID_PATCHES`, `POLICY_INSERTS`, `facePolicyPatches` — each row a PLAN decision; a missing target is reported on stderr, never skipped silently |
| `account-seat.ts` | the Account seat row (§3.1): `ACCOUNT_SEAT_ROW_ID`, `ACCOUNT_SEAT_SERVER`, `SEAT_TOOL_PREFIX`, `ACCOUNT_SEAT_NAME`, `DEFAULT_SEAT_DIR` (the repo's `account/`, resolved from this file's location, never `homedir()`), `seatDir`/`seatUrl` (the env or the defaults), `accountSeatPatches` — this process's node, `account/`'s `tsx`, the seat's env, 130 s, failing soft — and `composedSeatRow` (the row AS COMPOSED, read off the Loader's entries: disabled by a patch, or its service URL and seat name), which `main.ts` hands the seat route so the box follows an operator's patch, never the environment alone |
