| `POST /data/rooms/say` `{sessionId, text}` | `room.ts` | the operator's `@`: mentions resolved against the roster (by id, by one-token display name); nobody named → `addressed: []` and the client sends an ordinary prompt; else the message is appended to the room as the operator's own (never a prompt), a cold room is resumed through `sessionController.resolveAgent` — the host's own composition, model selection and preset join — and each named member turns. 400 a bad id or empty text, 404 not in a channel or `session/not-found`, 409 a corrupt roster or any other resolve failure, with dsh's code and message and, when the log predates dsh 0.2, the legacy-format note |
| `POST /data/rooms/state` `{sessionId}` | `room.ts` | the roster, the members the engine drove this boot, the caps left; never resumes |
| `GET /data/desk/status` | `desk.ts` | fence first (403, the fixed `FORBIDDEN`), then `deskStatus` through http.ts's `fencedGet`, read from the ledger afresh on every request: `{ok, pid, version, bootedAt, uptimeMs, desk: {enabled, dir}, asleep, runs}` — `pid`, `version` (`DSH_PIN`), `bootedAt` (ISO-8601) and `uptimeMs` are this process's; `desk.enabled` says whether this face mounted the desk's rows (`FACE_DESK`) and `desk.dir` is the ledger's directory; `asleep` is the ledger's gaps since this face booted, `{from, to, gapMs}`; `runs` is every run in the current ledger file, `{bootedAt, pid, endedAt?, code?, lost}` — the home's ledger whichever face answers, so a `FACE_DESK=0` face reports its home's runs and gaps, never a run of its own (a second face beside the service runs on a scratch home, §4.6). Since the desk's P1: `off`, the pause in force, `{setAt, by, until?}`, present only while one is (a pause past its `until` is left out, though its file waits for the next post to lift it); `deskSession`, the desk conversation the ledger names last; `turnsToday`, the `desk-turn` events since 00:00 New York time, `{count, usage: {uncachedInputTokens, outputTokens, cacheReadTokens, cacheWriteTokens}}`; and `phone` (since plan B1a; `telegram` before it), the phone bridge's state (`PhoneStatus`), `{configured, polling, lastPollAt?, accountFailing?: {since, reason}, networks: [{network, polling, lastPollAt?, conflictAt?, blocked?, pollFailing?}], queued, strangers}` — `configured` whether the face has the account's half to reach (the `mcp-account` row not disabled), `lastPollAt` the last inbox read that answered, and `networks`, `queued` (the account's outbox) and `strangers` (Not you's rows) as the account's last inbox answer gave them; a face that runs no bridge reports nothing polling and nothing connected. Since the desk's P2: `budget`, always, the day's tokens against `standing.yml`'s cap — `{dailyTokens?, used: {uncachedInputTokens, outputTokens, cacheReadTokens, cacheWriteTokens, total}, spent, error?}`, `dailyTokens` present only when a cap is set and `error` only when the ledger could not be read; and `standing`, present while the standing orders' clock runs, what it knows from memory (`StandingStatus`) — `{file: {path, state: missing\|loaded\|refused, loadedAt?, errors?}, ledger?: {error}, calendar: {clock, state: unknown\|ok\|stale\|failed, source?, today?, error?}, orders: [{id, dir, file, at, producer?, wake, enabled, expires, expired, hash, producerHash?, nextAnchor?, last?}], running?, queued, recent}`, each `hash` `ok`, `changed`, `missing` or `unknown` and `recent` the ten newest firings, each `{key, order, date, kind, outcome, t, sessionId?, wallMs?, usage?, files?}`. Since the desk's P3: `watch`, present while the watch runs, its `status()` (`WatchStatus`, §4.2 `watch.ts`) — `{state, markets: {us, cn}: {state, session?, watched, notWatched, lastPollAt?, lastError?, uncovered?, today: {sent, suppressed, repeats}}, holder?, muted?, files, near, marks, pending, recent, filings: {state, symbols, aShares, seeded, lastPollAt?, lastError?}, ledgerError?}` — which the Desk view draws and `desk_state` carries without `marks`. `ledgerError`, present only when the ledger could not be read, names its code (`EACCES`, `EISDIR`) or its message, and `asleep` and `runs` are then empty: an unreadable ledger is a 200 that says so, never a 500. Mounted with the desk off too, so a `FACE_DESK=0` face answers `desk.enabled: false`. `npm run service` reads it — `status`, which compares its `pid` with launchd's job's, and `url`; and `install`, `start` and `restart`, which take any HTTP answer there for a held port — with no `Origin`, so it passes on `Host` |
| `POST /data/desk/pause` `{until?}` | `desk.ts` | the pause a page can set (Markets › Desk's Pause since P3, `js/host/desk.js`, posting `{}`; the old client's Desk panel left with that client), through http.ts's `fencedPost`: the fence, 405 and 415 before the body is read, then 413 and 400 `body must be a JSON object`; `until` a duration `parseDuration` reads (`30m`, `2h`, `1d`) or absent for a pause until a resume, anything else 400 `until must look like 30m, 2h or 1d`, before anything is written; then `writeOff` set by `page` — which never shortens a pause in force — answering `{ok: true, off}`, the pause in force afterwards, possibly a longer one that stood. No resume route: the page, like the phone, only pauses (charter D19). Mounted with the desk off too; like every `/data` route it takes no cookie, so a shell turn can pause the desk — the safe direction |

### 4.5 Persistent state the face writes

| Path | Writer | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `$DSH_HOME/profiles/<profile>/cordis.yml` | `composeFace` | rewritten to `[]` every boot; edit `cordis.patch.yml` |
| `$DSH_HOME/profiles/<profile>/{package.json, cordis.patch.yml, pnpm-workspace.yaml}` | `setupFaceProfile` | only when the profile *directory* is absent; an existing directory is left untouched even if one of the three files is missing |
| `$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml` | the `connection` row the face mounts | a `client-connection/browser-session` grant — the cookie's signing secret — written by the first boot on a home; the 0.1.1 CLI still reads the file's keys past it |
| `$DSH_HOME/storages/**` | dsh-base's storage rows | workspace registry records (`registry.create`, `attachSession`) |
| `$DSH_HOME/storages/session_projcache/sessions/<id>.json` | dsh-base's projection cache | one checkpoint record per session, written behind the log and throttled by `writeEveryEvents: 200` / `writeIntervalMs: 5000`; what `session/list` reads for a cold session's projections; bootstrapped once from 0.1.1's single `session_projcache.json`, which stays in place |
| `$DSH_HOME/sessions/<slug>/<id>/session.v4.jsonl.zstd`, `session.lock` | dsh's session persistence | published by a session's first WRITE-open under 0.2.0 — a prompt, a command, a fork, a room turn, any resume — beside a 0.1.1 `session.jsonl.zstd`, which stays byte-identical; never rolled back. A read-open migrates in memory and writes nothing, and opening a cold session in the chat pages it without activating it (§5.4) |
| `$DSH_HOME/face/archived.json` | `sessions.ts` | `{archived[], deleted[]}`; plain write |
| `$DSH_HOME/face/search-index.sqlite` | `search.ts` (through `search-index.ts`) | the search index: a SQLite file (0600, schema stamped `user_version` 2) holding a copy of the conversations' text (what the operator and Gravit said, `search-text.ts`) and, per conversation, the revision, the log count read and the log's size; it is derived and can be deleted — the next search rebuilds it from the stored logs — and it follows a deleted conversation out |
| `$DSH_HOME/face/channels.json` | `roster.ts` | `{version:1, channels:{<wsId>:{agents[], bots[]}}}`; file lock + atomic write, mode 0600; the one file that needs a cross-process lock because the reconcile writes on GET |
| `$DSH_HOME/face/roster.log` | `roster.ts` | append-only, one dated line per operator roster write |
| `$DSH_HOME/face/agents.json` | `panels.ts` | `{connected:[{bin,label}]}` |
| `$DSH_HOME/sessions/<slug>/<id>/` | `deleteSession` | removed with every generation, the lock and the temps, cwd-fenced |
| `strategies/<name>/` | `createChannel` | copied from `_template`, never overwritten |
| `strategies/<name>/analysis/<run>/` | the Lunhui rows (`face/plugins/lunhui/lib/runs.mjs`), in the face process | `analysis/` made on a strategy's first freeze and each run directory exclusively, both mode 0o700; `run.json` (`{run, strategy, kind, as_of, session, opened_at, sealed_at, snapshot_id, evidence: [{source, file, sha256, bytes, received_at, session, host, delayed}], artifacts}` — `as_of` the newest `received_at` and `session` the newest evidence session at seal, both null until then) and `metrics.json` (`{freezes, calls: {<module>: n}, rejections: {<module>: [category…]}, submitted: [module…]}`) at the run's opening, one `evidence-<source>.json` per source (at most 256 KiB, `limit-up`'s 1 MiB), then, from the module rows, `run.json` sealed on the first context read and one `<module>.json` artifact per module (`environment.json`, `sentiment.json`, `theme.json` in a `cn-market` run, `leader.json` and `mode.json` in a strategy run; written as `<module>.pending.json` and renamed, then named in `run.json` `artifacts`), new files `wx` at 0o600, `run.json` and `metrics.json` replaced by a fresh file renamed over the old after each change; outside any session's sandbox (§9, R39); the evidence files and a write's crash leftovers (`*.pending.json`, `*.tmp`) gitignored, the rest tracked (R42); the face's channel routes only read it, for the runs card (§5.2) |
| `bots/<id>/` | `createBot`, `updateBotSettings`, `updateSoul` | copied from `_template`; `preset.yml`, `SOUL.md` and the composition's persona row rewritten together, staged then renamed; never overwritten by create |
| `bots/<id>/journal/` | a bot's HOME session | workspace-write, cwd = the journal; the only directory a bot writes (the write to `../SOUL.md` is refused, proven in `room-smoke`) |
| `roles/<id>/` (`ROLE.md`, `role.yml`) | the operator | not written by the face — read once per boot by `composeFace` (`readRoles`) and rendered into Gravit's preset (§3.8); a missing roles directory or a malformed role refuses the boot |
| `bots/gravit/agent.cordis.yml` | `npm run render:roles` (the operator runs it) | the generated mirror of that render, for readers; the face composes nothing from it (`listBots` hashes it into the row's `revision` and parses nothing), and `tests/roles.test.ts` fails while it differs from the render |
| `dsh/profile/persona.md` | the operator | not written by the face — read by `composeFace` into `system-prompt`'s `personaPrefix`, and a malformed template refuses the boot |
| `$DSH_HOME/face/desk/events.jsonl` | `desk.ts` (`appendEvent`) | the desk's ledger: one JSON event per line, each with its `t` — `boot` (`pid`, `version`, `deskEnabled`), `shutdown` (`pid`, the exit `code`), `asleep` (`from`, `to`, `gapMs`), written by a face with the desk on; `off-set` (`by`: `telegram`, `page` or `terminal`; `until` for a timed pause) and `off-cleared` (`by`: `terminal` or `expiry`), written wherever the switch moves — the phone, any face's Pause route, `npm run desk`, the post that finds a pause expired; `desk-session` (`sessionId`, `reason`: `created` or `new`), `desk-turn` (`sessionId`, `source` — `telegram`, `user`, `alert`, `wake`, `schedule`, … — `turn`, `outcome`: `ended`, `timed-out`, `cancelled` or `failed`, `wallMs`, `usage` when the harness accounted for the turn — the four buckets and `routes` — `cancel` for a cancelled one, saying what cancelled it — `restart` for a phone turn a restart cut, which the boot records with `wallMs` 0 and no `usage` (spec §16 H3) — and `error` for a failed one) and `desk-refused` (`reason: "fence"`, the repo-relative `path`), written by the desk conversation, by the annotation lane for an alert's check (`annotator.ts`, `source: "alert"`) and, for a standing order's turn, by its firing; and, since P2, `standing-error` (`errors`: why `standing.yml` is refused or the firing ledger cannot be read), `calendar-error` (`date`, the `clock` asked, its `error`) and `budget-spent` (`date`, `used`, `dailyTokens`; once per ET date, through `appendRecordOnce`), written by the clock row; and, since P3, `mute-set` (`by`, `until` for a timed mute) and `mute-cleared` (`by`: `terminal` or `expiry`), the mute's, and `watch-load` (`file`, repo-relative, `loaded`, `refused` — each refusal as the phone line lists it — and `error` for a file refused whole), once per distinct load of a watch file, written by the watch through its `appendChain`; and, since spec §16 H3 (R93), `desk-carry` (`sessionId`; `queued`, the phone texts a graceful stop found waiting, oldest first, at most 20 — each `key`, the message's id — `<messageId>#<inbox id>@<at>` since plan B1a (`phone-bridge.ts` `deliveryKey`), `telegram:<update_id>` in a carry an older face wrote —, `text`, the operator's words cut at 4,000 characters, and `at`, ISO-8601, when they were written, when the face knew — and `cut`, the phone turn under way — `turn`, `key`, `at`), written by the desk conversation's dispose before its shutdown cancel, and `desk-carried` (`of`, the carry's `t`; `posted`, `skipped`), written by the boot that answered it; append-only under `withFileLock` (`events.jsonl.lock` beside it), created `0600`; past 50 MB the next append first moves it to `events.<t>.jsonl` (`:` as `-`), which nothing reads, and the new file opens with the old one's last `desk-session` line, so the desk conversation is found again; a failed write is one `gravit-face:` line on stderr, and the face serves on |
| `$DSH_HOME/face/desk/OFF`, `OFF.lock` | `desk.ts` (`writeOff`, `clearOff`), from the phone's `/pause`, `POST /data/desk/pause` and `npm run desk`; the operator by hand | the pause switch: while a file by that name exists the desk opens no turn (§4.2). Written atomically, `0600`, as `{setAt, by, until?}`; an empty or unreadable file, `touch`'s, is a terminal's open-ended pause. Lifted by `npm run desk -- resume`, by deleting it, or at its `until` (the next post lifts it, an `off-cleared` by `expiry`). `OFF.lock` is the switch's writer lock, held only around one set or lift, for up to 2 s (§9, R59) |
| `$DSH_HOME/face/desk/MUTE`, `MUTE.lock` | `desk.ts` (`writeMute` from the phone's `/mute <duration>`, through `phone-bridge.ts`; `clearMute` from `npm run desk -- unmute`, or the watch at the mute's end); the operator by hand | the watch's mute (P3): while it holds, no alert is sent and none annotated — each is recorded `suppressed: muted`, and a batch due under it is dropped and recorded — while detection and the ledger go on. `OFF`'s rules on its own lock: written atomically, `0600`, as `{setAt, by, until?}`; a mute from the phone always has an `until`, and one that would end sooner than the mute in force writes nothing; an empty or unreadable file, `touch`'s, is a terminal's open-ended mute; lifted only by `unmute`, the file's deletion or its own end (`mute-cleared` by `expiry`); every set and lift through the face is an `events.jsonl` line |
| `$DSH_HOME/face/desk/standing.yml` | the operator: `npm run desk -- arm` and `rearm` (`writeStanding`), or a hand edit | the standing orders and the day's token cap (`standing.ts`, §4.2): a mapping of `budget:` and `orders:` (since P4 an order may carry `market: cn` — absent is `us` — and a strategy order that wakes carries `levelsSha256`, 64 hex or `none`), mode `0600`, replaced atomically under its file lock (`standing.yml.lock` beside it) and only over the text the command read; the face only reads it — at the clock row's ticks, when its size, mtime or inode moved — and any fault in it stops every order until it is fixed |
| `$DSH_HOME/face/desk/firings.jsonl` | the clock row (`schedule.ts`: `started` through `appendRecordOnce`, `refused`, `missed`, `interrupted`, `expired`) and a firing (`firing.ts`: `producer`, `woke`, `finished`), through `appendRecord` | the firing ledger, one record per step of each firing, each with its `t` and `kind` (`FiringRecord`, §4.2): the `started` that consumes the key `<id>:<session date>`, once whatever the number of faces; the producer's run (`ok`, `error`, `code`, `timedOut`, `wallMs`, `chars` counted before the cut); the session woken and its route; the `finished` (`wallMs`, the producer, the turn — outcome, cancel, deadline, wall time, usage, error — the files the turn changed, `filesTruncated`, a fence `violation`, `withheld`, what `deliver` answered, `chars`); a refusal (`reason`, `detail`, `reported`; since P4 `levels-hash` among the reasons), a miss (`anchor`, `why` — since P4 `cutoff` too, with its `moment` — the `asleep` gap, `foundAt`), a cut-off `started` found at boot (`interrupted`) and an expiry (`expired`, keyed `<id>:<expires>`); since P4 the `started` carries `levelsSha`, a miss, an interrupted firing and an expiry whose line the pause held carry `held: true`, and a `phoned` record (`of`, and a refusal's `reason` and `detail`) follows a held line once its send resolved final, so a restart holds it no more (§9, R81). A key's date is its order's market date — Beijing's for `cn`. `0600`, locked (`firings.jsonl.lock`) and rotated as the ledger is (`firings.<t>.jsonl` past 50 MB, which nothing reads), the clock row's own appends carrying the day's `started` lines into the new file (§9, R66); a torn line is skipped, and a file the face cannot read stops every firing until it can |
| `$DSH_HOME/face/desk/alerts.jsonl` | the watch (`watch.ts`, through one `appendChain`) | the alert ledger (`AlertRecord`, §4.2 `watch-eval.ts`), one JSON line each: `alert` (`id`, `pass`, the session `date`, `key`, `market`, `symbol`, `label`, `trigger`, `gap`, `quote` — price, `asOf`, feed, status, previous close and change — `holding`, `plan`, `source` file and index, `decision` `send` or `suppressed` with `suppressed` `cooldown`, `cap`, `muted`, `off` or `window`, `annotate`), `delivered` (`id`, the outlet's answer, `latency: {tradeMs, receivedMs}`, both `null` when the send was queued), `batch` (`id`, `date`, the capped `alerts`, its `delivery`, or `dropped` `off` or `muted`) and `annotation` (`pass`, `alerts`, `result` `opened` or `refused` with its `reason` and `sessionId`); since spec §16, `annotated` (`pass`, `sessionId`, `outcome` — the lane's turn's — `sent`, the message ids its reply went as, and `text`, the reply cut at 2,000 characters), written when the lane's run ends, a `delivered` with `replayed: true` and null latencies for an alert a restart caught between its `send` and its `delivered` and sent late at the first read, and a `delivered` `{ undelivered: "lost to a restart" }` for one older than 10 minutes; `0600`, under its lock, rotated past 50 MB as `events.jsonl` is, with nothing carried (R75). Read once at the watch's start into `rebuildDay` (the last 36 hours: keys, cooldowns, the hour's sends, the pending batch) and `findOrphans`, kept in memory for 48 hours for a phone reply's context (`contextFor`), and read by the pre-close brief and `/data/desk/status` |
| `$DSH_HOME/face/desk/filings.jsonl` | the watch (`watch.ts`, through one `appendChain`) | the filings' baseline and record (`FilingRecord`, §4.2 `filings.ts`): `seeded` (`symbol`, every `accessions` its first good poll listed, recorded silently) and `seen` (`symbol`, `accession`, `form`, `filingDate`, `accepted`, `items`, `url`), one line each; `0600`, under its lock; read once at the watch's start into `baselineFrom`, and by the brief's `filings` block. A filing's alert is in `alerts.jsonl` |
| `$DSH_HOME/face/desk/watch.lease`, `watch.lease.lock` | the watch (`watch.ts`) | which face watches this home: `{pid, since, beat}`, written atomically (`0600`) under P0's lock, the beat every 30 s; a lease whose pid is gone or whose beat is 120 s old is taken over by a check and a write under the lock, then a re-read; removed at `dispose` when it is this face's (§4.2, ruling 7) |
| `$DSH_HOME/face/desk/run/` | `runScriptProducer` (`producer.ts`), for a firing's script producer | the run base: made `0700`, refused when it is a symlink; each run copies the verified script into a fresh `gravit-producer-*` directory (`0700`), the copy `0400`, and removes the directory afterwards (one line when it cannot) — so what runs is the bytes that were hashed, never the file in `scripts/` |
| `$DSH_HOME/face/desk/inbox.cursor` | `phone-bridge.ts` | the highest account inbox number the bridge has taken (plan B1a), written atomically (`0600` in the `0700` desk directory) only once that message's post or `/new` settled — after the desk session's log was flushed — or its command was answered, or after 5 minutes with one line; never moved by a read; absent on a first boot, so the bridge reads the account's ring from 0; a value past the account's `last` (a fresh account home) is said in one line and starts again from 0 |
| `$DSH_HOME/face/desk/telegram.jsonl`, `telegram.offset`, `outbox.json` | nobody since plan B1a | the retired Telegram bridge's (`telegram.ts`, deleted) records, offset and outbox; an upgraded home keeps them on disk, read and written by nothing (§9, R96). Their successors are the account's: `<account home>/identity/telegram.offset`, `outbox.json` and its log lines (§3.9 "Identity") |
| `$DSH_HOME/face/service/face.log`, `face.err.log` | launchd: the service's stdout and stderr | appended across runs, never rotated; `install` creates the directory `0700`, and the plist's `Umask 077` gives the logs, like everything else the service's face creates, no group or other access; `npm run service -- logs` and `url` read them |
| `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.gravit.face.plist` | `npm run service -- install` (the operator) | the LaunchAgent (`scripts/service.ts`, §4.2), mode `0644`, carrying no key; rewritten by every `install`, removed by `uninstall` |
| `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.gravit.face.watchdog.plist` | `npm run service -- install` (the operator) | the watchdog's LaunchAgent (spec §16 H4; `watchdogPlan`, §4.2), mode `0644`, carrying no key and no port; written with the face's by every `install` since 2026-11-02 — a service installed earlier has none until `install` runs again — and removed first by `uninstall` |
| `$DSH_HOME/face/service/watchdog.log`, `watchdog.err.log` | launchd: the watchdog's stdout and stderr | appended across runs, never rotated, under the plist's `Umask 077`: each run's `health <code> <reason>` line, each line it sent or held under `OFF`, and the service's restart's own lines, the token redacted — up to 288 lines a day when nothing happens |
| `$DSH_HOME/face/desk/watchdog.json` | `scripts/watchdog.ts` | the watchdog's state between runs (`WatchdogState`: the desk's `outageSince`, `degradedChecks`, `degradedSaid`, `degradedSince`, `restartedAt`, and since plan B1a `accountDownChecks`, `accountSince`, `accountSaid`, `marketDownChecks`, `marketSince`, `marketSaid`), written atomically (`0600`) once at every run, so its mtime is the last check; the desk's part cleared at every `0` and `3`, the account's and the market's when they answer again; `status` reads it for its `watchdog:` line |
| `$DSH_HOME/.env` | `npm run service -- install` (the operator), or the operator by hand | created by `install` only when the home has none: the allow-listed names (`DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, `APCA_API_KEY_ID`, `APCA_API_SECRET_KEY`, `APCA_API_BASE_URL`, `IFIND_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `IFIND_REFRESH_TOKEN`, any `ALPHA_*`) from the repo root's `.env.deepseek`, `.env.alpaca` and `.env.ifind`, every other name reported and left out (`FACE_DESK_MODEL` among them: set it by hand; since plan B1a a `TELEGRAM_*` name too — Telegram's token is the account's, §3.9 — and an existing home's `TELEGRAM_*` lines are read by nothing and are the operator's to remove) — when no key file holds an allow-listed name, `install` writes nothing and says so (`wrote no …`); mode `0600`, opened exclusively, so a file or a dangling link that appears in its place is refused; never rewritten — `install` reads an existing one only to name the expected keys it lacks — so it is a copy: a key rotated in the repo's key files reaches a terminal face but not the service until this file is edited too, and a line is copied as written, a `$(…)` or `${…}` arriving literally. dsh's layered env load reads it at every boot (§1) |
| `desk/journal/` | the desk session (`gravit-desk`) and each firing of a `dir: desk` standing order, which saves the pre-close brief as `briefs/<date>-preclose.md`; the face makes the directory | workspace-write, cwd = the journal, as a bot's home is (the write to `../levels.yml` is refused, proven in `desk-smoke`); the desk guard denies a desk turn's write of a fence name there, and the fence refuses every desk turn while one exists (§3.4, §4.2); ignored but for its `.gitkeep` |

Not written any more: `$DSH_HOME/profiles/node_modules`, 0.1.1's module link farm (a stale one
answers only for a row outside the face's closure, §3.1; PLAN D13). Never written by the face:
`$DSH_HOME/settings.yaml` (PLAN D1).

Deleting a session does **not** detach it from its channel: `deleteSession` removes the
persistence directory and tombstones the id but never touches the registry, although in-process
the workspace entity does expose one (`WorkspaceEntity.detachSession`, reachable through
`ctx.workspaceRegistry.list()`; not a registry method, not a Remote, and not declared by the
face's `WorkspaceLike`). Recorded, not fixed.

### 4.6 Environment

| Variable | Read by | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `FACE_PORT` | `main.ts` | `3090` | `"0"` asks the OS; `""` means default |
| `FACE_PROFILE` | `main.ts`, `setup.ts` | `face` | honored by both `setup` and `start` |
| `FACE_ACCOUNT_SEAT_DIR` | `account-seat.ts` (`seatDir`) | the repo's `account/` (`DEFAULT_SEAT_DIR`) | the Account package the seat process runs from (`npm ci` there); set it only to run the seat from another copy |
| `FACE_BIND` | `overlay.ts` (`faceBind`), for the `webserver` row; `main.ts` for the boot line | `127.0.0.1` | the webserver's bind (§4.3): a concrete address only (dsh 0.2.1 refuses a wildcard at load); in the compose agent box the entrypoint sets the container's own address (`hostname -i`) — never a LAN address on the host, where it would serve the `/data` routes to the LAN behind a forgeable `Host` fence (§9, R51) |
| `PORTFOLIO_BIND`, `PORTFOLIO_HOSTS` | `account/src/portfolio/server.ts`, not the face | `127.0.0.1`, none | the Account's listener and the extra `host:port` values its `Host` fence admits (§3.9); set by `compose.yml` for the Account box (`0.0.0.0`, `account:4820`) and nowhere else |

module rows take no config. A `now` clock is a function, and `bootFace` structured-clones every
patch, so no patch can carry one into a booted row: on a real boot the freezes read the system
clock, and `tests/lunhui-market-run-smoke.test.ts` shifts `globalThis.Date` for its boot instead.

Every child the face spawns for a local agent run or probe has these scrubbed — an enumerated list
(`SCRUBBED_ENV` in `agents.ts`), not a prefix glob: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`,

Every other variable is inherited, `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` included; deliberately so
for `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `CODEX_HOME` (the CLI logs itself in; the face
never handles its credentials).

### 4.7 Gate 2: the per-order approval producer

Until 2026-09-04 nothing in the composed tree could raise an approval card for an MCP tool
call: the only producer of `{kind:"ask"}` was a sandbox escalation (a shell or file write
outside the workspace under `workspace-write`), and an MCP call never takes that path. The
approval *channel* — request, answerer, card, outcome, the paired `approval/asked` /
`approval/decided` events — was real and drilled; the producer for orders was absent.
`face/src/orders.ts` is that producer, armed by `boot.ts`'s `armOrderGate` inside boot's
`prepare` — before any row mounts, each half on its own `hostCtx.inject` fiber — in two parts,
because neither alone suffices:

1. A **`tools/pre-execute` listener**, registered `prepend` so it is outermost in the waterfall
   and an inner listener cannot swallow its answer. Non-order tools pass through. For the
   Account seat's twelve writes (`SEAT_WRITE_RAW_NAMES`, §3.1) and
   any tool under the face's own `mcp__account__` prefix that is neither one of them nor one of the
   thirty reads the gate knows (`SEAT_READ_RAW_NAMES`; carded until classified, so an Account that grows
   a tool cannot grow an ungated write) — matched on the **raw name suffix**
   (`name === raw || name.endsWith("__" + raw)`), so an operator renaming the MCP server row
   cannot slip a tool past — it returns `{kind:"ask", reason:"Account seat - <tool>: side=… usd=…
   symbol=… venue=…", displayReason:{en: <the same line>}}` under policy `ask` (the face does not
   know a venue's kind, and the Account's own card says PAPER
   (`describeOrder`: `key=value` pairs in a readable order, values capped at 40 characters, unknown keys
   appended; a key that is not a name (`x venue`, `a=b`) is denied before any card, at any depth, since
   keys are written bare; a value that carries whitespace, a quote, a bracket or a semicolon is drawn as a JSON
   string, cut first where it is cut, so the line reads back pair by pair — the client's card is
   titled from it — and no value can pass itself off as another pair; the key fields the operator
   decides on — a venue, a symbol, an id, an address, a payee's URL, an earn product, a pay's body —
   are shown WHOLE up to 120 characters, and a call whose key field cannot be shown whole is
   **denied** before any card: too long, or a URL that is not http(s), carries userinfo or does not
   parse; a batch's `legs` are each described as one order and a nested object is shown one level
   deep, with the same key fields whole or denied, a list's scalars under their parent key's rule
   (`to[2]`, `url[1]`), anything nested deeper than that one level denied, and more than ten legs
   denied — a card that read `legs=?`, or `extra=?` inside a leg, would approve blind). The retired
   order tools, `place_order` and `cancel_order` under any server name (`RETIRED_ORDER_RAW_NAMES`,
   the removed Python package's pair), are never carded: the guard denies them outright, its reason
   telling the operator to remove the MCP row that registers them. The approval
   request carries no arguments — only the
   tool name, the call id, `reason` and `displayReason` — and `api-remotes` forwards it to every
   connected browser's `$events` stream as an `approval/request` waterfall keyed by `eventId`.
   The card shows the tool name, the order line and two buttons; an upstream-style panel draws
   `displayReason` instead of `reason`, so both carry the line, and the order details reach the
   human only if they are inside it. Under policy `never` (`danger-full-access`, or a runtime
   preset switch) it returns **`deny`** in its own words rather than `ask`, because dsh would
   otherwise render the false `the user rejected tool …` when nobody was asked. No `approval`
   service or no session → deny. (`PreToolDecision` is stated structurally, widened with 0.2:
   `deny.info`, `cancel`, `ask.displayReason`.)
2. A **`tools.guard`**, deny-only and evaluated on *every* allow, including the allow that
   `allowed-once` becomes. It asks the calling session's **event log** — not "did my listener
   see this call" — for an `approval/asked` carrying this exact `callId` **and this tool's
   name** paired with an `approval/decided` whose outcome is `allowed-once`. A sighting is not a
   grant; only the log is. The log is read through `snapshotEvents()`, and only for a gated tool
   (a snapshot copies the whole log): 0.2.0 removed the `events` getter this guard used to read,
   the read went `undefined` without a word, and every approved order was denied. An UNREADABLE
   log — no `snapshotEvents`, a throw, a non-list — is denied with its own sentence,
   `cannot read this session's log to verify an allowed-once approval (dsh Session API changed:
   …)`, never with the "without a logged allowed-once approval" one; `orderGuardReasonForSession`
   is the one producer of both. The guard reads the name alone, per call, so a seat write that
   registers after boot is guarded all the same; a retired order tool is denied first, whatever
   the log holds.
3. A **boot audit** (`auditOrderTools` over the live registry, `{gated, uncovered, retired}`): a
   server carrying the seat's tools of which the gate covers no write (`uncovered`), or any
   registered retired order tool (`retired`), makes the face dispose the tree and throw — a gate
   that covers nothing must not look healthy, and the seat is the only order path. A home still
   mounting the Alpaca MCP row of before 2026-10-24 that registers the pair does not boot until the
   row is removed (that row's server cannot start anyway: its package is gone). A write the
   Account renames under the face's own prefix is carded as unclassified, and under a renamed
   server it is the audit's `uncovered`; `tests/account-seat-smoke.test.ts` against the repo's
   `account/` is the canary (§7.3). Boot
   also refuses a tree with no ACTIVE `api-remotes` entry (§4.1), without which every ask
   resolves `unavailable` and every order is denied at once, with no card anywhere.

Consequences worth knowing: a card with no connected browser **blocks**, it does not deny —
the gateway holds the request and replays it, same `eventId`, to the next `$events` client;
grants are one-shot (`allowed-once`, no allow-always); the seat's `portfolio_live_cancel` is gated
like every other write (the Account itself never cards it), so under policy `never` the
risk-reducing action is refused too; and the gate binds only when dsh runs inside the face — a dsh
tree composed without the face has only the Account's own Guard card. The answer is the
browser's `POST /api/$events/result` under its `$events` clientId (§5.2); the host would accept
any outcome of the approval vocabulary from a client, so keeping the operator to
`allowed-once` / `rejected` is `client/js/wire/api.js`'s job. **It is a gate, not containment** (§9,
R2), and the log proves a grant was recorded, not who recorded it (§9, R3a). Drill status is in
§7.4: the refusing half and the admitting half are automated on a real tree over `mcp__drill__*`
stand-ins of the seat's writes, the admitting half through the real `$events` channel too; a
person reading a seat card against the real service is the account-seat drill's, not yet run.

**An order tool the caller cannot see.** Before the policy, an order tool the CALLING scope cannot see —
`tools.get(exec.name, exec.agent)` is `undefined`, read from the live registry at call time:
not registered in this tree (a seat write with no seat mounted), or hidden by the session's
preset (the desk's mask, a masked bot's) — is denied in the gate's words, `<name> is not
available to this session - it is not registered here, or this session's preset hides it -
so no approval card is raised and the order does not run`: dsh runs the waterfall before it
resolves visibility (the desk spec's spike 3), so asking there raised a card that could only
park, and an approved one would then fail `unknown tool` at dispatch. With no registry live,
the listener decides as before. (`PreToolDecision` is stated structurally, widened with 0.2:

**The card's notice on the phone** (plan B1a; spec §5.6, the operator's Q2: notify only). When
Gate 2's decision is `ask`, `armOrderGate` calls `FaceBootOptions.onCardAsked(name, args)` before it
returns the decision, unawaited — never for a deny (a hidden tool, policy `never`, an unshowable key
field, no session), a read, another tool or a retired one; a throw from it is one `console.error`
line, and the card is asked either way. `main.ts` passes it only when `FACE_DESK` is not `0`
(ruling 10: a second face on a scratch home never phones), as `announceCard(cardPhone, name,
args)` (`card-notice.ts`, §4.2): one plain line, `Your call · <what> — waiting in Gravit` — for an
order `Your call · Buy 10 NVDA · limit 183 · alpaca-paper — waiting in Gravit` — sent as kind
`card` through the account's send, so the Cards waiting row and quiet hours decide whether it goes.
It carries no button and no link: every scheme link and `//host` and every dotted quad become
`<link>`, and every `.` not between two digits becomes `·`, so `evil.com` reads `evil·com` and no
client can make a host of it (the scrub is the account's own, byte for byte, `tests/card-notice.test.ts`
comparing the two blocks); the line is cut at 600 characters and scrubbed again after the cut. The
operator answers the card in the browser, never on the phone; the desk's `/pause` and `/mute` do
not hold a notice, which is not a desk send. The account's Guard card for the same write phones a
notice of its own (§9, R97).

### 4.8 The re-host's operator decisions (and the 0.2.1-rc.5 upgrade's)

The dsh 0.2.0-rc.2 re-host (2026-09-30) defaulted every decision that changes what Gravit can
do, what leaves the machine, or which operator data survives; each stays the operator's. The
numbers are the re-host plan's, which the code comments cite as `PLAN D<n>`. The go-live runbook
(`docs/superpowers/runbooks/2026-09-30-dsh-0.2.0-rc.2-go-live.md`, §4) walks each one that
needs an answer before the operator's home moves.

| PLAN | Decision | Default in the tree | To choose otherwise |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | a `profileContext` (settings forms, a live model save, `dsh-hmr`, `plugin-manager`) | none (§4.1) | a code change: every face layer moves into `profileContext.overlays`, and the first boot imports and renames the shared `settings.yaml` |
| D2 | Gravit's default model | dsh-base's `deepseek-official/deepseek-flash` until the operator adds the `agent-default-model` row (§3.1) | that row in `profiles/face/cordis.patch.yml` |
| D3–D7, D9 | telemetry, session-log upload, package inventory, `web_fetch`, MCP resource tools, `ralph` and `str_replace_editor` | the 0.1.1 posture (§4.3) | one operator row each |
| D8 | the browser cookie on `/data` (and, until stage 2 removed them, the `/market` and `/account` pages) | fence-only, as at 0.1.1 | a code change behind `isTrustedDataRequest` (Connection's `requestRejection`) |
| D10 | an HTTP proxy policy | none: the face's own fetches go direct; children still inherit proxy variables | a code change (`installProxyFromEnvironment`), which reroutes every fetch |
| D11 | the ten 0.1.1 room sessions the 0.2 migration refuses | left on disk and reported, never rewritten (§9, R20) | archive them in the face, or rewrite COPIES — never the originals — to a source kind the migration admits |
| D12 | the 0.1.1 global CLI and the 0.1.1 face on the shared home | never again once 0.2.0 has written it: 0.1.1 re-heals its link farm, forks history away from `session.v4`, and on its next workspace write detaches every 0.2-born session from its channel in `workspace.json`; a full restore of the backup is the only rollback | upgrade the CLI (its first run imports `settings.yaml` into its OWN profile) or give 0.1.1 tools their own `DSH_HOME` |
| D13 | `$DSH_HOME/profiles/node_modules` | delete once D12 holds | keep it: a mixed-version hazard for any row outside the face's closure |
| D14 | un-archiving host archives | refused with a 409 naming why (§4.4) | route it to `workspaceRegistry.unarchiveSession` |
| D15 | telemetry opt-in | the policy row off; `DSH_TELEMETRY_DISABLED` still works | `- id: session-telemetry-otel` / `disabled: false` |
| D16 | opening a cold session in the chat | page-only, never activating (§5.4) | follow on open, as the upstream client does — every browsed session then gets a v4 log and a lock |
| D17 | three subagent children with a version-2 descriptor and one log with a sequence gap, unreadable under 0.2 | left on disk and reported, like D11 (§9, R20) | export their transcripts while a 0.1.1 face can still render them, or wait for an upstream migration edge |
| D18 | the spill budget | dsh-base's `maxInlineTokens: 12500` (§9, R27) | one row restating `spill-policy`; about 4,200 tokens restores the old CJK budget and spills ASCII three times earlier |

The dsh 0.2.1-rc.5 upgrade (2026-11-02; spec
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-02-dsh-0.2.1-rc.5-upgrade-design.md` §8) re-took D9 and added
PLAN D19–D27, numbered on from the re-host's; the code comments cite them by the same ids, bare.

| PLAN | Decision | Default in the tree | To choose otherwise |
|---|---|---|---|
| D9 (re-taken) | `ralph` after dsh-base dropped its row | kept: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-ralph` declared and inserted by the policy layer with `maxRounds: 64` (§4.3) | `- id: tool-ralph` / `disabled: true`; or retire it in code (one commit) |
| D19 | dsh-base's new `working_directory {cd}` tool, which moves a session's directory | disabled by the policy layer; the `working-directory` service and its runtime context stay (§4.3) | `- id: tool-working-directory` / `disabled: false` |
| D20 | how a role runs at 0.2.1 | one preset per role, `role-<id>`, and the face's own blocking role tool, `plugins/role.mjs`, over `startActivation` with `delivery: "caller"` (§3.8) | dsh's `dsh-tool-subagent` with `agentPreset`, the report arriving as a notice — rejected: it turns the research run into a chain of notice-driven turns, loses a report when the face is not live at settlement and lets dsh's guidance start roles in parallel; re-taken if a later dsh drops caller delivery |
| D21 | the persona's working directory | not named: the `working-directory` runtime context states it on every request (§4.3) | none: the 0.2.1 loop registers no `cwd` variable |
| D22 | dsh-base's new `web-deepseek-api` row | mounted, unselected: no request unless the `web` row selects its providers; D6's two restated configs drop no new key | a `web` row selecting `deepseek-search-api` / `deepseek-fetch-api` |
| D23 | dsh-base's new `remote-access` row (the gateway's method-level access control) | dsh-base's own, no overlay row: the cookie-signed browser is the owner, which access control never checks | none needed for the face; a peer that is not the owner would meet it |
| D24 | where the real boots run | from a checkout outside `/tmp` and `$TMPDIR`; the room and bots fixtures refuse a temp-root checkout (`tests/fixture-root.ts`), the other fence smokes name the precondition (§7.1) | none: under either root dsh's `workspace-write` grants the write the smoke proves refused |
| D25 | the second user-global instruction file (`<DSH_AGENTS_HOME or ~/.agents>/AGENTS.md`), read with no row switch | audited, not overridden: `bootFace` prints one stderr line per global `AGENTS.md` that exists (§4.1 step 8) | delete the file, or move `DSH_AGENTS_HOME` (which also moves `skill-filesystem`'s default roots) |
| D26 | going back to 0.2.0 after rc.5 has run | lossy: every rc.5 `bash` call writes `job/registered` / `job/settled`, a `cd` writes `working-directory/change`, and 0.2.0 refuses a log with an event type it does not know; the backup taken before the first boot and the 0.2.0 checkout with its own `node_modules` are the way back | none: never one session's files |
| D27 | dsh's own `subagent` and `subagent_fork` | follow upstream: an id at once, a settlement notice (dropped if the face is not live), the fork continuable; the persona says so (§3.6, §4.3) | face-owned blocking versions over caller delivery with dsh-base's rows disabled, should a drill show Gravit relying on a blocking fork |

## 5. Frontend: the browser client (`face/client`)

Since 2026-10-19 the page at `/` is **gravit-ui** — the settled front end of
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-09-demo-v2-gravit-frontend-design.md`, mounted on the face by
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-19-gravit-ui-on-face-design.md`'s route A (all three of its
stages are built; the plans are `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-19-gravit-face-stage-1.md`,
`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-20-gravit-face-stage-2.md` and
`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-20-gravit-face-stage-3.md`, their rulings and the drill record
`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-19-gravit-face-ledger.md`). Vanilla ES modules, no bundler, no
framework: one store, pure reducers, string renderers, one `innerHTML` per render with
`data-action` delegation. Every host string passes through `esc()` (`js/html.js`) before it
reaches the page; the one HTML the page builds from host text is markdown — Gravit's answers, a
room member's, a channel's thesis — DOM-built by `js/wire/markdown.js` and serialized. Stage 1
serves **Messages** — the session list, a session's real transcript, the composer, the three gate
cards, rooms; stage 2 **Markets** and **Account**, which replaced the old `/market` and
`/account` pages and since the graft's stage 1 (2026-10-22,
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-22-account-graft-design.md` §6.1–§6.2, its plan
`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-22-account-graft-1-reads.md` and ledger
`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-22-account-graft-ledger.md`) read Linqi's Account through the
face's proxy (§4.4) — Markets the Account's markets by its tabs, the stars and a search, a
market's page with its candles and venues, the A shares among them, read from the Account; Account the
Account's Portfolio, Venues, Agents and Cards and the Statement drawer — and since the graft's
stage 2 (2026-10-24, the same design's §6.3–§6.4, its plan
`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-23-account-graft-2-owner-trade.md`) the page is one of the
Account's owner devices (a P-256 key the browser holds, paired and signing at the Account's door
through the proxy's `pair`, `prepare` and `exchange`), **Trade** (`#/trade`) places the owner's hand orders, and
the owner's other keys sign from Account and Markets, each drawn only while the page signs —
and since 2026-11-01 (the Account's two parts, `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-01-account-two-parts-design.md`
§5, plans 4a, 4b and 5) the face is the Account's only page: the Market half (Change… on Trade;
Close…, Change… and Leverage… on a market's page and the Portfolio; a market's page with the Account's view of
the owner in it, its order book, its latest trades and a perpetual's funding) and the wallet half
(the Account screen's tabs Portfolio · Money · Venues · Agents · Cards · Rules, Sell many,
every connector kind, every limit scope and every ask granted, Settings › Devices' sign-out with
Guard first) — and since plan B1b (2026-11-04, `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-03-account-split-and-identity-design.md`
§5.1–§5.2, §5.6, its plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-04-identity-plan-b1b-identity-tab.md`) a seventh
tab, Identity (Gravit's networks, Connect Telegram in four sheets and one signature, what reaches the
operator where with quiet hours, Not you); the Account's own Superagent (the Desk and its Brains), Intents and Memory are drawn
nowhere (spec §5.4); stage 3 the list
grouped by channel with a page per channel (its status, thesis, backtests, journal, files and
agent and bot rosters), the row actions (fork, archive, un-archive, delete), **Discover** — the
inventory of what Gravit runs: the MCP servers, the bots, the local CLI agents and Gravit itself,
the skills, with the face's few runtime actions and no shop — and the research surfaces (tool
results drawn as tables, tiles and charts; a conversation's subagent children, with Stop; a room
member's trace). The product speaks English, and the wire's Chinese prose (a quote's or a
provider's message, a search note) never reaches a screen: a state is worded
from the wire's enums, and the old chat page's pure modules moved under `js/wire/` with their
words in English; what the operator and Gravit wrote (a channel's files, a bot's name and soul, a
skill) and what a server says of its tools are drawn as written, escaped. The muted lines that
say what something is doing — the status line under the composer, Discover's own line, the A
shares' quote connection, a search's state, the watchlist's trouble, the Account's own refusal
sentence drawn as its words, the Account's and a channel's stale stamps, a tool result's
`Partial` — are the only explanatory lines a screen carries. Since the dsh UI port's plan 6
(2026-11-04) every word the face itself writes on the page — a label, a key, a status line, a
sheet's `said`, an aria-label — is read from one English table, `js/i18n/en.js`, through
`js/i18n/words.js` (§5.4, "The words"); the move changed not one byte of any screen (D35). What
is drawn as written stays outside it: titles, the operator's, Gravit's and bots' words, Lunhui's
output and the modules' Chinese sub-titles, dsh's and the Account's texts, tickers and symbols,
key names, numbers in `en-US`, the A-share units and the room's two notices in Chinese.

### 5.1 Pages and files

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `index.html` | the shell: `<title>Gravit</title>`, `#app`, the two sheets, an inline script that reads `gravit-ui.prefs` once before first paint and applies the saved theme, then the text and code sizes and the two font families as `js/prefs.js` `cssOf` sets them (the same rules written again inline, since a module runs after the first paint; `prefs.test.js` holds the two together), `js/app.js` as a module. Holds not one byte of host data. The Google Fonts link (Manrope 400–800 · Noto Sans SC 400, 500, 700 and 800 · IBM Plex Mono 400 and 500) is the browser's own fetch — offline the system stack stands in |
| `js/app.js` | `boot(win, host)`: the store, the live layer, the actions, the markets, account, seat, channel, Discover, module, Run sheet and trace host layers, the owner device, the owner sheet and Trade (stage 2 of the graft), the tab's Account stream and the render loop (§5.4); `makeStore`, `initialState`, `prefsOf`, `routeOf`, `settle`, `answersFrom`, `complete`, `gravitMarkdown`, `getJsonVia` (a refusal rejects with its status and, when it parses, the face's body as `error.body`, where the hosts read the Account's sentence), `postJsonVia`, `Timers`, `SEARCH_QUIET_MS` (300) are exported for the tests |
| `js/i18n/words.js`, `en.js` | the face's words (the dsh UI port's plan 6, spec §5.10): `en.js` is `EN`, one frozen flat table of literal keys (`<area>.<part>.<name>`, an area then one or two lower-camel segments, 29 areas from `common` to `lunhui`; 1,721 keys since main's Slack merged (1,686 at plan 6), 33 of them plurals); a value is a non-empty string or `{one, other}`, holds no `<`, `>`, `"` or an `&` before a letter or `#`, and names its params `{name}` (`{n}` in a plural). `words.js` reads the active table: `t(key, params)` plain text (for `esc()`, `attrs()` and lines held in state), `th(key, params)` HTML text (the value verbatim, every param escaped unless it is `rawHtml(markup)`'s), `tn`/`thn` a plural's form by its count (`Number(n) === 1`, `{n}` `String(n)` unless given); a key the active table lacks reads from `EN`, one `EN` lacks reads as itself, a missing or null param as nothing; a value with no `{` is returned as it is, one with params costs one replace with a module-level regex. `setTable(table)` (an object only; the epoch moves when the identity changes), `withTable(table, fn)` (synchronous, restored in `finally`) and `wordsEpoch()` (the count the memoized renderers add to their keys) are plan 7's switch's seam; nothing calls `setTable` on the page yet |
| `js/prefs.js` | the sizes and fonts (plan 6, spec §5.11, D31), pure: `SIZES` (`textSize` 12–20, 15; `codeSize` 10–16, 12), `sizeOf(name, v)` (a whole px, clamped; the base for anything not a finite number), `cleanFont(v)` (composed to NFC first, so a decomposed accent stays a letter, then every character outside letters, digits, space, `_`, `.` and `-` a space, spaces collapsed, at most 64 code points; `''` for the default), `cssOf(prefs)` (`--fs`, `--fm`, `--font-sans`, `--font-mono`, each `null` at its default; a family as `"<name>", var(--font-*-base)`), `applyPrefs(root, prefs)` (each value set, each default removed) |
| `js/keys.js` | the page's keys in one table (plan 6, spec §5.12): `SHORTCUTS` (frozen; four General rows — `newConversation` ⌥⌘N, `searchConversations` ⌥⌘K, `settings` ⌥⌘,, `shortcuts` ⌘/ — each with its `code` and `mods`, and five Composer rows — Enter, ⇧Enter, `/`, `@`, Esc — that the sheet lists and nothing matches; every row `bound: true` until the browser drill finds one the browser keeps), `shortcut(id)`, `shortcutWords(row)` (what it does, a literal-keyed `t` read when asked), `chordOf(ev, mac, table?)` (the General row a keydown is, matched on `ev.code` and the modifier flags, ⌘ `metaKey` on a Mac and `ctrlKey` elsewhere, the other not held; the two punctuation rows, `settings` and `shortcuts`, also on `ev.key` `,` or `/` with the same modifiers, for AZERTY and QWERTZ, where the character sits on another key's code; `null` while an IME composes — `isComposing` or keyCode 229 —, for AltGr off a Mac (`getModifierState('AltGraph')`: it sets Ctrl and Alt both and types a character, `ń` on a Polish layout, which the page must not swallow), and for a row not bound), `chordLabel(row, mac)` (the names, `⌥⌘K` or `Ctrl+Alt+K`). dsh's ⌥⌘G, ⇧⌘F, ⌥⌘A and Esc twice are not in it (D33) |
| `js/store.js`, `js/reducers/index.js` | `createStore({initial, reducers, storage, key, accept, persist})` — `dispatch(type, payload)`, `get()`, `subscribe(fn)`; the reducer table is the merge of the per-slice modules |
| `js/reducers/host.js` | the host reducers (§5.3): `hostStatus`, `hostList`, `hostWindow`, `hostEvent`, `hostGate`, `hostGateGone`, `hostProjection`, `hostThinking`, `hostPreview`, `markSeen`, `hostThumb` (`{attachmentId, src}`, a history image's thumb — the whole stored image — as a `blob:` URL, `null` for one the host will not give; the dsh UI port's plan 4); since plan 5 `hostEarlier` (an earlier page folded in before the window), `hostEarlierLoading`, `foldMessages` (a window folded by `hostEvent`'s rules in one pass), and `hostProjection`'s `turnOutline` and `sessionStats` keys |

The host's account: the page (`accountLoading`/`accountLoaded`/`accountFailed`, the failure keeping the last page with the Account's sentence), `holdings*`, `paper*` and `statement*` (each failure keeping the sentence), `history*`, `agents*`, the connect and paper sheets' reads — `venuesHere*`, `paperBooks*`, `keyfile*` (its `keyfileLoading` records what it asked), `reach*`, each failure keeping the sentence —, `setHistoryRange` (`1d`, `1w`, `1m`, `all`); the Account seat's (`seatLoading`/`seatLoaded`/`seatFailed`, a failure keeping the last view); the drawers' `openStatement`/`closeStatement`, `openVenueDetails`/`closeVenueDetails` (a venue's Details, one drawer at a time through `closeOverlays`) and `openSettings`/`closeSettings` Since 2026-10-31 the China ranking's read (`rankLoading`/`rankLoaded`/`rankFailed`, by the sort it was read for), the `china` tab, and an A share's candles kept by its `cn:` id. |

### 5.2 Wire contracts

The client speaks dsh 0.2's Typert Remote wire through `js/wire/api.js` (written against
0.2.0-rc.2; at 0.2.1-rc.5 the one change it reads is `session/projections`' kinded envelope,
below); 0.1.1's
apiproxy wire (`POST /api/<dotted.method>`, `POST /api/respond`, the downlink-only
`/api/events.mux`) was deleted upstream, and `call` refuses a dotted name before any fetch. Every
`/api` request and the mux upgrade carry the browser cookie (§4.4) with no code of the page's; a
401 is reported as `Not signed in — open the URL gravit-face printed`.

**Unary** — `call(endpoint, args)`: `POST /api/<ns>/<method>` with
`{type:"client-request", rpcId, method:"<ns>/<method>", payload:{args}}` — the method repeats the
path, the payload is exactly `{args}`, and `content-type: application/json` is load-bearing (the
host 415s anything else). The answer is `{type:"server-response", rpcId, result:{ok:true,
value?}}` or `{ok:false, error:{code, message, details}}`; `call` checks the echoed `rpcId`,
resolves the value, and rejects with the host's `code` (`session/not-found`,
`gateway/arguments-invalid`, …) or the HTTP `status`. Every wire parameter is sent
(`{_request:{}}`, `{request:{…}}`): an unknown top-level key is `gateway/arguments-invalid`. The
Remotes stage 1 calls: `session/list`; `session/create` (`{workspaceId}` for a channel, `{}` for
the host's default project directory — the repo root; `cwd` only for Talk to, below); `session/prompt`
(`mode:"queue"`, a client-minted `requestId` — a retry with the same id is admitted once — one
text part, and since the dsh UI port's plan 4 the draft's image and file parts after it (below), the
browser's `clientTimeZone`); `commands/execute` (a slash line, which 0.2.0's
prompt would hand to the model as text; `undefined` — no command claims the line — falls back to
a prompt); `session/cancel`; `session/rename`; `session/projections` and `session/page`, the two
non-activating reads (since the dsh UI port's plan 5 `session/page {request: {address: {kind:
'session', sessionId}, throughSeq, beforeSeq, maxMessages: 50}}` → `{records, hasMore}` also pages
a conversation's earlier history: `paginate` returns the contiguous slice ending at `min(throughSeq
+ 1, beforeSeq)`, so `beforeSeq` is exclusive, cut at a message group's earliest source; a follow's
window is paged against the snapshot's `cursor`, a paged one's against the cut's `asOfSeq`). Since 0.2.1 `session/projections` answers `{kind: "sequenced", asOfSeq,
values}` for a v4 log, `{kind: "migration-required", values}` with no `asOfSeq` for an older one, or
`null`; `readProjections` (`js/wire/summaries.js`) is the one reader (a kindless 0.2.0 answer reads
as sequenced), `js/host/live.js` opens a migration-required session on the status line `open:
session/migration-required` — where 0.2.0 showed the refused open — and skips its preview, and
`js/wire/member-traces.js` reports such a member's trace unavailable. Stage 2 adds no Remote: Markets and Account read the face's `/data` routes
(below) — the Venues tab's `credentials/describe` left with the graft's stage 1. Stage 3 adds
`session/fork` (`{request:{sessionId}}` → the child's `sessionId`; the host
refuses `session/fork-unavailable` for a session with no completed turn, which is why an empty
conversation offers no Fork); `session/create` with `{cwd: <the bot's homeCwd>, agentPreset:
<its id>}` for Talk to; `session/modelCatalog` (`{}`: its `default` selection on the Gravit item,
its groups as a bot's model routes); `credentials/describe` on the Gravit item, with
`{refs: ["DEEPSEEK_API_KEY"]}` (per ref `{configured,
source?, writable}`, never a value); and `subagents/interruptByParent`
(`{childSessionId, parentSessionId, mode:"continuable"}`, bare, as the old client sent it) for a
child's Stop. The list's pins add `workspace/pinSession` and `workspace/unpinSession` (`{request:{sessionId}}` → `{pinnedSessionIds}`, the whole set) and the stream `workspace/follow` (below); the face's `GET /data/search` is a `/data` read, not a Remote. The composer's menus (the dsh UI port's plan 3) add `commands/list` and `skills/list` (below), and its attachments (plan 4) `session/attachment` and the `uploadFileBinary` route (below). Not called: `subagents/prompt`, `workspace/rename`, `directoryPicker/pick`. The
surface stays closed by design: `session/selectModel`, `agentPresets/*` and `settings/describe`
are not called.

**Streams** — one WebSocket, `/api/remote.mux`, carries any number of logical streams keyed by a
client-chosen `streamId`: client frames `open` / `cancel`, host frames `item` / `end` / `error`,
exact keys. Four kinds ride it:
- `$events`, internal to `api.js`, one per socket generation and opened with exactly `{args:{}}`:
  `ready` first (the `clientId` every answer is bound to, and the host's `home`), then `emit`
  (host facts: `api-session/added|removed|status|activity|error`, `agent-preset/selected`),
  `waterfall` (an `approval/request` or a `user-questions/request` waiting on the operator:
  `{event, eventId, agentId, request}` — `agentId` is the session id; `request` carries the tool
  name, call id, `reason` and `displayReason`, or the questions) and `cancel` (that wait is over;
  it carries no outcome). Any other waterfall is handed straight back with `next`. Every pending
  gate is replayed, same `eventId`, right after each `ready`.
- `session/control`: a `baseline` of every attached session's projections, then `projection`
  frames — `tokenUsage`, `contextPressure`, `title`, the `room` unit's whole value,
  `subagentCatalog` and the rest. The live layer re-opens it 2 s after the host ends it, 10 s
  after an error (`live session state unavailable: <code>` on the status line meanwhile).
- `session/follow`: one session's transcript — a `snapshot` (`{header, cursor, records, hasMore,
  projections}`: `records` the tail window cut like a page at 50 messages, `DEFAULT_MAX_MESSAGES`,
  `cursor` its through seq and `hasMore` whether records lie before it; since the dsh UI port's plan
  5 the live layer keeps both as the conversation's `window`), then gap-free `event` records and,
  opened with `assistantStream: true`, `assistant-stream` frames whose `block-start` chunks are the
  pulses (0.2.0 logs no `assistant/chunk`). A follow item names no session; the live layer
  re-addresses it.
- `job/list {request: {sessionId}}` (plan 5): `{type: 'rows', jobs}` frames, each the whole set the
  session sees — its own jobs and every unowned one (`streamJobRows`) — as `JobView`s (`id`, `kind`,
  `label` (the command), `status` `running | stopping | completed | killed | failed`, `startedAt`,
  `finishedAt?`, `progress?`, `detail?`, `owner?`, `output: {total, earliest}`). Reading it never
  activates a session. `job/follow {request: {sessionId?, jobId, from?}}`: `opened {job, from}`,
  then `output {chunks: [{at, text, channel?, gapBefore?}], next, lossy?}` (`at` and `next` byte
  offsets) and `status {job}`; `sessionId` is the caller, omitted for a job with no `owner`.
  `job/kill {request: {sessionId, jobId}}` is a plain `call` answering `{outcome: 'requested' |
  'already-finished'}` (rc.5 answers a second kill of a settled job `already-finished`, not
  `job/not-found`). A job's end is its `detail`: `dsh-tool-bash` settles `completed` with `exit code:
  N`, or `killed` with `signal: X` or `killed before exit`, sandbox notes after `; `, and a human kill
  adds `cancelled by the user` (`JobController.kill`).
- `workspace/follow`, opened with `{}`: a `baseline` item whose `value.pinnedSessionIds` is the workspace's pinned set, then a `pinned` item carrying `pinnedSessionIds` per change. The set is host state, shared by every tab and window of the host.

**Reconnect** — there is no resume cursor. A socket close, a frame outside the stream grammar,
and an `$events` end, error or non-`ready` opening all lose the generation the same way: `onDown`
runs while only the lost socket exists (the live layer suspends the follow there — the view
drops to `page` with `stale` set — and the status line reads `Reconnecting… (<reason>)`), a fixed
1.5 s later a new socket re-opens every registered stream under fresh ids (`$events` first), and
`onReady` clears the line and re-reads the list, which `reconcile` reads to re-decide the open
conversation: followed again if live, re-paged if cold. A follow the host itself ends is
re-decided 2 s later the same way — never blindly re-followed.

**Answering a gate** — through the live layer's `answer` (§5.3), which calls `mux.answer(eventId,
value)`: it POSTs `$events/result`
`{clientId, eventId, outcome:{kind:"result", value}}` under the CURRENT generation's clientId: an
approval with the bare `"allowed-once"` or `"rejected"` (the host itself would take any value of
the approval vocabulary, so `api.js` is where `cancelled` and `unavailable` stay host-side), a
question with `{answers:[{id, selected, custom?}…]}`, the whole batch (`answersFrom` in `app.js`
reads the pressed card's inputs, matched by name; a batch with a question left blank is refused
on the status line, `Answer every question first`, before anything is sent). The host answers a settled or undelivered gate with a silent `ok`, so
`api.js` tracks the gates each generation was delivered and refuses: `not-ready` (no clientId
yet), `not-pending` (this connection does not hold the gate), `gate-gone` (withdrawn while the
answer was in flight), `bad-value`. A `cancel` that lands after this tab's answer resolved means
the answer lost a race — the host never cancels the winner — and is reported too (the last 64
answered ids per generation are remembered); the live layer turns that report into the card's
`Settled elsewhere`. A gate not replayed within 1 s of a reconnect's
`ready` was settled while the page was away: `api.js` retires it through `onGateGone`, and the
live layer owns no grace timer of its own.

**Room routes** — `/data/rooms/say` is called **before** `session/prompt` when the conversation
is in a channel and the composer's draft is bound for the room: it holds a bot chip, or its text,
each chip read as a space, carries `(^|\s)@` (`isMentionText`); a file or conversation chip's own
`@` never sends it there alone (`actions.send(text, {room})`; a bare call with no `room` reads
the text, as before). An answer of `addressed: []` means the text named nobody on the roster and
it goes out as an ordinary prompt instead. The server's `MENTION_RE` (`src/room-rules.ts`) ends a
name at a `.`, so a file chip `@news-scout.md` sent beside a bot chip also addresses a bot
`news-scout` on the roster (a residual, §7.4). `POST /data/rooms/state {sessionId}` (`{roster:
[{id, name, model?, broken?}], members, caps}`) is read by the `@` menu alone, for its roster; a
room's members on screen still come from the `room` projection and the list fold (§5.3), and a
member's gate is attributed through that fold.

**The composer's reads** (`js/host/composer.js`, the dsh UI port's plan 3) — `commands/list
{agentId: <sessionId>}` answers an array of `{definitionId?, name, description, input?: {hint,
attachments?}}`, `name` without the slash; it is called only for a conversation the store marks
`live`, because at dsh 0.2.1-rc.5 it resumes a cold one (the mounted `dsh-api-session-controller`
sets the gateway's agent lookup to find-or-resume; the spec's D13 expected `gateway/lookup-not-found`
there, and Task 9's smoke measured otherwise). `skills/list {request: {sessionId}}` answers
`{skills: [{path?, name, description, whenToUse?, modelInvocable}]}` and reads a cold session
without activating it. `GET /data/files?q=<encoded>&dir=<repo-relative>` (§4.4) answers `{ok,
items: [{path, kind: 'file' | 'directory'}], truncated}`; `dir` is the conversation's channel
folder relative to the root channel's, sent only when that folder is not the root. A command
chosen from the menu, or a sent `/` line, is `commands/execute {agentId, line,
submittedAttachments: []}` as before (a line sent with files carries their parts, below). **What a chip sends**: a bot chip `@<id>`; a file chip
`@<path>` (D15: relative to the conversation's channel folder when under it, `.` for the folder
itself, absolute otherwise or in no channel, `@"<path>"` when it holds whitespace), the root
channel's `dir` standing for the repository root (the same `process.cwd()` `src/main.ts` gives
`/data/files`); a conversation chip `@[<label>](dsh-session:<payload>)`, byte for byte
`formatSessionReferenceMention({sessionId, label: title})` of `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-reference`
— the payload `base64url(UTF-8 JSON.stringify(sessionId))` without padding, the label's `\` and
`]` escaped with a backslash — which the host's `session-reference` row turns into a
`Referenced sessions` message for the model (spec §5.5 wrote a bare id, which fails the row's
canonical check).

**Attachments** (the dsh UI port's plan 4; the parts built by `js/composer/files.js`, sent by
`js/host/actions.js`, read by `js/host/attachments.js`) — `session/prompt {request: {requestId,
sessionId, mode: 'queue', content, clientTimeZone}}`, `content` the text part when the words are not
blank (an attachment-only prompt is valid: `hasPromptContent` wants text or an attachment), then the
draft's attachments in its order: `{type: 'image', mediaType, data: <canonical base64>, name}` or
`{type: 'file', receiptId}` (`PromptContentPart`); a `/` line sent with files is `commands/execute
{agentId, line, submittedAttachments}` with the same two shapes (`CommandSubmitAttachment`). A file
that is not an image uploads first: `POST /api/session/uploadFileBinary?sessionId=<encoded>&name=<encoded>`
with `content-type: application/octet-stream` (415 otherwise) and the file's bytes as the body, same
origin under the owner's cookie (`wire/api.js` `uploadFile`, an `XMLHttpRequest` for its
`upload.onprogress`; it answers `{done, abort}`, `done` resolving `{receiptId, file}` and rejecting
`aborted` on an abort or a timeout, a non-200 with the 403 fence hint `call` gives). The host answers
HTTP 200 with `{ok: true, value: {receiptId, file: {attachmentId, name, bytes}}}` or `{ok: false,
error: {code, message, details}}`; the route resumes a cold session (the session controller
registers the upload service's agent resolver as find-or-resume, `registerAgentResolver`), so an
upload needs no follow. A receipt lives in memory on the session until the prompt that holds it is in
the history or the agent is disposed. **The two refusals** the page acts on are
`session/attachment-invalid` with `details.reason`: `FILE_NOT_STAGED` (`resolvePromptFileReceipts`:
a receipt the session no longer holds — the face restarted, the agent was disposed; D18) and
`MODEL_DOES_NOT_SUPPORT_IMAGES` (an image on a route whose model takes text only; D19); `call`
carries `details` on its error. A command's admission failure settles as `{kind: 'error', text}`
with no code, and the one it maps is the text `File upload receipt is unknown for this session.`
(`RECEIPT_UNKNOWN`, from rc.5's `dsh-commands` `admitCommandAttachments`). **The limits**:
`session/projections {request: {sessionId}}` → `values.imageLimits` (`maxImageBytes`,
`maxImagesPerMessage`, `maxMessageImageBytes`, `maxImagePixels`, `maxImageDimension`,
`mediaTypes`), the attachment store's deployment limits and the same for every session, read without
activating it; since plan 5 the same read's `values.turnOutline` (`[{turn, seq, prompt, response}]`,
strictly increasing by turn, `seq` the `turn/start`'s, `prompt` at most 50 and `response` at most
120 characters with a trailing `…` when cut, `response` `''` until `turn/end`; every started turn)
and `values.sessionStats` (`{turns, steps, llmMs, toolMs, ttftMs, ttftSteps, decodeMs,
decodeTokens}`, all 0 until their first event; `turns` counts turns with a closed step), which reach
`session/control` live as `{type: 'projection', sessionId, key, value, seq}`; `tokenUsage` is four
totals (`uncachedInputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `cacheReadTokens`, `cacheWriteTokens`). **The thumbs**: `session/attachment {request: {sessionId, attachmentId}}` →
`{attachment, data}` for an image the log references (base64 `data`, the whole stored image — no smaller thumbnail exists, up to `maxImageBytes`; files are never given back).
**History** stores `{type: 'image', attachment: {attachmentId, mediaType, bytes, width, height,
name?}, offloaded?}` and `{type: 'file', attachment: {attachmentId, name, bytes}}` in the operator's
`user/message`; the mapper keeps them, with `blocksText`, as the message's `attachments` (each field
only when well-typed, a block without an `attachmentId` dropped), and an attachment-only message is
a bubble with no words. What reaches the model for a file is never its bytes: the host saves a
read-only copy under `$DSH_HOME/attachments/v1/files/…` and gives the model one line naming it, its
size, its hash and the copy's path, which Gravit's `read` (UTF-8 text) or its shell reads.

**`/data` routes** — fence only, no cookie. Every list refresh reads `/data/channels.json` (the
channel index, `presets`, the host's `archived`), `/data/bots.json` (the bots' display names) and
`/data/sessions-meta.json` (the face's own `archived` and `deleted` ids) beside `session/list`;
a failed or malformed one keeps its last good answer — the groups never blank and nothing is
un-archived by a failure — and before any good answer the list still lands, with no channels, no
names and nothing archived (a bare `bootFace` mounts no `/data` route, as `gravit-client-smoke`
pins). The list is
re-polled at the trailing edge of a fixed 1.2 s window that its first trigger opens — the old
client's debounce re-armed on every trigger; through a sustained burst this one refreshes every
1.2 s rather than once at its end — and its triggers are the `$events` facts
`api-session/added|removed|status|activity` and `agent-preset/selected`, the followed
session's turn frames, and a control-stream `title` the list does not show yet.

**Markets and Account's `/data` reads** (since plan A2 on two upstreams: the market's public
reads through the market proxy, the Account's through the account proxy, §4.4; `fresh=1` is the
face's own flag, past the proxy's cache) — Markets: every explore is asked of both halves with one
query, `GET /data/market/explore?…` and `GET /data/account/connected/explore?…`, and joined in the
host (`host/explore-join.js` `joinExplore`, below): `?limit=200` (All, Watching, and All results
with no query) or `?tab=<kind>&limit=200` (a kind's tab) on showing and every 20 s while Markets is
on screen in a visible tab, a tab changed while shown read at once; `GET /data/account/venues` once,
on the first showing, whose verdicts the join reads; quotes every 5 s for the drawn rows' most
traded lines (twelve a call, none while one is out; on a market's page its own market's line),
split by the page's venues: a connected line's `GET /data/account/connected/quotes?pairs=…`, the
rest — the A shares — `GET /data/market/quotes?pairs=…`; the search `explore?q=<q>&limit=200` of
both halves once the box has been quiet for 300 ms; each old `us:`/`crypto:` star `explore?q=<its
symbol, a coin's base>&limit=12` of both halves once per boot, one at a time; a market's page
candles, book and trades keyed first: a public line's `GET /data/market/<read>?venue=&symbol=…`, a
connected line's `GET /data/account/connected/<read>?…`, and an Account that does not answer
falls back to the market at a public line of the same connector, else says `The Account is not
answering` — never another connection's line; and, for a coin, a perpetual or a stock, `GET
/data/account/compare?base=<base>&side=buy`. Account: `GET
/data/account` at boot, on entering Account, every 20 s while it is on screen in a visible tab
(80 s while the stream is open), on Refresh and right after a receipt, the seat's too
(those two `?fresh=1`); `holdings?cost=1` — and while the page, one the face recognises, names a
paper venue its paper lens `holdings?cost=1&paper=1` beside it — on entering Portfolio, on Refresh,
on a market's page, and when a page naming a paper venue lands with the lens never read or after a
page the face did not recognise (then `&fresh=1`);
`history?range=<1d|1w|1m|all>` (`&paper=1` when Paper leads) after the holdings on entering
Portfolio, after that page landing's holdings read and in a snapshot's re-read, and on a range —
not after Refresh's or a market page's holdings read;
`statement` on opening the drawer and on a market's page; `agents` on entering Agents. The stream:
one `EventSource` per tab at `/data/account/stream?client=face-<24 hex>` (`&since=<the last id>`
on a new source), open while the tab is visible, and `POST /data/account/stream/markets`
`{client, markets, n}` for a connected market a page follows; beside it the market's,
`/data/market/stream` and `POST /data/market/stream/markets` (`wire/market-stream.js`
`createMarketStream`), for a public market a page follows, the stream not in use told `follow([])`; an event reads again what it names, past the
cache — `order`, `fill`, `paper`, `balance`, `position` the holdings and the page, `statement` the
statement, `card` the page (and `/data/seat.json?fresh=1` for a card raised or answered),
`snapshot` everything; a `quote` frame is the followed market's price (the market stream's
`snapshot` and `quote` land as `streamSnapshot` and `streamQuote`). The A shares use no wire of
their own: `explore?tab=china&sort=`, `explore?q=`, `quotes?pairs=china|<code>` and
`candles?venue=china` are the market's reads through the market proxy alone (`wire/china.js`
shapes the answers), polled with the rest — China has no push channel.

**Account › Identity's wire** (plan B1b, over the five routes plan B1a proxied, §4.4 and §3.9
"Identity") — `GET /data/account/identity` on entering the tab, at the Account page's beat while
`#/account/identity` is on screen in a visible tab (20 s, 80 s while the stream is open), and
`?fresh=1` on Refresh, on Retry and right after a done sheet of an Identity kind (`connectNetwork`,
`disconnectNetwork`, `routing`, `block`; app.js `IDENTITY_SHEET_KINDS`): the proxy's 2 s read cache is
not cleared by a write, so a read straight after one asks past it (ruling carried from B1a). The
Connect drawer: sheet 1's Next is one `POST /data/account/identity/telegram/token` `{token, keyHash,
salt}` through the owner's `postVia` (`{status, body}`, nothing logged) — the token read from the
`#identity-token` field and the field cleared before anything is dispatched, the body forwarded by
the proxy unparsed and unlogged; its answer is the pending view `{ok, pending: {id, network, bot,
link, qr, expiresAt, state}}`. Sheet 2 reads `GET /data/account/identity/pending?id=<id>&fresh=1`
every 1.5 s (`PENDING_POLL_MS`; always fresh, since the 1 s cache would hide a heard sender for a
beat): `waiting`; `conflict` (another reader of the bot, said, still waiting); `heard`, whose
`sender` carries `{id, name, handle, masked, text}` — the numeric `id` since plan B1b, which sheet 4
signs as `operatorId` and the page draws only masked (ruling of B1b Task 2); `expired`, or 404 —
and the page ends it itself when `expiresAt` has passed, or, when `expiresAt` cannot be read, 10
minutes after sheet 2 began (`PENDING_WAIT_MS`); a read with no answer sets `silent` and reads again.
Sheet 3's Not me is `POST …/identity/pending/not-me {id}` (its answer the pending view, waiting
again); closing the drawer, Back from sheet 2, Start again and sheet 4's Cancel are `POST
…/identity/pending/drop {id}`, fire and forget. Sheet 4 and the other three sheets are the owner
sheet's ordinary prepare → What you sign → exchange (§5.3), the account's owner types
`connectNetwork {network, pending, botId, speaksAs, operatorId, talksOnlyWith, routing, keyHash, salt}`,
`disconnectNetwork {network}`, `setRouting {routing, quietFrom, quietTo}` (both `""` for Off) and
`blockSender {network, sender, masked}`. A generation counter in `host/identity.js` drops every
answer that lands for a drawer since closed or moved on. Slack's Install app… (plan B2) is the same
drawer over the same routes but its sheet 1: Next is one `POST /data/account/identity/slack/token`
`{appToken, botToken, keyHash, salt}` — both read from `#identity-app-token` and `#identity-bot-token`
and both fields cleared before anything is dispatched, `keyHash` over salt then `appToken`, a NUL and
`botToken` — whose answer is the same pending view with `workspace`; sheet 2's link is Slack's
`app_redirect` (`https://slack.com/app_redirect?app=…&team=…`), and `heard`'s `sender` carries the
full Slack `userId` beside `{id, name, handle, masked, text}`; sheet 4 signs `connectNetwork` with
`network: "slack"`, `botId` and `operatorId` as `<team>:<user>`. The manifest sheet 1 shows is the
identity read's `slackManifest`; no route of its own.

**Stage 3's `/data` reads and writes** — a channel's page: `POST /data/channels/overview
