`overflow` says whether more than twenty were cut, so exactly twenty is not more (`moreThanTwenty` joins it with the
wire's `hasMore`). A title match's preview line is `search-view.js`'s own (`conv.preview`, else the last spoken
message's text, with no sender prefix), kept there so a host view imports no render code. `highlightRuns(snippet,
match)` splits a snippet into `{text, mark}` runs, one unmarked run for a missing or out-of-range match;
`searchPhase` is `idle`, `searching`, `results`, `empty` or `failed`, and a failed content read keeps the title matches.

**Stage 3's views** (pure). `groupsOf(state)` (`js/host/list-view.js`) orders grouping.js's
buckets: every channel a group, an empty one too (a new channel's page is reachable from the
list), the root first, then — since P4 — `Desk`, every `gravit-desk` conversation wherever it
ran (`isDeskPreset`, so a strategy's report never lands among its research), then each group by its
newest conversation, the empty channels by name; a bot's home sessions under the bot (`bot:<id>`),
the rest under `No channel`; `Archived` last. Each
group is `{key, label, kind, workspaceId, isRoot, conversations, collapsed, shown}`: a channel goes
by `channelLabel` (its display title, else its name — the label New message's Where and Details
use too), `collapsed` is the viewer's `collapsed[key]`, else true for Archived alone, and a
collapsed group shows only the conversation on screen. Within a group the rows the host's pin set names (`state.pinned`) lead, newest first, then the rest, also explicitly newest first; the records handed back are copies carrying `pinned`, an archived row is never pinned, and a pinned id the list does not hold matches nothing. `itemsOf(discover)` (`discover-view.js`)
turns the listings into cards under namespaced ids — `mcp:<server>` with its tool count on Data,
`bot:<id>` on Bots (never the default composition), `agent:gravit` first then the connected and
the found CLI agents (`agent:<bin>`, `Connected`, `Not found`, `Found · <version>`) on Agents,
`skill:<name>` with its group on Skills, `module:<name>` for the six Lunhui modules on Research
(`researchItems`, always six, the listing filling their chips); `searchItems` matches name and line, `itemById` finds an
item for its page. `childrenOf(conv, childRows)` (`children-view.js`) composes the parent's
`subagentCatalog` with the child rows (`composeSubagentCatalog` → `normalizeSubagentCatalog` →
`subagentControls`): `{children: [{id, label, mode, state, canStop}], unavailable}` — a malformed
catalog is unavailable, never an empty list; an unknown-mode entry is `unavailable` and never
stoppable; `canStop` is a running continuable child.

**Composed answers' views** (`js/host/lunhui.js`; plan 2 of the run view). A composed message
names its run and the view modules it reads (`viewOf`: `{key, strategy, run, modules}`, the key
`<strategy>/<run>/<modules joined by commas>`). At the end of every render the app asks
`wantedViews(state)` — the open conversation's composed answers, on Messages only, whose key has no
entry, each key once — and, when there are any, `ensureViews(store, getJson)` reads each through
`GET /data/lunhui/view` (`viewPath`; an empty module list asks `modules=`, which the route reads as
none, §4.4): `lunhuiViewLoading` at once, then `lunhuiViewLoaded` with the answer's `view`, or
`lunhuiViewFailed` with words (`HTTP <status>` when the face answered, else the error's message,
`the answer held no view` for a 200 with none). Each key is checked again before its dispatch, so
a render between two loads asks nothing twice. **Retry** (`lunhuiRetry`) deletes the key's entry
and the next render asks again. A tile, tab, bucket, index or rung pick is `lunhuiUi` by the
answer's id (`rung` and `bucket` as numbers). The minute cursor's functions (`minuteAt`,
`applyCursor`, `runView`, `cursorFor`, `reapplyCursors`) live here too and touch no store (§5.4);
`runView` finds any loaded view of the run, since the indices do not depend on the modules asked.

### 5.4 Rendering

`boot(win, host)` builds the store (`makeStore`: the prefs, never a saved state), starts the live
layer and the actions, sets the markdown hook (`setMarkdown` in `render/markdown.js`, re-exported by `render/thread.js` — the DOM-built
`gravitMarkdown` — `renderMarkdown(text).node.outerHTML`; tests hand in a stub or none, and with none set Gravit's text is
escaped), makes the tab's Account stream (`createAccountStream` over `win.EventSource`,
`win.fetch`, the app's timers and `win.crypto`; opened at boot while the tab is visible, closed
while it is hidden), starts `startAccount` (and reads the page at once) and `startSeat`, then
`startMarkets` (the Account's reads on the app's timers, the stream, the wire's quote and search
factories over `win.fetch` and `win.EventSource` for the A shares, the browser's storage),
`startChannels`, `startDiscover`, `startModules` and `startTraces`, and renders on every store change. Since the
graft's stage 2 it starts the owner device first (`startOwner` over `win.crypto.subtle`,
`indexedDbKeys(win.indexedDB)` — `memoryKeys()` where there is none — `signedOutFlag(storage)` and
`postVia(win.fetch)`; `startAccount`'s `onPage` hands every page to `owner.standing`, so the first
page pairs it once), then `startSheet` (its `afterAction` reads the page, the holdings and the
statement past the cache, the seat too after `letIn`, `limit`, `endLimit` or `revoke`, and closes a
done sheet but the order's; its `onChange` runs a connect sheet's key-file and reach checks after
the sheet's 300 ms quiet, each only when what it asks changed), hands `startMarkets` the owner and
`afterAction`, and starts `startTrade` over the sheet and the stream; a stream event reaches the
trade host too. One render is one string — `renderRail(state)` + the screen
(`renderMessagesScreen`, `renderChannelScreen`, `renderMarketsScreen`, `renderTradeScreen`,
`renderDiscover`, `renderPlugin`, `renderModule` or `renderAccountScreen`) (+ `renderSettings` when the drawer is
open, + `renderSheet` while a sheet other than the ticket's is open, + `renderRunSheet` while a
module card's Run sheet is) — written to
`#app.innerHTML`; the loop first records and then restores what the person had: focus and caret
(by element id, else the control's data attributes), the typed value of every input with an id
(an editor's box only while the same editor stays open; New message's Where select never — its
channel is the store's), the ticked radios and checkboxes with an id (a question card's picks, the
person's own until they press Answer), every `<details>` with an id the person had open (a
Trace, What you sign — open again by id), the composer's draft (its words, chips and caret or
selection, §5.5: written back into the editor by `editor.write` after the page's write, the caret
where it stood while the same draft stays on screen, at the end when another draft takes its
place), the scroll of the rows, the main pane on the same screen, a
drawer body while it is the same drawer, and the thread's position while the person reads up,
however much arrives (at the bottom, or on another conversation, the thread follows the tail).
After a Markets render the ids of the rows drawn go to `markets.rowsInView` — on a market's page,
which draws none, the page's own key — so the quotes poll asks for what is on screen. While an IME composes (pinyin), renders
are held until `compositionend`; while a primary press is down they are held too — at most
`POINTER_HOLD_MS` (1 s), a `pointercancel` or a blur ends it — so a quote tick (the page renders on
each, about twice a second while a coin streams) cannot replace the element a click is aimed at,
and the held render lands after the click. Clicks are delegated by `data-action` (`open`, `startDraft`,
`cancelDraft`, `toggleRail`, `toggleGroup`, `changeWords`/`commitEdit`/`cancelEdit`,
`stopGravit`/`confirmYes`/`cancelConfirm`, `suggest`, `answer`, `answerQuestion`,
`toggleDetails`, `openSettings`/`closeSettings`, `setTheme`, the composer menu's `menuPick`, the attachments' `attachFiles`, `attachRemove`, `attachRetry`, `openImage`, `lightboxClose` and `lightboxKeep`; the thread's (the dsh UI port's plan 5) `toggleSecret`, `earlier`, `jumpTurn`, `openUsage`, `openJobs`, `openJob`, `stopJob`, `clearJobs` and `copyText`; the row actions `fork`, `archive`,
`unarchive`, `deleteConv`; the research surfaces' `stopChild` and `openTrace`; a channel page's
`newRound`, `channelRetry`, `editRoster`; Discover's `shelfRetry`, `connectAgent`,
`disconnectAgent`, `rescanAgents`, `talkTo`, `editBot`; Markets' `mkTab`, `mkSort`, `mkClear`,
`toggleWatch` (on or off as the star is drawn, `watchedOf`), `removeAsked`, `openMarket`,
`setRange`, `handToGravit`; Account's `refreshAccount` (the page and the seat past the cache, the
holdings), `setHistoryRange`, `openVenueDetails`/`closeVenueDetails`,
`openStatement`/`closeStatement`, `exportStatement`; the owner device's `pairDevice` (the code in
`#pair-code`, on Pair or on the pair form's submit — Enter in the box — held while a pairing is in the
air), `signIn`, `signOut` and `letDevice` (each a sheet but Sign in), `openSheet` (an
owner key's sheet, its seed built from the store by `data-kind` and the key's data — the connect
and paper sheets once their read lands), `askRevoke`/`askDisconnect` (asked in place, then their
sheet on `confirmYes`), `grant` (`grantOf`'s sheet), the sheet's `sheetField`, `sheetSubmit`,
`sheetAgain`, `sheetClose`; Trade's `tradeKind`, `pickMarket`, `openTicket` (a market page's Buy or
Sell: `#/trade/<id>` with the ticket on that side), `ticketVenue`, `ticketSide`, `ticketOutcome`,
`closeTicket`, `toggleSigns`, `cancelOrder` — every owner key acting only while the page signs); a
disclosure's own key (Trace's `<summary>`)
toggles its `<details>` itself and cancels the browser's toggle — the action's first dispatch
re-renders inside the click, so the browser would toggle the element the render replaced — and
its action runs on opening only; typing in `#mq` (`mkQuery`) sets the query at once
and searches once the box has been quiet for `SEARCH_QUIET_MS` (300 ms; a blank box at once), in
`#dq` (`dq`) Discover's query; choosing `New channel…` in Where opens its name
box, any other channel is `setDraftWhere`; a roster box's change is `toggleRosterTick`; a sheet's
or the ticket's field (`sheetField`, `ticketField`) changes the sheet (a box by `checked`, a pick's
boxes as the values ticked), and the ticket's venue or outcome re-seeds it at the new line; typing
in `#tq` (`tradeQuery`) searches Trade after the same quiet; the composer's `submit` is `send`, a
bot editor's `saveBot`, the Create page's `createBot`, the ticket's `placeOrder` the sheet's
submit; a Run sheet's box as typed (Stocks, the Note) and its pick as changed (Where, On, Cites)
are `runSheetField`; typing in `#cq` (`convQuery`) is `startSearch`'s `type` (§5.3); the row actions `pin` and `unpin` are the pin key's and Details'; ⌥⌘K (Ctrl+Alt+K off a Mac, matched on the key's place `KeyK`, not its character) focuses the list's box, going to Messages first from a screen with no list; Escape in the box clears the query, and again leaves the box, before the chain below, and both keys wait out an IME composition; an open composer menu takes Escape before the search box and the chain (D34), and since plan 4 the lightbox next, after the menu and before the search box, and since plan 6 the shortcut sheet after the lightbox and before the search box (D34's last slot); since plan 6 the keydown asks `keys.js` `chordOf` first, so ⌥⌘K, ⌥⌘N (`startDraft`), ⌥⌘, (`openSettings`) and ⌘/ (the shortcut sheet, opened and closed again; Ctrl+Alt+N, Ctrl+Alt+, and Ctrl+/ off a Mac) work from any focus, the editor and every input included, each `preventDefault`ed, none inside an IME composition, and none does anything while the lightbox or an owner sheet stands (What you sign is never navigated away by a key, the controller's ruling: ⌥⌘K too, which plan 2 let focus the box under one); a General key other than ⌘/ closes the shortcut sheet first, while ordinary typing leaves it open (it has a search box); the rail's ticks take ↑ ↓ Home End with no modifier (`stepRail`, matched on `ev.key` as the menu's arrows are, after the menu's keys and before the Escape chain), so a chord never reaches them; Escape cancels an editor, a confirm, or closes a module card's Run sheet
first, then the owner sheet, then a drawer (Details, Settings, the Statement, a venue's Details),
then Trade's ticket; Enter commits an inline editor.

**Routes** — `#/messages/<sessionId>`, `#/messages/new`; `#/markets` and `#/markets/<id>` with
an Account key (`coin:BTC`, `stock:NVDA`, `event:<venue>:<market>`, kept whole) or a face id
(`cn:600519`, canonicalised; an old `us:AAPL` or `crypto:BTC/USD` too) — the id is everything
after `#/markets/`, so a coin keeps its slash; a percent-encoded link is decoded; one that is
neither opens Markets; `#/channel/<workspaceId>`; `#/discover`, `#/discover/<shelf>` (`data`,
`bots`, `agents`, `skills`), `#/discover/create`; `#/plugin/<id>` (a channel's and a plugin's id
are read like a market's: everything after the screen, decoded); `#/account/portfolio`,
`#/account/venues`, `#/account/agents`, `#/account/cards` (an unknown tab is Portfolio);
`#/trade` and `#/trade/<id>` (since the graft's stage 2: Trade, `<id>` an Account key read like a
market's, whose ticket opens on entering — a buy, or the side a market page's Buy or Sell asked
for; a market the ticket does not trade opens none). `routeOf` folds every other route to
Messages (`#/mail` included), and `settle` rewrites the address bar when it normalised one.
Leaving Trade closes its ticket and lets its line go before a market's page follows its own;
Trade's picks are read only on Trade in a visible tab (`trade.show`). `hashchange` →
`follow()`: the conversation the route names is handed to `live.open` once; a deep link the list
has not answered yet waits for the `hostList` that carries it, and with no conversation on screen
the list's first open conversation (`firstOpen`) is opened; when the last open conversation was
deleted and nothing took its place, `live.leave()`; Markets' reads and the A shares' wire run only
on Markets in a visible tab (`markets.show`), and the Account's read is polled only on Account in
a visible tab (`account.poll`); entering Account reads the page (past the cache when it opens on
Cards), and each tab what it draws on entering it — Portfolio the holdings and then the curve,
Money the earn read, Venues the seat, Agents the agents and the seat, Cards the page past the cache
(Rules draws the page alone); a market's page
(an Account key) is handed to `markets.page` and reads the holdings and the statement, and leaving
it hands `null`; `visibilitychange` re-decides both screens and closes the Account stream while the
tab is hidden, opening it again when the tab returns; entering a channel's page reads its overview
once; entering Discover from outside it (a shelf or an item's page included) reads the four
listings; an item's page reads its own cards on opening (the Gravit item's three reads, a skill's
content), the Create page the model routes.

**The rail** (`render/rail.js`) — the first level: the brand, Messages (its badge counts the
conversations with a card waiting on you; current on a channel's page too), Markets (`#/markets`,
current on Markets and a market's page), Trade (`#/trade`), Discover (`#/discover`, current on Discover and an item's
page), Settings at the foot, Account (`#/account/portfolio`, current on Account, with the
Account's leading figure under it once its page has answered — `· Paper` when Paper leads — and a
badge counting the cards waiting there); it collapses to a strip of icons. The second level, on
Messages and beside a channel's page: the new-message key, the search box `#cq` (`Search conversations`, the key's hint `⌥⌘K` or `Ctrl+Alt+K` by the platform the browser reports), then the groups (`groupsOf`, §5.3) —
each a head (its fold key, `Collapse <label>` / `Expand <label>`; a channel's name a link to its
page, marked while that page is open) and its rows, pinned first and newest first within each part, a pinned row carrying a filled pin glyph (`.row-pin`) and every non-archived row a pin key (`.pin-key`, a sibling button in a `.row-wrap`, hidden until the row is hovered or a key inside it has focus, so Tab reaches it; a touch screen has no reveal — Details has Pin) — the unread dot (`unreadOf`),
the avatar by kind (a bot's letter, a cluster for a group), the title, `rowTime`, the preview (the
host's one-message page; until it lands, the last message drawn). A folded group shows only the
conversation on screen; Archived is last and folded until opened. While the box holds a query (anything but blanks) the groups give way to `.conv-results`: `N conversations`, then a `.conv-hit` per result — title, `rowTime`, a grey `Archived` chip when archived, the channel in bold and the snippet with its match in `<mark>` — and, after an archived-by-the-face hit, an `Un-archive` key; the states are `Searching every conversation…` with three skeleton bars, `No matching conversations`, `Could not search inside conversations` (under title matches when there are any), and `Showing the first 20. Narrow your search.` when the answer was cut or the wire said `hasMore`.

**The screen** (`render/messages.js`) — the head (the title; a centred cluster, the member
names and count for a group; `Working` while `running`; the Details key), the thread, the
composer (`Tell Gravit…`, `… @ a bot by name` in a group) and the status line (`role="status"`,
`.bad` red). **Details** carries This task (the title with `Change words` → an inline editor →
`session/rename`; Created from the snapshot header; Where — the channel by its title, or `Default
directory`; Agent — Gravit or the bot; `Archived · By the host` for the host's own archive) and
its row keys — `Change words`; `Fork` once there is something to fork (dsh forks from a completed
turn); `Pin` or `Unpin` (absent on an archived row); `Archive`, or `Un-archive` for the face's own archive; `Delete`, asked twice (`Yes,
delete`) — Archive and Delete absent while Gravit runs or a card waits; Members for a group;
**Children** when the conversation's catalog names any (`childrenOf`: the label, `One-shot` or
`Continuable`, `Running` / `Not running` / `Unknown` / `Unavailable`, and `Stop` — asked twice,
`Yes, stop` — on a running continuable child; `Children unavailable` for a malformed catalog;
since dsh 0.2.1 every local child is continuable — a running role child included, whose Stop
ends the role call as an error, §3.8 — and a catalog entry of mode `external` is the `unsupported`
diagnostic until an external backend is mounted);
Usage from the projections (Tokens in = uncached input + cache reads, Tokens out, Context as a
percentage) and `Stop Gravit` while running, a two-step confirm. **New message** is a title
(`Name this (or your first line is the name)`), Where — a select of the channels by their titles,
the root first, then `New channel…`, which opens a name box under it (a refusal stays in the box;
the new channel is selected once it exists) — and the composer; the first words create, name and
prompt, then the new conversation is opened and promoted to a follow. The **empty
state** (no conversations) offers three suggestion chips that fill the composer (`putWords`:
after what the draft holds, on a new line, the caret at the end; Hand to Gravit the same).

**The composer** (the dsh UI port's plan 3; `js/composer/`, `renderComposer` in
`render/messages.js`) is `form.composer`: `div#composer-menu.composer-menu` (the menu's slot),
then `.composer-box` with `#say`, a `contenteditable` `div.composer-input` (`role="textbox"`,
`aria-multiline`, labelled by the hidden `Tell Gravit`, `aria-controls="composer-menu"`,
`aria-expanded` and `aria-activedescendant` from `menuAria`, the placeholder `Tell Gravit…` or
`Tell Gravit… @ a bot by name` as `data-placeholder`, drawn by `:empty::before`), and Send. Its
markup is `editorHtml(runs)`: text escaped (newlines kept under `pre-wrap`; a draft ending in a
newline gains the browser's trailing `<br>`), a chip a `span.ref-chip` with `contenteditable=false`
and its JSON in `data-chip` (through `attrs`), a chip that ends the draft followed by a zero-width
space so the caret has a place after it. `makeEditor` reads it back: one walk over the nodes,
zero-width spaces dropped, a chip whose `data-chip` does not parse to one of the three kinds
dropped, a `BR` a newline, a `DIV` or `P` a new line as the browser shows it (a `BR` that ends a
block, or the editor, counts nothing), and `caret`, `selection` and `place` count the same units.
**Keys**: Enter sends (`sendNow`), except while a menu shows rows (it chooses), while an IME
composes (`isComposing`, `keyCode` 229 or the page's own composition flag) and with Shift held (the
browser's newline); a paste of words is `text/plain` alone, CR and CRLF made LF, put over the selection
(`replaceRange`), without a render (a paste with files, below). **The menus** (`app.js`: `menuTick`, `buildMenu`, `drawMenu`,
`chooseItem`) follow the token before the caret after every input and every caret key: `/` at a
word's start (after punctuation too) on a conversation only (D10), `@` anywhere; a chip ends a
token as a space does. Opening, filtering and moving write `#composer-menu` alone and set
`#say`'s two aria attributes; nothing renders the page. The `/` menu is `Commands` (each its name
capitalized, `/name` and its line; `plan`, `permission` and `feedback` hidden; a command that
takes arguments only at the draft's start) and `Skills`; the `@` menu is `Bots in this room` (a
channel conversation's roster, each with its glyph, `@id` and line), `Files and folders` (only
while the root channel is known; a query holding `/` walks that folder, its path as a crumb) and
`Conversations` (the open ones but this, its channel's first, newest first, eight at most, with
their age); a query filters by letters in order, prefixes first (the `/` menu then draws no group heads). The
footer reads `↑↓ Move · Enter Choose · Esc Close`. ↑ and ↓ move, wrapping; Enter or Tab chooses;
Tab on a folder opens it in place (`@<path>/`); Esc or Shift+Tab closes and keeps the draft, and
the token Esc closed stays closed until it changes; a pointer press in the menu keeps the focus in
the editor, and the editor losing focus anywhere else closes it. Commands, skills and the roster
are read once per trigger (its kind, place and draft), files once per query; an answer draws only
while its trigger stands (`menuSeq`, `menuSource`), so a late answer after the query moved on or
after Esc draws nothing. **A choice**: a skill or an argument command becomes `/name ` in the
draft; a command with no arguments leaves the draft and runs at once (`actions.runCommand`); a
bot, file or conversation becomes its chip and a space. **Sending**: a draft with a bot chip, or
whose text (each chip a space) carries an `@`, is bound for the room in a channel conversation;
one of those that also holds a conversation chip is refused before sending, `Conversations go to
Gravit, not to a room's bots`, and kept (O9). Otherwise it is serialized (§5.2), trimmed and
cleared, and a failed send puts it back under its own conversation, words typed meanwhile kept
after it on a new line. **The bubble**: the operator's sent text runs through `sessionRefRuns`, so
a well-formed conversation mention draws as a `.ref-chip` (the `chat` icon and the label, not
editable); a file or bot reference stays as typed.

**Attachments** (the dsh UI port's plan 4; `js/composer/files.js`, `js/host/attachments.js`, the
draft's files in `app.js`). Inside `.composer-box` the rail `#composer-files` leads (hidden while
empty), then `.composer-row`, which never wraps: the paperclip (`aria-label="Attach files"`,
`attachFiles`, which clicks the hidden `#attach-input`, a multiple file input), the editor, Send.
Above the box, between the menu's slot and it, `#composer-note` (`role="status"`, hidden empty), the
line of a refusal of the files added: the pre-checks (`Up to <n> images a message`, `<name> is over
<m> MB`, `Images in one message: up to <t> MB`) or the model line (`Gravit's model takes no images.
Remove the image, or run Gravit on a model that does.`, a bot's own conversation naming the bot for
both). The node is kept across renders and only its text written, so a screen reader announces a
change once. **The rail** draws each file in the draft's order: an image whose object URL passes
`isImageSrc` as a 64 px square, any other file as `fileCard` — the file icon, the name and `<EXT> ·
<size>` (`CSV · 2.8 MB`, `FILE` with no extension; under 1,024 bytes `<n> B`, under 1 MiB `<n>
KB`, else `<n.n> MB`), while it uploads `<loaded> / <total> MB` in the total's unit, a failed one
in the down colours with `Upload failed · ` and a `Retry` key (`attachRetry`) — each with its remove
key (`aria-label="Remove <name>"`, `attachRemove`, shown on hover or focus, always under `hover:
none`). **Adding**: the picker's `change`, a paste whose clipboard holds files and is not a rich copy
(a non-empty `text/plain` with `text/html` is one: its text is pasted, nothing attached), and a drop
(`pointAt` puts dropped text where the pointer is; a `data:` or `blob:` URL dropped as text inserts
nothing) each call `addFiles`: `admit` against `attachments.limits()` (an image is a file whose type
the limits' `mediaTypes` hold; any other, an SVG or a HEIC included, is a file), an image given its
object URL, the first refusal as the note; on a conversation each non-image file uploads at once to
that conversation's session (`startUpload`; New message's wait as `ready` until the conversation is
made). A progress tick writes `#composer-files` alone (`drawFiles`, and only while that draft is on
screen); adding, removing, a finished or failed upload and a refusal render the page. An upload's
ticks and its landing go to the draft it belongs to whatever is on screen; Retry, or a second start,
aborts the one in flight first; a removal aborts it and revokes the image's URL; a failure keeps its
reason (`error`) and says it on the status line. **The drop overlay**: while a drag carrying Files is
over Messages, `.drop-overlay` covers the page (`Drop files or images here`, then `Images: up to
<n> a message, <m> MB each` from the limits), kept up by each `dragover` and gone `DROP_QUIET_MS`
(300) after the last, or at the drop or `dragend`; a drop carrying files is prevented anywhere (a
screen with no composer adds nothing), one carrying text only where it lands in `#say`; a drag that
starts inside the editor is cancelled, so the browser never moves or copies a chip. **Sending**
(`sendNow`, in order): a bot chip with files is refused, `Files go to Gravit, not to a room's bots`
(D20; a typed `@word` beside files is a prompt to Gravit); a `file` still `ready` on a conversation
starts uploading; an upload in flight holds the send (`Files are still uploading`), a failed one too
(`A file did not upload. Retry it or remove it.`); a conversation in `refusesImages` with an image
draws the model line and calls nothing (D19); a `/` line with files whose kept command row does not
take attachments is refused, `/<name> takes no files` (D12). Then the draft clears and renders
before anything is awaited (a second Enter finds it blank), the images are read
(`blob.arrayBuffer()`, `encodeBase64`; a failed read puts the draft back with `send: <name> could
not be read`), and the parts go with the words (`contentParts`). On success the sent images' URLs
are revoked and the note cleared; a failure puts the whole draft back under its key, words and files
added meanwhile after it. `MODEL_DOES_NOT_SUPPORT_IMAGES` adds the conversation to `refusesImages`
and draws the model line; `FILE_NOT_STAGED` or a command's `ATTACHMENT_NOT_FOUND`, the first time,
uploads every `up` file again and sends once more (`restage`; off screen it says `Files uploaded
again; the message was not sent`), a second time or after a failed re-upload says `send:
session/attachment-invalid (<reason>)` and keeps the draft (D18); any other reason says the same line.
New message moves the draft (and its note) to the conversation as `session/create` answers, uploads
its files there, then prompts; refused or unrenamed, the page opens that conversation with the whole
draft and the line. **The lightbox**: `openImage` on a thumb that passes `isImageSrc` (a loading
frame or a card opens nothing) sets `lightbox`; while it stands on Messages the page appends
`.lightbox` (`role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`, `aria-label="Image"`, the image at most 92 vw by 88 vh,
its close key `aria-label="Close"`); a click on the backdrop or the close key closes it
(`lightboxClose`), a click on the image does not (`lightboxKeep`). Its close key takes focus on
opening and keeps it across renders, Tab and Shift+Tab stay on it, ⌥⌘K does nothing under it, and
on closing focus returns to the image it opened from (else the overlay's close key, else the
editor); leaving the conversation (`nav`, `closeOverlays`) closes it. **Settings**
(`renderSettings(state, {mac})`, a drawer on every screen) is, in order (the plan's call; plan 7
puts Language first): Theme (Cream · Black · System, a seg whose values are the stored codes
`cream`, `black`, `system` and whose labels are the table's); **Text size**, a `div.stepper`
(`role="group"`, `aria-label="Text size"`): `−` (`aria-label="Smaller text"`), `output#pref-textSize`
`15 px`, `+` (`Larger text`), each key `data-action="stepPref"` with its step, `aria-disabled="true"` at
its range's end (still focusable, so focus stays on it; `stepPref` does nothing on it); **More font settings**, a `details#more-fonts.fold` the page keeps open across renders,
holding Text font (`placeholder="Default: Manrope, Noto Sans SC"`), Code font (`Default: IBM Plex
Mono`) — inputs `data-action="setFont"`, each keystroke dispatched as typed (`typeFont`; the reducer
cleans it and the box is left alone, so a space can be typed — while a turn streams each render
writes the box back by script and its blur fires no `change`), and on `change` the cleaned family
written back into the box before the render so what was kept is what shows — and Code size's stepper (`Smaller code`,
`Larger code`); **Keyboard shortcuts**, `button#show-shortcuts.btn-sm` `Show all`
(`data-action="openShortcuts"`) beside `kbd.sc-key` `⌘/` (`Ctrl+/` off a Mac); then Devices (below).
`stepPref`, `typeFont` and `setFont` dispatch `setPref`, and `applyPrefs` sets the root's custom properties at
boot (beside `applyTheme`) and after each change.

**The shortcut sheet** (`render/shortcuts.js`, plan 6) is drawn after the drawers, outside
`<main>`, before the drop overlay and the lightbox: `div.scrim` (`data-action="closeShortcuts"`)
and `section.shortcuts` (`role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`, `aria-labelledby="sc-title"`; fixed and
centred, `min(440px, 100% - 32px)` wide, z 51 — above a drawer's 30, under the drop overlay's 60
and the lightbox's 70): `h2#sc-title` `Keyboard shortcuts` with its close key `#sc-close.close-key`
(`aria-label="Close"`), the box `input#sc-q` (`type="search"`, `placeholder` and `aria-label`
`Search shortcuts`, `data-action="scQuery"` → `setShortcutsQuery`, its value and caret kept across
renders by the typed map), then General and Composer as `h3.sc-section` over `ul.sc-rows` of
`li.sc-row` — `.sc-what` (`shortcutWords`) and `kbd.sc-key` (`chordLabel` by the platform) — only
rows marked `bound`; a query (trimmed, any case) keeps the rows whose words or chord hold it, a
section it empties draws no heading, and none left reads `No shortcut matches`; last `p.sc-note`
`⌘ is Ctrl off a Mac. Keys follow dsh's web bindings.` It lists keys and rebinds nothing (P7);
leaving the screen (`nav`) or an opener's `closeOverlays` closes it, as it does the lightbox.
Focus: on opening `#sc-q` takes it and `scFrom` records the opener (Show all's key, recorded by its
action as `openImage` does for Safari; for ⌘/ what had focus); while it stands focus stays on the
box or the close key, Tab and Shift+Tab alternating them; on closing, with the same drawer under
it, focus returns to the opener; the lightbox over it gives focus back inside the sheet. It is
tracked beside the drawers (`last.shortcuts`), so a drawer under it — Settings, when Show all
opened it — keeps its opener: Esc closes the sheet, focus goes back to Show all, and a second Esc
closes Settings.

**The words** (plan 6, spec §5.10). Every word the face writes goes through `js/i18n/words.js`
with a literal key, in the escaping the literal had: inside `esc(…)` or an `attrs` value it is
`t(…)` there; raw template text is `${th(…)}`, which inserts the table's value verbatim and
escapes each param (so `Can't run · ${esc(reason)}` still draws `Can't`, never `Can&#39;t`, and
never `esc(t(…))`); a sentence with interpolations is one key with its params in source order,
a param that is markup passed as `rawHtml(…)`; a plural is `tn`/`thn`. A line held in state (the
status line, a sheet's `said`, a field's `error`, a seat line, a receipt, a Run's title) is `t(…)`
where host code makes it, and escaped once where it is drawn. No words call runs at a module's top
level: a word list a module once held as a constant (`TABS`, `MONTHS`, `SEARCH_LINE`, `DAYS`, a
host's tabs, sorts and kinds) is a function of no argument read when drawn, beside its frozen ids
(`ACCOUNT_TAB_IDS`, `TRADE_KIND_IDS`, `SHELF_IDS`), and `MODULES` reads its words through getters.
Logic never compares a table word: an order's `mine`, China's `notAnswering` flag, a seg's id, a
module headline's `quiet`, a Discover kind line by shelf, an unread code are what the code tests.
A seg passes `[label, value]` pairs whose values are codes. A memoized renderer adds
`wordsEpoch()` to its key (`railHtml`). What stays as written is marked `// en-kept: <reason>` on
its own line (63 such lines at plan 6: provider, wallet, chain and network names, key names, the
Account's wire words compared, `P&L`, errors never on screen).

**The thread** (`render/thread.js`) — the operator's words right in the primary bubble (since the
dsh UI port's plan 4 with the message's attachments in `.you-files` above it, right-aligned in
`.you-body`: a lone image a `.you-image` key up to 240 px wide and 320 px tall, with others 64 px
`.you-thumb` squares, an image not read yet an empty frame (`loading`), and an image whose thumb is
`null`, offloaded by compaction or not an image's URL drawn as its file card, named by its name or
`Image`, its line `<TYPE> · <size>`; a file its card, which opens nothing — the host gives no file
back; an attachment-only message has no bubble), Gravit's
left in grey through the markdown hook (headings, lists, code, quotes, GFM tables in the
`.viz-table` style, links coloured and underlined; an interrupted answer is cut-marked
`Interrupted`); a
bot's words in a group under its sender name, through the same markdown hook; a system line centred; a context row a collapsed
`<details class="sysline ctx">` headed `context · <source>`; no tool row (the operator's word, 2026-10-28: `renderMessage` draws nothing for the kind and `renderThread` skips
it, so a divider reads the gap between the rows it draws; a gate the call raised, a receipt or a
refusal is a row of its own); a room member's answer that names
its member turn followed by a `Trace` disclosure (`trace-<sessionId>-<msgId>`), read on opening: `Loading…`,
the turn's context lines and words (its tool calls not drawn, so a turn of tool calls alone reads `No steps`), the loader's
words, or `No steps`; the seat's card (`Your call: …`, the venue chip and the reason, ✗ Decline then ✓ Approve →
`rejected` / `allowed-once`); the approval card (the tool name, the display reason, the audit
reason only when it differs, the same two keys); the question card (`data-gate="<eventId>"`;
every question with its inputs named and id'd `q-<eventId>-<questionId>`, so two pending cards
never share a radio group, radio or checkbox by `multiSelect`, and a free-answer box beside
every question — `Other…` beside a menu, `Your answer` without — which is dsh's `custom`; one
Answer key for the batch); a receipt a green bubble; a refusal a red card
with the code. An answered or closed gate shows its end state as a chip — `Approved`,
`Declined`, `Answered`, `Closed`, `Settled elsewhere` — and no keys. Dividers after a
15-minute gap; the three-dot thinking row at the tail while the host streams a turn.

**The thread at its edges** (the dsh UI port's plan 5; `js/mask.js`, `host/turns-view.js`,
`host/jobs*.js`, `render/thread.js`, `render/messages.js`, `app.js`).
- **The masked bubble and the excerpts** (§5.9, D25, A2). The operator's own bubble runs each text
  run of `sessionRefRuns` through `maskSpans`, so chips stay chips; a secret run is
  `span.secret[data-secret]` holding `span.secret-raw` (the original, transparent and selectable,
  laid over its mask in the same mono font) and `span.secret-mask` (`*`s, unselectable), then its eye
  `button.secret-eye#secret-<msgId>-<n>` (`data-action="toggleSecret"`, `aria-label="Show secret"`,
  then `Hide secret`; the `eye` / `eyeOff` icons at 14 px). Unrevealed, the raw run is `aria-hidden`
  and the mask is `role="img"` `aria-label="secret, hidden"` (the controller's ruling: a key spoken
  aloud is shown); revealed, the raw run is plain text and no mask is drawn. A selection across a
  masked value copies the original, with no `copy` listener. Every excerpt is `maskExcerpt`ed
  whoever spoke (the operator's ruling): the list's preview line (`previewOf` stays the raw text),
  a search hit's snippet before `highlightRuns` (its length kept, so the match marks the right
  characters) and the rail card's prompt and reply. A conversation's title is derived from its
  first prompt, so it is `maskExcerpt`ed wherever drawn (the controller's ruling, extending the
  operator's): the list row, a search hit, the head (`head-title`, a room's `head-task`), Details'
  This task, a conversation chip's label in a bubble, the `@` menu's conversation rows and a market
  page's conversations. Gravit's, a bot's and the host's bubbles, context rows, the composed answer,
  the draft (its chips' labels included), the rename box and a job's command and output are never
  masked. What is revealed is `revealed`, a `Set` of `<conv>|<msgId>|<n>` in `app.js`, cleared when
  the conversation on screen changes.
- **The thread box and the earlier key.** A conversation's thread sits in `div.thread-box` beside
  `nav.turn-rail#turn-rail` (`aria-label="Turns"`); New message and the empty state keep a bare
  `.thread`. While `window.hasMore`, the thread opens with `button.earlier-key#earlier-<conv>`
  (`data-action="earlier"`): `Earlier messages`, and `Loading…` with `aria-disabled="true"` while
  `window.loading` (not `disabled`, so the pressed key keeps focus across the read; a press while it
  reads asks nothing); after the last page the key goes and `#say` takes focus. On the same
  conversation, a window start below the one last drawn keeps the reader's place: `renderThread`
  marks the first message at or past `last.anchor` with `data-anchor` (beside any id it has), and
  the keep adds the anchor's `offsetTop` after minus before (the scrollHeight difference without
  one), at the bottom too; where the thread does not scroll (≤ 860 px) the document's
  `scrollingElement` is moved instead. Focus put back on the same control, or on `#say` when the
  earlier key went, uses `{preventScroll: true}`.
- **The rail and its card.** `renderThread` draws a `div.turn-mark#tmark-<conv>-<turn>` before the
  first message whose seq is past each tick's seq when the tick is loaded or that message falls
  before the next tick (the window's oldest turn can read unloaded while its prompt is drawn); loaded
  ticks left over go at the end. `railHtml(conv, {active, hover, pulse, focus})` is the rail's markup,
  memoized on its inputs (`conv.id`, `outline`, `loaded`, the window's start and hasMore, active,
  hover, pulse, focus, and since plan 6 `wordsEpoch()`), `railView` memoized on the first five:
  the `nav` is `role="toolbar"` `aria-orientation="vertical"` (plan 6), one `button.turn-tick`
  (`aria-label="Turn <n>"`, `data-action="jumpTurn"`) per outline entry, `loaded`, `active` or
  `pulse`, one tick `tabindex="0"` — the focused one, else the active, else the last — and the rest
  `-1`, so the rail is one Tab stop; ↑ ↓ Home End move the focus along it (`stepRail`, one rail
  write per arrow), Enter and Space are the button's own press; the pulsing tick is
  `aria-busy="true"`; for the hovered or focused tick a `.turn-card#turn-card-<turn>` (`Turn <n> ·
  jump`, drawn in capitals by CSS, the prompt and, when not empty, the reply, both `maskExcerpt`ed
  and escaped), which that tick names in `aria-describedby`. `app.js` keeps `rail =
  {active, hover, pulse, focus, jump}` outside the store, reset with `revealed` (`focusin` sets hover
  and focus, a genuine `focusout` clears both, the pointer leaves focus as it is). A scroll of `#thread`
  (coalesced to one `timers.after(80)`), `mouseover`/`focusin` on a tick and
  `mouseout`/`focusout` out of the rail redraw `#turn-rail` alone (`drawRail`, keeping a focused
  tick by its id with `preventScroll`), never the page; a render's own focus restore (`refocusing`),
  the rail's own redraw and a `focusout` from a tick a page write took out of the document
  (`isConnected` false, as Chrome fires it) change no hover, and while a press is down the redraw waits for its
  release. `measureRail` reads the marks' `offsetTop`s and `activeTurn` once after a render whose
  rail inputs changed. `jumpTurn` on a tick whose mark is drawn scrolls it into view at once
  (`toMark`: `scrollIntoView({block: 'start'})`, never smooth — a glide is cut short by the next
  render, whose keep would read a place mid-glide and might snap back to the tail); on an unloaded one it sets `pulse` and `jump` and calls `live.earlier(id, {toSeq:
  tick.seq})`, asking once more when a running read ended above the tick; the render that draws the
  mark scrolls to it and clears both, a failed read (or one with no mark and no render held) clears
  them, and another conversation opened meanwhile has replaced `rail`, so a late answer touches
  nothing. At ≤ 860 px the rail is hidden.
- **The pills and Usage.** Under the thread `div.thread-foot` holds the status line and
  `statsPills(conv)`: one `button.stats-pill` per non-empty `pillsText` part (`pill-figures-<conv>`,
  `pill-tokens-<conv>`; `data-action="openUsage"`; since plan 6 `aria-label="<its text>, open Usage"`)
  — `<t> turn(s) · <s> step(s) · <v> tok/s` and `<k> tokens · cache <p>%` — or nothing when both
  are empty. `openUsage` (and `openJobs`) go
  through `openDetailsAt(section)`: `openDetails` opens Details over `closeOverlays` (or leaves an
  open one), and the render after it scrolls `#dsec-usage` (or `#dsec-jobs`) into view after the
  drawer's own scroll keep, once. Usage (`section.dsec#dsec-usage`) adds, after Tokens in, Tokens out
  and Context, `Cache hit`, `Turns · steps`, `Model time`, `Tool time`, `First token` (the average)
  and `Speed` from `statsView`, each only when its figure exists: a zero model, tool or first-token
  time and a speed with no `decodeMs` are not figures (the controller's ruling).
- **The chip and Background jobs.** In the head, before `Working`, `button.btn-sm.jobs-chip`
  (`data-action="openJobs"`, `chipText`: `1 job running`, `2 jobs running`, `2 jobs finished` when
  none runs; its `.jobs-dot` `live` while one runs). Details' `section.dsec#dsec-jobs` (`Background
  jobs`, right after This task) draws each running job as a `div.job`: `details#jobd-<id>`, open
  while it is the store's open job, its summary (`data-action="openJob"`, `data-job`) a dot,
  `code.job-cmd` (the command, escaped, never masked) and `span.job-meta` (`metaLine`, the live
  clock a `span[data-job-clock]` that a 1 s `timers.after` loop rewrites without a render while one
  is drawn); inside, an empty `pre.job-out#jobout-<id>` and `div.job-note#jobnote-<id>`, a settled
  job that wrote nothing a `div.job-end` reading `(no output)` alone (since plan 6; the end line —
  `exit 0`, `signal TERM`, `killed`, `failed` — is the meta line's only, so it is drawn once), and Copy
  (`aria-label="Copy command"`, `copyText`); beside it Stop (`job-stop-<id>`), the confirm `Yes,
  stop`, or `Stopping` (`job-stopping-<id>`, `tabindex="-1"`). The finished go in
  `details#jobs-finished-<conv>` (`Finished · <n>`, drawn open while it holds the open job) with
  Clear (`clearJobs`). `openJob` reads the disclosure's own state after the click toggled it:
  opening follows the job and dispatches `openJob`, closing unfollows it. The open job's `pre` node
  is kept across renders as `#composer-note` is: `render()` takes it before its `innerHTML` write
  and puts it back over the fresh one (`replaceWith`), with the `scrollTop` it had, before any
  scroll keep, so a render neither rewrites nor re-creates its text. `app.js`'s `writeOutput` sets
  its `textContent` (`outputOf`) on each output frame (`onOutput`), and once into a `pre` a render
  drew for the first time; a `pre` at its end stays at its end, one the reader scrolled up keeps its
  place. The note reads `output
  unavailable: <code>` for a refused follow or `output ended` for one that ended while the row is
  live. `Yes, stop` marks the job `stopping` at once (`markJob`) and puts focus on `Stopping`;
  `kill` answering `false` marks it back. The subscriber drops a Stop confirm whose job no longer
  runs, and unfollows the open job once it is no longer drawn (its row gone, Clear, Details
  closed, another conversation).

**Markets** (`render/markets.js`, every figure and word about a market a view's — `tableOf`'s,
`pageOf`'s) — the head (`Markets`, the
search box `#mq`, `Search markets`); the tabs (`tabsOf`: All, the Account's kinds where it lists
something, each with the Account's count once All's read has answered; All results while
searching, Watching once anything is starred, and Desk last — the Desk tab, below); the sort seg Most traded · Biggest moves, and
Closing soonest where a row closes (two or more rows); and one table — the star (`Watch BTC` /
`Stop watching BTC`; `Remove` for an old star `Not listed at the Account`), the name (`mkAv`'s tile
of the face's own letters, the name over its sub, `Closed` past its end, `Paper` where only a
paper account trades it first; a market no read lists, `Not in this read`, and a star not listed
open no page), the price in its unit (`$63,226.60`, `62¢`, `¥1,688.00`), the 24 hours (the arrow,
`up`/`down` for a screen reader, the percent or an event's cents), the volume (`$1.9B`, `412k
contracts`, `2M shares`) and Source (the Account's words for where the price is from, with its
age); with a query, `N markets for “q”` and Clear. With no rows: `Nothing watched yet`, `No
markets`, `Loading…` or `Searching…`, `Markets unavailable` or `Search is unavailable`. The muted
lines: the Account's sentence from the read the rows are from, the search's failure or
partial answer while searching (the Account's `missing` names China when Tencent did not answer), China's own lines (the session, stale, `Couldn’t refresh China`), the
watchlist's trouble (a refused `setWatch` among it, in the Account's words). On a page that signs
the star of an Account row signs the Account's own watch (§5.3). No image the Account names.

**The Desk tab** (`render/desk.js` over `deskViewOf`; the desk's P3) — the Markets tabs' last,
`Desk`, drawn in place of the table while it is chosen and nothing is searched; it reads
`/data/desk/status` when Markets is shown, then every 10 s (`startDesk`), and asks no market read. The head: the
desk's status lines — the boot, the pause, Telegram, the budget, a ledger that cannot be read —
beside one control, **Pause** (no Resume and no arming: both are a terminal's, spec §5.7). Then its
sections: **The watch** (its state, each market's line with that market's today, the batch held,
the mute, an unreadable alert ledger and the filings' state; `The watch is not running.` without
one), **Alerts** (the recent ones, each its time, what fired, its outcome and its latency — `1.8 s`,
or `—` for a send queued or never sent; `No alerts yet.`), **Levels as loaded** (the watch's `marks`,
each with its mark, plan and file, then every file with refusals or an error, numbered `#i SYM:
reason`; `No levels loaded.`), **Standing orders** (since P4 an A-share order's line led by `market cn, `,
as `standingLines` prints it, and `its session`, a link to `#/messages/<sessionId>`, the session its last
firing woke — the report, read where it was said), **Firings**, and **Runs and
sleep** (the last ten runs, the sleep gaps as `20 min` or `1 h 5 min`). `Loading…` before the
first read, `Desk status unavailable` when a read fails with nothing kept, and the failure's
sentence over the view kept until a read answers. **A level's mark**: a Markets row whose symbol has a
level gets `<span class="mk-level">` after its name (`stop 170 · -1.30%`, the nearest level, the
distance from the watch's last price), and its page `<p class="mk-plan">` under the price — the
mark, the plan and its file — from the status's `marks`.

**A market's page** (`#/markets/<id>`, `marketPage` over `pageOf`) — `‹ Markets`; the head (the
tile, the name, the kind and the symbol at the line it follows, or an event's category and
`closes <date>`; `Closed` past its end) with — on a page that signs, for a market of a Trade kind
(`tradeableOf`) — **Buy**, and **Sell** where something of it is held, each `openTicket` (Trade on
the market, the ticket on that side), then Hand to Gravit (a new message in the root channel
with `Look at <base> (<name>)` in the composer, `handWordsOf`), Watch / Watching and — for a
perpetual, on a page that signs for an Account that takes writes, where a venue sets leverage from
here — **Leverage…** (`marketLeverageSeedOf`); the price (the
stream's or the quotes poll's for the line it follows, else the explore read's) with the explore
read's 24 hours, an event's outcomes in cents, where the price is from with its age, and the facts
24h volume and Venues. **Price history**: the `CANDLE_RANGES` seg (`setRange`, naming the page),
the range's closes once a candles read answered (`candlesSvg`: the closes as an area and a line in
the box the three charts share, the low and the high touching the margins, the axis at the first
and last bars' times on the operator's clock, an event's in cents; the Account's `ends` and `note`
under it), `No history` for fewer than two, `Loading…` while a range not drawn yet is read, the
Account's sentence or `History unavailable` over a failed read, the closes kept while the range is
read again. **Across venues**: each line with its price in the market's unit, `Best`, `Paper`, and
for a public listing `Connect to trade` (a link to `#/account/venues`). **You here** (since plan 4a
in place of You hold and Open orders, from the asset sheet; `Account unavailable` before it answers:
the venues it could not read, the holding, the positions with their cost and — on a page that signs
for an Account that takes writes — **Close…** (`Sell…` for a stock or an event) and **Leverage…**, the
owner's open orders with **Change…**, and under `What agents do here` a line per agent order working
here, with its Change…, or statement line by them; `You don’t hold any.`), **Order book** (ten levels
a side, best first, bids beside asks, whose book in its words, `Top of book` for a book of the best
bid and ask alone; `Order book unavailable`), **Latest trades** (twenty, newest first — price, size,
the side that took where the source says, when — or the Account's sentence when the source
publishes none; `Trades unavailable`), a perpetual's **Funding** (paid and received, hour by hour,
newest first, `None yet.`, the venues not read named; `Funding unavailable`), **Gravit on it** (the conversations
naming it, as links, when there are any) and **On the statement** (`✓` on a filled or settled
line; `Open the Statement →`), each on its own read: `Loading…` until it answers, its
empty words — `You don’t hold any.`, `Nothing on the statement about it yet.` — only after an
answer, the Account's sentence or the part's own `… unavailable` when it failed before any answer,
and the lines it read kept under a later refusal; a market the asset read does not name (an event no
connected venue lists) holds nothing here. The compare rows are read and not drawn. A `cn:` page is the Account's quote (`quotes?pairs=china|<code>`) with its history (`candles?venue=china`): the
price, the change with its basis, `as of 14:30 · Live`, the facts Previous close, Volume, Source,
Gravit on it.

**Account** (`render/account.js`, every figure and word a view's) — the head (`Account`, the mode
and writes chips from `headOf`, Refresh, Settings) and under it the device line (`renderDeviceLine`,
below), the Account's refusal sentence as a muted line when it gave one, and the seven tabs Portfolio ·
Money · Venues · Agents · Cards · Rules · Identity (`tabsOf()`, `router.js` `TABS`; `Cards · N` while cards wait; `#/account/<tab>`). The
owner's keys below are drawn only while `owner.role === 'signs'` — absent, not disabled, otherwise:
the device line says why — and the Market half's and Money's only for an Account that also takes
writes (`marketKeysOn`: `writesOn`, the page's `connectLive.writes.on`).
**Portfolio**: the leading figure with its label (`Net worth`, or `Paper` when Paper leads) and the
second beside it, smaller; the change line in one run (the change — `—` when the Account gave none
— the range, `partial`, since when on All, and on the paper curve `since start <signed dollars>`
and `rebuilt`); the 1D · 1W · 1M · All seg (`setHistoryRange`); the curve (`curveSvg`, labelled by
the leading figure); the venues a read could not reach; the stale stamp and Retry after a failure,
and the Statement key; **Assets** (each asset's venues under it; Asset · Amount · Price · 24h ·
Value; **Sell many…** over the table, and an earning row's **Take out…**, the Earn sheet on that
product) and **Positions** (Position · Value · Entry · Mark · P&L, `Paper`; each row's **Close…** —
**Sell…** for a stock or an event — and a perpetual's **Leverage…** where its venue sets it), the
leading lens's — the lens's refusal sentence where `Holdings unavailable` would be; **Open orders**
(`orderWords`, with whose each is; `No open orders`). Before the page: `Loading…`, `Account
unavailable` with Retry, `Account unreadable` for a page the face does not recognise. **Sell many**
is a drawer (`renderSellMany`): `Everything you hold that isn't a dollar. Pick up to 10: each is its
own order at market and its own signature.`, the rows with a checkbox and an amount each, the
venues not served or not read named, `At most 10 at once`, **Review <n> sales**; then each leg —
`Asking…`, what it would sign under `What you sign`, `waiting`, `signing…`, its answer or the
Account's refusal — **Back** and **Sign <n>**; **Done** with the closing line.
**Money**: **Receive** — `Send only the asset on the network the row names: anything else may not
arrive.`, one row per account and network (`<account> · <network words>`, an exchange's asset chip)
with **Show address**, then the address, its memo where one is needed (`Memo / tag — needed with
it`), whose it is with the Account's note, **Copy** and **Read again** — or the Account's refusal;
none: `None of your accounts gives an address to send to from here. …`. **Move** — on a page that
signs, each account money moves from with what it holds (`Agent wallet` chipped) and **Move…** (the
move sheet from it; `Sign and move`); on a read-only Account `Read-only: the Account was started
without trading, so it moves no money.`. **Earn** — each product's venue, amount and yield with
**Take out…**, **Put in…** under them (`Sign and put in`, `Sign and take out`), the venues not served
on this network, a failed read in its words alone (`Earn could not be read.` when it gave none),
`Nothing is earning to take out.`. **Waiting for your wallet** — the payments the Account built for
the operator's own wallet (`walletRow`, as Trade's Under way draws them): `Waiting for your wallet`,
what the last send said, **Send from wallet…** or **Report again**, off while one is in the air.
**Venues**: each venue's value, front line and what it trades, its health (`Not answering since
14:02`), what it does, `Paper` or `Closed to agents`, stale, and **Details** — a drawer
(`venueDetails`: its holdings and the Account's facts under their labels, the key file by its path,
`No details`; a paper venue's **Top up** and **Start over**) that takes focus and closes on Escape —
**Close to agents** (any page that reads the Account, unsigned, off while its press is in the air;
its sentence or the Account's refusal under the list) or, closed, **Reopen…** (signed, `Sign and
reopen`), and **Disconnect…** (asked in place, `Yes, disconnect`; none on an agent wallet); a paper
venue has no switch to agents; under the list **Connect an account** (every kind of connector, below)
and **Open a paper account**; the `A-share quotes` line from the Account's China state
(`markets.providers`, which `chinaStatusUpdated` fills from the ranking's status or a refused quote
read — so the line stands once the Account has answered for China); the Account seat box (the
service with the Account's own mode and writes, the seat and its limits, the venues with `Paper`
chips, the cards waiting, the stamp, Refresh, and **Answer under Cards** while cards wait).
**Agents**: Gravit's seat first (its standing and limits in the seat box's words, `Cards N · Open
orders N`, `—` while the agents are unread; while its seat is admitted **Give a limit…**, **End
limit…** and **Revoke…** — the Account's words for what revoking Gravit stops, then `Yes, revoke` —
and while it knocks **Let in…** on the request at the seat view's own address), then the others with
their status, until when and limits — each with **Give a limit…** (every scope: trade, venues,
payees, earn), **End limit…** on each standing limit of the four, **Revoke…** — and `Knocking` keys,
each with **Let in…**; `Loading…`, `Agents unavailable`, `No agents`. **Agent wallets** under it:
each wallet's name, whom it pays for, its address and what it holds of how much it keeps at most,
with **Top up…** and **Take back…** (move sheets) for an Account that takes writes, and **Open an agent
wallet…** (`Make it`) while a key is let in; `Let an agent in first: a wallet pays for one agent.`
otherwise. **Cards**: `Waiting for you` grouped by agent — each card's reason, value, answer-by time
and `What it asks` (a disclosure of every signed field verbatim), with **✓ Approve** and **✗ Reject**
(one card, one signature) — or `Nothing waiting`, and the `Asks`, each with **Grant** where `grantsAsk`
says the face grants it (every kind: a limit, a venue, a key, a top-up, a session, leverage, the mode)
and **Decline**, and under them a Grant that could not open, in words. **Rules**: **Mode** — the
Guard · Beast seg (Guard one click on any page that reads the Account, `setGuard`, unsigned; Beast a
signed sheet, `Sign Beast`, its key only on a page that signs and only while Beast is not in force),
what the last Guard press said while it still reads true, `Only a browser that signs switches to
Beast.` on a page that does not, the lead `Guard: what agents ask for waits for you on a card. Beast:
inside the limits you signed, it goes at once. Guard is one click; Beast is signed.`, the line
`Beast removes the Account's card only: Gravit's orders still raise their Gate 2 card in this face
first.`, the table of what each mode does door by door (`An agent, inside its limit` · Guard ·
Beast, `Now` on the mode in force) and how long a card waits; **Limits** — **Each move at most** (the
cap, **Change…**, `Sign the cap`), **Agents' session** (`Agents may act until <date>.` or `Ended: …`,
**Renew for 30 days** or **Start a new one**) and, where a venue sets leverage from here, **Their
leverage** (`Up to <n>x on a perpetual, …`, **Change…**, `Sign leverage`); on a read-only Account
each of the three says `Read-only: the Account was started without trading, so there is no …`.
**Identity** (`render/identity.js` `renderIdentityTab`, drawn from `state.identity` alone, not the
Account's read; plan B1b) — three cardboxes in the page's existing classes (no CSS of its own but
`.sheet-steps` and `.identity-qr`): **Gravit** (`Where Gravit reaches you beyond this face, and who
it talks to there.`; Telegram's row — `Not connected` with Connect… (`identityConnect`), or a
`Connected` chip, `Speaks as`, `Talks only with`, the problem line, Details (`identityDetails`,
`aria-expanded`; `Since <date> · token <fp> · <polling | not polling | the problem>`) and
Disconnect… (`btn-danger`, `openSheet` `disconnectNetwork`); Slack's row the same since plan B2,
its key `Install app…` (`identityConnect` with `data-network="slack"`), its problem line saying
`Another program holds this app's connection to Slack` on a conflict and `Not hearing Slack …` on
failing reads; iMessage a `Later` chip and no key);
**What reaches you where** (an `acct-t` table, What · Face · Telegram · iMessage · Slack, a checkbox
per cell with its `aria-label`, Face ticked and disabled, Telegram's and Slack's `identityTick` each
live only on a signing page once that network is connected, iMessage disabled; `Not saved yet: Save… signs the change.` and Save…
while the draft differs; Quiet hours `<from>–<to> ET` or `Off`, `Inside them alerts, the brief,
reports, cards and fills are not sent, and not sent later; replies, urgent alerts and the watchdog
always go.`, Change…) and **Not you · n** (`<network> · <masked> · <n> message(s) · last <clock, or
date and clock>`, Block, or `Nobody else has written to Gravit.`). The owner's keys only while the
page signs; otherwise `Only a browser that signs changes these.` and the draft is not drawn. No
data and a failure or kept words: `The account is not answering.`, the words, Retry
(`refreshIdentity`, fresh); no data otherwise `Loading…`; an answer without `ok: true` `Identity
unreadable` and Retry. **Connect Telegram's sheets 1–3** (`renderConnectDrawer`, an `aside.drawer.sheet`
drawn only while no owner sheet is up, Escape closing the owner sheet first): `Connect Telegram · 1
of 4 · Bot token` — `<input id="identity-token" type="password" autocomplete="off"
spellcheck="false" data-lpignore="true" data-1p-ignore="true" data-form-type="other">` with no
`<form>` around it (ruling of B1b Task 2: no save-password prompt; Enter is Next through the
document's keydown), never drawn with a value, Paste (`navigator.clipboard.readText()` where the
browser allows), the Kept in / Never in lines, Cancel and Next (`Checking…` while busy); `2 of 4 ·
Say hi` — the link only when it is exactly `https://t.me/<username>`, the QR an `<img
class="identity-qr">` only when it starts with exactly `data:image/svg+xml;base64,`, the expiry on
New York's clock (`etClock`), `Another program reads this bot's messages: stop it, and this sheet
goes on.` on a conflict, `The account is not answering: this sheet keeps asking.` while silent,
Back and Cancel; `3 of 4 · Is this you?` — Name, Handle, `Telegram id: …123` (masked only; the full
id is never in the HTML), Message, Back, Cancel, Not me, This is me. Each ends with its numbered
`connectSteps(step)` in an `<ol class="sheet-steps">` above its keys; an error on sheets 2–3 carries
Start again. Sheet 4 and the other three are `renderSheet` (§5.1's row): `Connect Telegram · 4 of 4
· What you sign`, `Disconnect Telegram`, `What reaches you where`, `Block …789`. **Slack's sheets**
(plan B2): `Connect Slack · 1 of 4 · App tokens` — `App manifest`, the account's `slackManifest` as
escaped text in `<pre class="identity-manifest" tabindex="0">` with Copy (`identityCopyManifest`:
the clipboard, else the `<pre>` selected; `Copied` once taken; `The account gave no manifest: update
the account, then open this sheet again.` without one), then `App-level token (xapp-…)` and `Bot
token (xoxb-…)`, two password fields under Telegram's field's rules (Enter in the first moves to
the second, in the second is Next), the Kept in lines, Cancel and Next, and its five steps (create
from the manifest at api.slack.com/apps, the `connections:write` app-level token, install for the
bot token, paste them only here); `2 of 4 · Say hi` — `Open Gravit in <workspace>` only when the
link is Slack's `app_redirect`, the QR, `Workspace: <name>`, `Another program holds this app's
connection to Slack: stop it, and this sheet goes on.` on a conflict; `3 of 4 · Is this you?` —
Name, Handle (`@<username>`), `Slack id: U…` (the full user id: a display name anyone can copy, the
id no one can), Message; sheet 4 `Connect Slack · 4 of 4 · What you sign` with `Tokens kept in:
Account · :4820` and, under its steps, `SLACK_STEPS_4_NOTE` (`On Slack, type the phone's commands
with ! — !status, !pause 30m, !mute 30m, !new, !stop.`); `Disconnect Slack` says both tokens are
deleted from the account; the routing sheet's `On Telegram: …` and `On Slack: …` lines, one for each
network connected.
**The Statement** is a drawer (`renderStatement`): the lines newest first, each with its
time, the Account's description, who it was by, its status and fee, its amount; Export CSV (a
`statement.csv` blob of `statementCsvOf`, its URL revoked a tick after the click); `Loading…`,
`No statement lines yet`, `Statement unavailable`, the Account's sentence over the lines kept. The
Settings drawer gains **Devices** (`renderDevices`). Not on the face, by the design (spec §5.4): the
Account's own Superagent (the Desk and its Brains), Intents and Memory — their server code and seat
tools stay in `account/`.

**The owner device on screen** (`render/owner.js`; every word `owner-view.js`'s, `sheet-view.js`'s
or the Account's) — the device line under the Account head's chips, one muted sentence by role:
`This page signs for the account`; `Waiting to be let in — a browser that signs lets it in, under
Settings › Devices`; `Pair with the code the Account printed in its terminal` with the pair box (a form:
`#pair-code`, **Pair**, Enter submits it); `Signed out` with **Sign in**; `This browser cannot
sign for the account`; nothing while
`unknown` — the Account's last refusal to the device joined on with ` · `, Pair and Sign in off
while a pairing is in the air. **Devices** in Settings (`devicesOf`): each owner `label · id`, this
page's own marked `this page`; each device waiting `kid · since <date>`, with **Let it sign** — and
this page's **Sign out** — only on a page that signs. **The sheet** (`renderSheet`, a drawer over any
screen, `aria-label` its title): its title (`titleOf`), its fields by type (a seg, a pick as
checkboxes, a box, a select whose nothing-picked is an empty option, text — a number typed as
text), a connect sheet's check under them (`connectCheckOf`: `Key file found: <path>`, `Missing: a,
b`, the venue's words, a browser wallet's words — `No browser wallet answered on this page. Type the
address to watch it.`, `Waiting for <wallet>…`, `<wallet> signed: <address> is yours.` — an address's
or a command line's example, a sign-in's state; above the address a **Use <wallet>** tile per browser
wallet the page found, and under it **Sign in at <venue>**, off while it starts, waits or is ready,
with `Open <venue>'s sign-in page` as a link when no tab opened), the quote box (`Fill it in to see what it
would be.` or the missing words, `Asking…`, the Account's refusal with **Prepare again** when that
is the answer, the quote's words), the countdown, **What you sign** (a fold of every shown line,
dimmed while the form is not the draft asked for), what the Account said once done, **Cancel** and
the go key (`goWord`: `Let it in`, `Give the limit`, `End the limit`, `Revoke`, `Connect`, `Open the
account`, `Top up`, `Start over`, `Disconnect`, `Approve` or `Reject`, `Decline`, `Let it sign`,
`Sign out`, `Sign and place`, `Sign and reopen`, and the Market half's, Rules' and Money's —
`Sign and close` or `Sign and sell`, `Sign and change`, `Sign leverage`, `Sign Beast`, `Sign the cap`,
`Renew for 30 days` or `Start a new one`, `Sign and move`, `Sign and put in` or `Sign and take out`,
`Make it`), on only while the sheet is ready and current. A sign-out in Beast carries the box
`Switch to Guard first: whatever an agent asks for waits for a signature`, ticked for the last device
that signs.

**Trade** (`render/trade.js`, `#/trade`; after gravit-ui's Trade at `feat/gravit-ui @ 2418df7`, its
stand-in logic replaced by the Account's prepare) — the head (`Trade`, the Account's writes chip),
the kinds seg (Crypto · Stocks · RWAs · Predictions), the picker (`pickerOf`: **You hold** — the
leading lens's rows matched to an Account key, a prediction held opening as a sell of its outcome —
**Watching** and **Most traded**, or `Results for “q”` while the search box `#tq` holds a query;
`Loading…`, `No markets`, `Markets unavailable`, `Searching…`, `Nothing matches “q” under Crypto.`),
**Under way** (`underWayOf`: each working order in `orderWords`, its id, **Change…** where
`amendSeedOf` gives a seed, for an Account that takes writes, and **Cancel** — one click — where the
Account knows what cancels it, on a page that signs; a DEX order or a payment waiting for the
operator's own wallet as a `walletRow`, an order keeping its Cancel; `Nothing under way.`; what was
said on Trade, a cancel's answer or a fill, over them; under them **Cards waiting** when the page
has cards — `cardsOf`, each `reason · value · answer by` in the Cards tab's words (`cardFactsOf`)
with **Review →** to `#/account/cards`, rows only, no key that signs), and the ticket panel:
`Pick a market`
with none open; else the head (`Buy ETH` / `Sell ETH`, the close key), the market picked, a
prediction's outcomes in cents, **Where** (the able lines as keys, `Best` and `Paper` marked; the
other lines dim, a public listing with `Public` and **Connect to trade** → `#/account/venues`),
Buy or Sell, **Amount** and **In** (Dollars or the market's unit — Shares, Contracts, the base),
**Order** (Market or Limit; a limit's price field, a prediction's in cents), **Extended hours** on a
limit where the picked line offers them, the quote box (`quoteOf`: the Account's words with
`Paper`, `≈ <dollars>`, `up to <dollars> if the price moves`, `fee <dollars>` or `fee as <venue>
charges it`;
dimmed with What you sign while the form is not the draft asked for), the countdown, **What you
sign** (`#tk-signs`, closed until opened, the seventeen fields and the nonce verbatim), the
Account's refusal or what it placed (`Placing it…` while signing), **Prepare again** when that is
the answer, **Sign and place** — on only while the shown preparation is the form's — and **Hand to
Gravit instead**. On a page that does not sign the screen still draws the picker and Under way,
and the ticket panel draws the device line where the form would be: no Sign and place, no
Cancel.

**A channel's page** (`render/channel.js`, `#/channel/<workspaceId>`) — part of Messages: the list
stays beside it. The head (the channel by its title, its status chip, `New round` — a new message
with Where on the channel); the one-line headline, `Next: …` and the numbers as rows; **Thesis**
through the markdown hook (`No thesis yet` for the template or none); **Latest backtest** — its
file and up to twelve of its scalar fields — and **Backtests** (file and size), both only for an
old strategy that carries a `backtests/` directory (none is written since 2026-10-24); **Research
runs** after Latest backtest, only for a channel whose overview lists a run (`runsView`, §5.2) — the
latest sealed run's line (run, as of, snapshot, the `cn-market` run it cites), a chip per module
(its headline values, `not evaluable`, the counterevidence's item count, or for the mode its mode
word alone, `mode: WAIT`), the expectation card as key-value rows, the previous card's review as one
line (`review: 弱于 of <run>`), each artifact whole in a collapsed details, then a dim line per run (as of, its
artifacts, its size, `unsealed`) and `older runs not listed: N`; **Journal** (the newest
twenty, date before text), **Files** (name, size, date); **Agents** and **Bots** — the rostered
names, each with `Edit`: a box per choice (the connected CLI agents; every bot but the host's own
composition), ticked as rostered, a seventh bot box shut while six are ticked, ✓ and ×. `Loading…`,
`Channel unavailable` with Retry, a failed re-read keeping the page under `As of HH:MM · stale` and
Retry, `Channel not found`. Every channel-written string is text.

**Discover** (`render/discover.js`) — the head (`Discover`, the search box `#dq`, `Search`, the
`Create a bot` key); the shelves **Data**, **Research**, **Bots**, **Agents** (with `Rescan`),
**Skills**, each with `See all` and its cards (the mark, the name, one line, the kind tag), a failed
listing saying `Couldn't read <Shelf>` with Retry beside the others, `Loading…`, or the shelf's
empty words; a search draws one grid (`N results`); `#/discover/<shelf>` the shelf as a grid with
`‹ Discover`. **The Research shelf** (module cards spec §5.1) is a grid, never a scrolling row, of
the six Lunhui modules (`Lunhui · 6 modules` in its title), always six whatever the listing
holds: each card links its glyph, name, 副题 and `MODULE` tag to `#/module/<name>`, then its role
and channel words (`CN market analyst · cn-market`), then a foot with the chip and `Run`
(`moduleChip`, `runKey`) — `runModule` opens the module's Run sheet; the key is off while the rows
are not mounted and, `title="Running"`, while a Run of the module is running. While it runs
(`activeRuns`: the conversation `running`, or the record under a minute old) the chip is the link
`Running · <title> ›` (`.chip.live`) to its conversation; when it stops, the chip reads the listing
again. Otherwise the chip reads the newest run among the module's channels (`chipOf`): its headline words
(`ok`, or grey for the quiet ones — `no candidate`, `WAIT`, `0 items`), `not evaluable · <missing
sources>` (`warn`), `not run` when that run lacks the module, `no run yet` with no run; a strategy
or either module's chip leads with the run's channel, `not run` too (`lunhui-s02-rotation · not run`). When the listing says the Lunhui rows are
not `mounted`, the line `Lunhui rows not mounted` shows and the cards stay, dimmed, their chips
grey. **A module's page** (`render/modules.js`, `#/module/<name>`, spec §5.3) wears the plugin
page's chrome (`main.disc.plugin-page`, `‹ Discover` back to the view it came from, Discover lit
in the rail): the head — the glyph at 72, the name, `<role> · deepseek-flash · <channel words>`,
`MODULE` beside the chip — the live one while a Run is running, before the listing is read too —,
`Run` as on the card —; three key-value boxes, **Reads** (Freezes,
Artifacts, Channel), **Writes** (File, Headline, Under — `strategies/<channel>/analysis/<run>/`
with the channel named as far as it is known) and **Runs on** (Role, Route, Budget `10 calls per
run · one artifact per run`); **Runs**, a table across the module's channels newest first —
Session, Channel, Run, Status (a chip: `OK` green, `NOT_EVALUABLE` amber), Headline — at most 24
rows, or `No run yet`; **Latest artifact**, the latest run's artifact as compact JSON in a
collapsed details once its channel's overview answers with that run, `Loading…` while it reads,
`open the channel page to read older runs` when the overview's latest is another run or the read
answered for a run the listing has since moved past, `Couldn't read` when the post failed; and, for Sentiment, Leader, Mode and Counterevidence, the legend of
Appendix A under its title — a label beside its reading, paragraph ids only. Before the modules
listing is read, Runs and Latest artifact say `Loading…` (`Couldn't read` when it failed) and the
head's chip `…` (`—`); an
unknown name reads `Loading…` while the listing is read, then `Not found`. `#/plugin/module:<name>`
is not redirected: it draws the plugin page's minimal body for a Research item (its role and
channel line), and nothing links there.
**The Run sheet** (`render/run-sheet.js`, spec §5.4) is a drawer of any screen in the owner
sheet's chrome (`div.drawer.sheet.run-sheet`, `role="dialog"`, `aria-label` `Run <Title>`, focus on
its close key and back to the opener on close), drawn from `sheetOf` over the modules listing:
**Where**, a select — fixed on `cn-market` for a market card, the strategies for Leader and Mode,
both for Counterevidence; **On**, a radio per option (`label.opt.on` open, its detail under it;
`label.opt.off` greyed, its reason under it — `theme already there`, `needs Leader, then
Counterevidence, on this run`, `mode already registered on this run`, `run no longer the latest`;
the stale one neither disabled nor checked while the newest run would take it, so a click on it
picks it again; disabled with the newest run's own reason when it would not):
`Latest run · <run> · session <date>` with what it froze, and `New run` for the three market cards
and Leader; **Cites**, a select of the two newest sealed `cn-market` runs for Leader (their frozen
sources and theme words, the line `theme not evaluable: the pick comes from the limit-up pool
alone` under a NOT_EVALUABLE theme, a warning when the cite lacks sentiment or theme), read-only
for Mode and a strategy's review (the run's leader's market run); **Stocks** for Leader's New
run alone (`#run-stocks`, its hint, `not a main-board code: <code>` or `at most 4 codes`; hidden on
Latest run, whose message has no codes, the typed text kept for New run); Theme's source line
(`boards missing in <n> of the last <m> runs`, from each listed sealed `cn-market` run's `frozen`); **Note to
Gravit** (`#run-note`); **Runs via** and **Writes** (the file and the conversation's title); what
was said, red; **Cancel** and **Run**, off with the blocker as its title while it cannot run.
The two boxes keep what was typed across a render by their ids; the selects and radios draw the
store's value.
**An item's page** (`#/plugin/<id>`, `‹ Discover` back to the view it came from): an MCP server's
State (`Pending`, `Loading`, `Active`, `Failed`, `Unloading`) and its tools, each description
clamped to two lines (a server may describe a tool with a whole method list); a bot's model
(`Default` when it names none), home, description, soul (pre-wrapped text), skills, setup issues
and `Can't run · <reason>`, with `Talk to <name>` (absent for a broken or unlisted bot) and `Edit`
— Name, Description, Model (Default, the catalog's routes, a route it lacks still offered), Soul,
each box's id carrying the revision it was drawn from; a CLI agent's version, sign-in (`Signed
in`, `Not signed in`, `Unknown`) and tool, with Connect or Disconnect; Gravit's Model, Host and
Keys cards, each `Loading…`, `Couldn't read` or its rows (`Present` / `Absent` per key); a skill's
group, description and content. An unknown id reads `Loading…` while its listing is read, then
`Not found`. **The Create page** (`#/discover/create`): Name, Id, Description, Model, Soul,
`Create`; the new bot's page opens. Discover's own status line carries its refusals. No Install,
Uninstall, Publish, review, install count or price.

**The composed answer** (plan 2 of the run view; spec §5.2–§5.3) — a `composed` message
(§5.2, `presentLift`) draws in a `msg-body composed`, wider than a card, as `composedHtml`: the
