  delegated child (`NOT_GRAVIT`), a submit's only to refuse anything else (`NOT_A_ROLE`); the strategy a call names is its only anchor, so a session in one
  channel, or at the root, can freeze quotes into another channel's directory (the other three
  freezes into `cn-market` alone). The bound is `runs.mjs`'s anchoring: a strategy name in the
  channel grammar naming a real directory directly under `strategiesRoot` that holds a regular
  `THESIS.md`, a run id under that strategy's own real `analysis/`, every entry `lstat`ed and never
  followed, containment compared by `realpath`, every directory re-checked (`stillResolved`) before
  each use, a new file opened `wx`, a replaced one written fresh and renamed over the old. A check
  and the use after it are still two calls (Node has no `openat`): a concurrent writer inside the
  strategy tree can race them. A metrics write killed before its rename leaves a
  `metrics.json.<hex>.tmp` (0o600, read by nothing, never swept — a sweep would race a concurrent
  writer's staging file); an `openRun` killed between its two writes leaves a run with `run.json`
  and no `metrics.json`, which reads fail-open as zero counts. And runs are not bounded: eight
  freezes bound one run, never how many runs a session opens, each a new directory and a new round
  of Tencent and Eastmoney requests. Recorded, nothing built.
- **R40 — The Lunhui calendar is one table a year, and only 2026 ships.** Stage 0's R33 — the
  graft ledger's (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-19-lunhui-plugin-graft-ledger.md`), not this
  document's — re-worded (modules spec A25). `lib/calendar.mjs` loads `lib/calendar/<year>.json`, each from that year's
  SSE notice, at import; a China date outside every table refuses every freeze with
  `CALENDAR_UNCOVERED` before any run is touched (every freeze also when the latest opened
  session, the one its evidence would record, lies outside), so nothing is frozen on a guessed weekday. Live from
  2027-01-01 until `2027.json` lands (§10, item 20). The tables are hand-entered: a holiday range
  is not checked for order or overlap, an empty calendar directory reads as no coverage — every
  freeze refused — rather than failing the mount, and `getMarketSession` across two years is
  untested until a second table exists.
- **R41 — The Eastmoney endpoints are unofficial, and from this machine their quotes are
  delayed.** No contract stands behind `push2ex.eastmoney.com` or `push2.eastmoney.com`: a changed
  reply shape is the parsers' `UPSTREAM_INVALID`, a refusal that writes nothing for that source
  (the distribution's refusal excepted: the index freeze lands its Tencent items without the
  counts, spec §17). Measured 2026-10-25: the clist answers 302 to `push2delay.eastmoney.com`
  with `dlmkts` set, so the boards, members and fund flow are delayed quotes; every Eastmoney item
  carries the host that served it and `delayed`, and the file's meta joins them (A28) — a
  `push2ex` reply carries no `dlmkts` and is never redirected, so a pool's or the distribution's
  `delayed` is false by construction: no delay declared, not a measurement of the data's age.
  Since 2026-10-26 the clist has mostly answered 502 from here, so the boards freeze fails while
  it does. The market counts come from `push2ex`'s up/down distribution instead (spec §16,
  2026-10-27): one request that takes no date and answers its latest session, refused when its
  `qdate` is not the freeze's session — from 09:15 China time until Eastmoney rolls the date, a
  window of unmeasured width, the index freeze lands without the counts; that bucket 11 and -11
  are 涨停 and 跌停, and that its universe (5,375 shares on 2026-10-27) is the Shanghai and
  Shenzhen shares with a price limit, are inferred, not documented, and a bucket the reply lacks
  reads as null, never 0. The hash stored with the counts is over the reply's `data`, not its
  bytes: the live reply's `svr` differs per request. The pools and the clist read `data` without
  looking at `rc`; only the distribution's parser does. A request's 7-second timeout is per hop, so a followed
  redirect can take 14 s. A request already in flight runs to completion after a sibling of the
  same freeze fails. Only the 涨停 pool's null or empty reply refuses `NO_MARKET_DATA`; an empty
  炸板 or 昨日涨停 pool is an empty list, so a day on which Eastmoney served the one and failed the
  others empty would freeze as a quiet day. And the evidence is point-in-time only from the first
  freeze: every source answers what it holds now, nothing rebuilds a past session, and a run's
  `as_of` is when it was frozen; its `session` is the trading day that data belongs to, so a
  Saturday's freeze reads Friday's session, not Saturday's clock. Since the boards stand-in
  (spec `2026-10-30-lunhui-boards-standin-design.md`) a boards refusal of this kind no longer
  leaves the theme module without boards when 问财 answers: egress `quantapi.51ifind.com` from the
  market (the market's `POST /api/cn/ifind` since 2026-11-03, the Account's before: the exchange, the query and at most one re-exchange, a 15-second
  deadline for the whole ask, a 4 MiB cap), reached only after Eastmoney's refusal.
  Its residuals: a trial account's refresh token dies with the trial (the stand-in then refuses
  "凭据被拒"); whether 问财 serves an open session's numbers live is unmeasured (the file stamps the
  session it asked for and its receipt time); `涨跌幅:前复权` is a total-return change on an
  ex-dividend day; a board's change is its members' equal-weight mean, not an index's; 同花顺's
  concept names differ from Eastmoney's, so a stand-in day's candidates do not compare name for
  name with another day's; and the named list of non-theme tags (`wencai-excluded.mjs`) was
  compiled from the 389 names of one day.
- **R42 — A run's evidence files are not in git.** `.gitignore` holds
  `strategies/*/analysis/*/evidence-*.json` (A26; `tests/lunhui-ignore.test.ts`), and a write's
  crash leftovers, `*.pending.json` and `*.tmp` under a run (R39): `run.json`, with
  every evidence file's sha256 and size, `metrics.json` and the module artifacts are
  tracked. A clone, or the machine after the files are deleted, holds the hashes and cannot rebuild
  a context or re-check an artifact's citations; the evidence lives only on the machine that froze
  it, about 2 MiB a run at most.
- **R43 — The runs card reads a tree Gravit's sessions can write.** `readAnalysisRuns` re-checks
  `analysis/` and each run directory (`stillAt`) just before its reads and opens every file
  `O_NOFOLLOW` with one link, but the check and the read are still two calls, so a writer inside
  the strategy tree can race them, as in R39; a run skipped mid-read leaves no mark on the card.
  `accepted` means `run.json`'s `artifacts[]` names the module and its file is present, readable
  and an object within its cap — the record a module submit appends after its rename
  (`writeArtifact`), so a crash between the two leaves a file no reader takes, and a retry is
  accepted; `lunhui_read_run` marks `accepted` by the same record; an unnamed or unreadable
  artifact is left out of the card with no hint (`lunhui_read_run` lists it unaccepted);
  `latestRun` is chosen among the 50 listed runs.
- **R44 — A context read seals the run, and the reads a submit needs live in one process.** Any
  caller may read a module's context (A23 fences only the submit). Until 2026-11-02 A23's
  `NOT_A_ROLE` gate admitted any unseeded child — a plain spawn child included, since the header
  could not tell a role child from one — so "Gravit never submits" held for its root and its forks
  only; *that half closed 2026-11-02* with the dsh 0.2.1-rc.5 upgrade: each role child composes its
  own `role-<id>` preset (PLAN D20/B1) and `callerIsRole` (`face/plugins/lunhui/lib/errors.mjs`) also
  requires the header's `agentPreset` to start `role-`, so a plain `subagent` child of Gravit's,
  which joins `gravit`, is `NOT_A_ROLE` (`lunhui-rows.test.ts`, `callerIsRole`'s cases). The first read seals the run: a Gravit session that reads a context before its last freeze, or a read the operator
  prompts by hand, ends that run's evidence (`RUN_SEALED` after it), and the protocol's order is
  the only guard. Each read counts against its module's ten calls whether its build succeeds or
  not. `READ_FIRST` rests on two in-memory records — the service's set of
  `<strategy>/<run>/<module>` reads and each module definition's map of digests — the set never
  pruned for the process's life (a key a read), the map dropping a module's digest (every evidence
  item of the module's sources) only at its accepted submit, neither persisted: a face restart,
  or a module row reloaded while the backbone lives, makes the next submit `READ_FIRST`, and the re-read costs one more call; a run whose budget is spent then
  cannot take that module at all. The digest a submit is checked against is the latest read's, and
  the evidence files under it are read again at each read, so a hand edit of a sealed run's
  evidence between two reads (R39's class) changes what the second validates against while
  `snapshot_id` stays the seal's. Recorded, nothing built.
- **R45 — A module's hypotheses are the tree's paraphrase, held in code.** Each contract's
  `HYPOTHESES` (`lib/contracts/<module>.mjs`) restates one of `strategies/cn-market/THESIS.md`'s
  three hypotheses in the tree's own Chinese words with the manuscript's paragraph ids, never its
  text (D10′, the corpus stays out of git); the artifact's `hypotheses_version` hashes that string.
  The two are copies, not one source: an edit of `THESIS.md` reaches no context until the contract
  is edited to match, and the contract tests check the paragraph ids and the seven states, not the
  wording. A paraphrase can drift from the manuscript it cites, and nothing in the tree can check it
  against the corpus. The hints and repair texts are the tree's own as well. Recorded, nothing
  built.
- **R46 — A strategy module reads other runs without their lock, by design.** `readSealedRun`
  (the cited `cn-market` run), `previousArtifact` (the strategy's earlier `mode.json`) and
  `readThesis` take no mutex: a sealed run's evidence no longer changes, its `artifacts[]` only
  grows and an artifact lands whole by its rename, so the strategy run's own mutex is the only one
  held, and two runs never wait on each other. What that leaves: the cited run is read once, at the
  strategy module's read, so an artifact accepted on the market run afterwards reaches only a later
  read, and the submit never re-reads it; a hand edit of a sealed run's evidence or artifacts
  (R39's class) changes what the next strategy read shows while `market_snapshot_id` stays the
  seal's. The read seals the strategy run before it checks the cited run, so a refused cited run —
  `STALE_MARKET_RUN`, `MISSING_EVIDENCE`, `NO_SUCH_RUN` — still leaves the strategy run sealed,
  its quotes fixed; and a strategy run whose session is more than one trading day past every sealed
  market run can never pass A5, so the protocol has Gravit make a new sealed market run and, when
  the strategy run itself is stale, open a new strategy run. A run's freshness is the freeze's: a
  market run cited the next session is a day old by design (A5), and `lunhui_read_run`'s listing
  offers the newest five sealed runs without judging their session — the protocol has Gravit take
  the day's or the previous trading day's. Leader, reviewer and mode stand on one market run only
  because the reviewer's and the mode's reads compare the leader's `market_run`
  (`MISSING_EVIDENCE`) and the mode's gate compares the counterevidence's; a read of the leader
  alone cites whatever run it is given. The previous card is sought among the strategy's last 50 earlier runs, by run id and
  `opened_at`; an older card is never graded. Recorded, nothing built.
- **R47 — The strategy table and the mode's terms are held in code.** `MODE_FOR` in
  `lib/contracts/mode.mjs` maps two directory names, `lunhui-s01-repair` and
  `lunhui-s02-rotation`, to `S01` and `S02`; `REQUIRED_PRECONDITIONS`, the no-source list, the
  admitted states and `R_FAMILIES` are constants beside it, the tree's copies of strategy-spec
  §3–§4 and §6 and of the theses. A renamed strategy directory concludes `WAIT` only, and a new
  strategy registers nothing until the contract is edited; an edit of a thesis reaches none of the
  rules (THESIS.md is not validated, D13′). The mode reads THESIS.md's `## Falsification` section as
  text it shows the role, at most 1,500 bytes: an operator's longer section is cut from the end,
  and the E4 paragraph sits last in each of the two theses (S01's section 1,445 bytes, S02's 1,421
  today), so it is the first text a longer section would push out of the context. As with R45, a
  copy can drift from the documents it restates. Recorded, nothing built.
- **R48 — Only `S01` can register, and nothing it registers is confirmed.** `S02` is refused while
  its catalyst has no source (E4: an announcements freeze, a new egress host, a later plan), so a
  `lunhui-s02-rotation` run concludes `WAIT`. `S01` needs the run's counterevidence artifact
  accepted `OK`, with an `items` array and the mode's own `market_run` (A22), which `cn-reviewer`
  writes through the `lunhui-review` row since plan 4; the strategy smoke registers one on Friday
  and grades it on Monday on fixtures, and no live run has yet. Even a registration never
  confirms: its minute confirmation is `unmet: no source` for want of minute bars. Until the first
  live `S01`, the runs card's review line stays empty on a real face. Recorded; the announcements
  source is §10 item 21.
- **R49 — The reviewer's review is bounded by what its context and the mode's show.** The
  reviewer reads the artifacts' bounded views (four claims at most, 120 characters, three ids a
  list), never the artifacts whole, so an item it raises against a claim it did not see cannot
  exist, and an item may be against only a module whose view was shown. The mode, in turn, shows
  each item's first 120 of its 160 characters, its `kind`, `against` and three of its ids: a
  long item's tail is the reviewer's file's alone, and the mode answers items by id. The mode's
  context has about 1.1 KB to spare at every input's maximum (30,233 of 30,720 bytes, measured with
  ASCII-heavy items); items written in 4-byte characters could take 1.5–2 KB of it, and then the
  environment view and next the theme's are skipped — the theme's makes the run `NOT_EVALUABLE`,
  never an `S01` over an unseen theme. The reviewer runs before the mode by the protocol's order
  alone: a review read before the market run's sentiment was accepted is `NOT_EVALUABLE` and
  leaves the mode `WAIT`. `evidenceRequired` names every listed source missing when the context
  shows no evidence row, even one that was frozen — the status is right, the missing list
  imprecise. The rebuilt example could in principle cite an artifact pruned later (a `WAIT`
  example cites none). The strategy smoke's Monday grade re-reads Friday's quote bytes under
  Monday's session (one fixture set), so the next-day grade is not tested on new prices.
- **R50 — The seat's key in the agent box.** Under `docker compose` (§3.9) the Account's home —
  the desk's seat keys, `agent-wallets`, the paper book, the owner-device registry — is the volume
  `account-home`, which the agent box does not mount, so Gravit's shell there cannot read it. The
  seat's own key does not move with it: the seat is the face's child, so `seats/gravit.json` lives
  in the agent box's `seat-home` volume, and a shell turn there can still read it and sign at the
  Account's door with no Gate 2 card, exactly as on the host (R1, R34). The Account's own card on
  every seat write and the limits the operator signs stand against that, as today; the split
  narrows the charter's D17 R1 to the seat's key, it does not close it. Closing it means moving the
  seat into the Account box behind an HTTP MCP transport instead of stdio (§10 item 25). On the
  host dev loop nothing changed: the seat's key is in `~/.buyer-agent-demo`, readable by a shell
  turn (R34).
- **R51 — The two widened `Host` fences are DNS-rebinding defences, not authentication.** The
  Account's `PORTFOLIO_HOSTS` admits `account:4820` beside loopback, and the face's `/data` fence
  (`isTrustedDataRequest`) stays Host-based when `FACE_BIND` widens the face's listener (in the
  box, to the container's own address since 2026-11-02; `0.0.0.0` before, which dsh 0.2.1 refuses).
  A peer that reaches either port can send `Host: 127.0.0.1` and pass: at the Account, every read
  and the routes the door does not authorise; at the face, every `/data` route (`/api` still wants
  the cookie). Writes are authorised by the owner's signed envelope and the seat's key at the
  Account's door, unchanged. In the compose topology this is fine: the only peers on the private
  `gravit` network are the three boxes; the face's port is published on the host's loopback only,
  and since 2026-11-01 the Account's is published to nobody (`expose`, no `ports`), so its only peer
  is the agent box; the market's (`MARKET_HOSTS`, `market:4821`) is published to nobody either, its
  peers the account and agent boxes, and it holds no key and takes no write.
  Set on the host Mac, `PORTFOLIO_BIND=0.0.0.0` or a `FACE_BIND` naming a LAN address is a LAN exposure; the
  READMEs say both are for the box only (`account/README.md` "In the box", `face/README.md` "The
  three-box drill"). The hardening — a peer-address check on `req.socket.remoteAddress`, or a token
  for non-loopback peers — is §10 item 26, not built (it would change the door's admission, which
  the copy keeps as is).
  Recorded, nothing built.
- **R52 — An old composed answer draws the run as it is now.** A composed message keeps the run,
  the module names and Gravit's words, not the view it was checked against: the page rebuilds the
  view from the run's files whenever it reads it (§5.3), and no artifact carries an acceptance time
  to pin the answer to. `ALREADY_SUBMITTED` keeps one artifact a module a run today, so the view
  moves only when a run's files change after the answer — an artifact edited on disk, against
  `GRAVIT.md`'s rule, or a future re-submit path — and then a module re-submitted later on the same
  run draws its newer text in an old answer, under a summary the check confirmed against the older
  one. The modules an answer reads are fixed at its call (`presentModules`), so a module accepted
  on the run after the answer stays out of it. Recorded, nothing built.
- **R53 — One owner device, and a lost browser profile, leave the Account with no way back but
  `--fresh`** (charter D18). Since the Account's own page retired (2026-11-01) the face's page is its
  only page, and a new owner device is let in only by an owner device that already signs
  (`convertToMultiSigUser`, Settings › Devices on the face); the pairing code is printed only while
  the Account has no owner. With a single device, losing that browser profile — its site data cleared,
  the profile deleted, the machine replaced — leaves no device that can sign and no code: the only
  way back is `npm run account -- --fresh`, which throws away the owner, the venues, the agents and
  their limits. Signing the last device out on purpose is different: the Account then has no owner
  and prints a new code. The mitigation is a second face browser kept paired (another browser or
  profile on `127.0.0.1:3090`, let in from the first one's Settings › Devices) — the owner drill
  recommends one — and `npm run account:owners` says how many owner devices the running Account has.
  Recorded, nothing built: no export of the key, no recovery code (the Account's posture).
- **R54 — A wallet challenge without the face's origin names the retired page.** `POST
  /api/account/wallet/challenge` builds the EIP-4361 sentence's domain and URI on
  `x-gravit-face-origin` when the face sends it (the proxy always does) and otherwise on the
  Account's own `Host`, `<protocol>://<host>/account` — a URI that answers `NO_PAGE` since the page
  retired. Unlike `signin/start` it is not refused without the header: only the face's proxy calls it,
  the sentence connects nothing (connecting is still the owner's signed `connectVenue`), and the
  proof checks the signature, not the URI. A local program that asks without the header gets a
  sentence naming a 404 address. Cosmetic; recorded, nothing built.

---

- **R55 — The desk's P0 assumes one desk-enabled face per home, and has not yet met launchd.** A
  `boot` while a run is open marks that run `lost` (`runsOf`), so a second desk-enabled face on
  the service's home would read as the service's run lost; and two dsh processes on one harness
  home are unexamined, so a second face runs on a scratch home with `FACE_DESK=0` (§4.6,
  `face/README.md` "Run as a service"), never on the service's. A `kill -9` inside an append can
  leave `events.jsonl.lock` behind; `withFileLock` takes a lock over only while its recorded pid
  is gone, so once that pid is reused every append waits its 2 s and fails with one stderr line
  until the lock is removed by hand. `withFileLock` also never takes over a record that is not a
  pid line (`holderExited`, dsh-atomic-write), so a kill between the lock's create and its pid
  write leaves an empty lock that wedges the appends the same way. Both exits in `main.ts` end
  the desk's run first, so that wait delays every teardown by its 2 s; on the fail-loud path it
  can spend `installFailLoud`'s whole 2 s release bound, so the process may exit before the room
  engine, the data routes and the tree are released. A face running code from before the desk —
  any checkout the merge has not reached — answers 404 at `/data/desk/status`, so
  `npm run service -- status` says `not answering`, and `url` marks the log's URL as maybe the
  previous run's, while that face holds the port (`install`, `start` and `restart` still refuse
  it: there any HTTP answer counts); when a face that does answer the route is not launchd's
  job, its pid differing, `status` says so in one line. The 10 s that `stop`, `restart`,
  `install` and `uninstall` wait for launchd to let go of the job may be shorter than launchd's
  default exit timeout (system-defined, unmeasured until the drill; the plist sets no
  `ExitTimeOut`), and the face's teardown is unbounded: a face that takes longer than 10 s to
  exit is reported as a failure, though it stops — and `restart` then starts nothing, so the
  service stays stopped until `start` or the next login. Under launchd node is its own
  responsible process, and macOS guards `~/Desktop`, `~/Documents` and `~/Downloads` per app:
  for a checkout there (the operator's is in `~/Desktop`) the first start may raise a privacy
  prompt, possibly at a login nobody watches, or fail with `EPERM` in `face.err.log` every 30 s;
  `install` warns, and cannot tell whether access was granted. And no launchd call has run for
  real — the tests drive a fake `launchctl` — so the desk drill (§7.4) is the first. Since plan
  B1a the phone is one more thing a second face must not share: the account polls Telegram once,
  and reading its inbox changes nothing, so a desk-enabled face reading the same account, on any
  home, gets every text the service gets and answers it too, each face's cursor its own (until
  B1a the second face was a second poller of the bot's token, splitting the updates in 409s). Nothing enforces one
  desk-enabled face per home — it is the operator's discipline (`CLAUDE.md`, `face/README.md`): a
  second face started without `FACE_DESK=0` on the service's home interleaves its `boot` lines, so
  the live run reads as lost; it cannot resume the service's desk session, which dsh holds under a
  cross-process lock, so it records a `desk-session` of its own, and the two faces then hand the
  conversation back and forth at every post; and it answers the phone's texts beside the service.
  The desk's P2 added no lease: a second desk-enabled face on the home ticks
  the standing orders too, and the firing ledger's once-only `started` lets one of the two run
  each firing, the other logging `another face on this home started <key>; this one does not run
  it` (R66); the rest of this residual stands.
- **R56 — The desk's cwd sits on dsh's instruction chain; the face holds it, not the sandbox**
  (charter D25). dsh reads `GRAVIT.md` and `GRAVIT.local.md` in every directory from the project
  root — the nearest `.git` — down to a session's cwd, and in the directories between the cwd and
  any file a tool touches; a `.git` makes a directory a project root, whose `.dsh/skills` and
  `.agents/skills` are skill roots. The desk's sandbox lets it write its cwd, and the journal is
  ignored by git, so a file planted there would steer every later desk turn and no diff would
  show it. Two lines in the face hold it. The desk guard's write check (`desk-tools.ts`,
  `installDeskGuard`) denies, before it runs, a desk agent's `write`, `edit` or
  `str_replace_editor` (any command but `view`) whose path names one of the five (`FENCE_NAMES`,
  case-folded) — a file the turn wrote would steer the rest of that same turn, which no check at
  a turn's start can see — with a deny-only `tools.guard`
  behind its listener, so no later `tools/pre-execute` listener can talk it out of a denial. The
  same check holds the files other tools obey, which dsh's names do not cover: any dot-file below
  the root (`the desk never writes dot-files: <name>`) — a `desk/journal/.gitignore` holding `!*`
  would make git list the journal, the operator's book, for the next `git add -A` (charter D24),
  and an ignore file's negation would lift ripgrep's hidden-file skip (R57) — and any `CLAUDE.md`,
  `CLAUDE.local.md`, `AGENTS.md` or `AGENTS.override.md` below it, case-folded
  (`the desk never writes <name>: another agent reads it`), which the operator's coding agents load
  from the folder they work in, a shell behind them, and which git would never show in the ignored
  journal. The fence (`desk-session.ts`) refuses every desk turn while one of the five sits directly
  in `desk/` or anywhere under the journal, a `.dsh` or `.agents` sits at the repository root, any symlink
  sits in the fenced tree (`desk/` and the journal lstatted themselves), or an entry cannot be
  read; the conversation checks before it opens a turn for a post, and the supervisor at every
  `turn/start`. What they do not hold: the root `GRAVIT.local.md` — the operator's machine-local
  overlay, ignored by git — is read by every desk turn and writable by a workbench session at the
  repository root (R9); it is not fenced, because it is a legitimate operator file. A file another
  session plants while a desk turn runs steers the rest of that turn: the fence checks at its
  start. A turn the browser or a background job's notice opens is checked at its `turn/start` and
  cut, not refused before it opens, so its first model request may already carry a planted text
  (the desk has no job tools, so no wake comes today; P3 evaluates a pre-step reject hook when
  wakes exist). The write check judges names, not where a link points — any symlink already
  refuses every turn, and the desk cannot make one — and never the checkout's own ancestors (it
  judges a path's names below their common ancestor with the repository root, and as spelled; a
  desk session whose own cwd sits under a fence name writes nothing), so a root that sits under a
  fence-named directory leaves that directory's other subtrees unjudged (no production checkout
  has one). Its root is taken as given: a relative one is accepted, not refused (production passes
  `process.cwd()`, absolute and physical); `deskWriteDecision` lets a `view` with a cwd that is no
  string through, which the installed guard never hands it (it throws first, and denies); and the
  case of a cwd above the root is in its comment, not its tests. On a case-sensitive
  volume the fold refuses a few names dsh would not read: the safe side. Two everyday trips, both
  intended: an Emacs lock file (`.#name`, a dangling symlink) refuses every desk turn while a
  journal note has unsaved edits, and a root `.agents/` or `.dsh/` adopted for another tool
  refuses the desk while it is there. Pinned by `desk-guard`, `desk-session`,
  `desk-conversation`, `desk-smoke` (the threat on a real request) and `phone-smoke`'s canary (until plan B1a `telegram-smoke`'s).
- **R57 — The desk reads only inside the repository, held by its guard; what it reads still goes to
  DeepSeek** (charter D27). An unattended desk turn reads text nobody vetted — a forwarded message,
  a web page, a filing — so `DESK_ALLOW` names no `bash` and no `job_*` (a security ruling during
  P1, overturning the spec's §2 default that the sandboxed shell stays): such a turn must not read
  the key files and reach the network. The sandbox fences writes, not reads (R3a), so the read
  side is the desk guard's (§4.2): its read check denies a `read`, `read_image`, `grep`, `glob`
  or `str_replace_editor` that reaches outside the repository — where the volume says the path
  lands, so a symlink cannot carry it out — or names a `.env`, `.env.<anything>` or `.git`, or
  any other dot-file below the root — the checkout the service runs from holds `.mcp.json`,
  `.claude/settings.local.json` and `.codex/`, formats made to carry tokens, and the
  `.claude/worktrees/*` checkouts — or searches dot-files; its secret check denies any call whose
  arguments carry a key's value from the face's environment, to DeepSeek's search, to an MCP
  server or to a file; the bridge redacts every such value from what reaches the phone. `glob`
  lists names and reads none. The secret check is a backstop, not the line: it finds a value as
  it is, as JSON writes it inside a string and as `encodeURIComponent` encodes it (an upper-case
  `%3A`), and misses a lower-case `%3a`, a base64 spelling and a value split across arguments; the
  read check, which keeps the key files out of the turn, is what holds. What remains: a key kept
  in a file whose name carries no key and no dot — a `credentials.json`, a note — or one an MCP
  tool returns still reaches DeepSeek in the tool result, since nothing filters a desk agent's
  tool results today; and it reaches the phone too unless the face's environment holds that
  value. That filter is a follow-up, not missing infrastructure: dsh-tools 0.2.0-rc.2 already runs
  a `tools/post-execute` waterfall that can replace a result's content (`lib/index.js` about
  3503-3529; `lib/types/index.d.ts` 70, 465), so the face could redact its secret values from
  every desk agent's tool results (§10, item 5). The realpath cannot see a hard link inside the
  repository to a key file elsewhere, and a symlink swapped between the check and the tool's open
  is not seen: the desk can make neither, having no shell and its writes kept to its journal and
  the temp areas, but another session could. Two refusals are false positives, left as they are:
  a spilled image attachment, which `read_image` would read from a spill directory the allowance
  gives only `read` and `grep`; and a spill root configured elsewhere (`spill-local.root`), which
  the allowance does not know. And the dot-file rule rests on ripgrep's
  behaviour as measured with rg 15.0.0, the binary dsh packages: a `--glob` lifts ripgrep's
  hidden-file skip, and its `*`, `?`, `[...]` and `{...}` all match a leading dot (`*.alpaca`
  searched `.env.alpaca`), so a `grep` include led by a wildcard is refused — `*.md` included,
  since no rule that admits `*.md` stops `*.alpaca` — while `glob`, whose pattern lists names, is
  refused only a dot-led one; a ripgrep that behaves otherwise changes what the rule must be. A
  `grep` with no include is kept off hidden files by ripgrep itself — unless an ignore file it
  reads whitelists one: a negation (`!.env.alpaca`, or a doublestar that ends one) in a
  `.gitignore`, `.ignore` or `.rgignore` in the tree it searches, or in a directory above it,
  which ripgrep reads too, lifts the skip for what it matches. `desk-guard` keeps the repository's
  tracked ignore files free of such a negation; an untracked one, git's own exclude files and those
  above the repository it does not see. The desk cannot write one — each is a dot-file — but
  another session could. The ruling's cost: the desk cannot compute with a shell or read outside
  the repository — a desk session whose cwd lies outside it can read nothing there — nor read any
  dot-file in it, and `str_replace_editor`'s writing commands outside it, `/tmp` included, are
  refused too. Adding `bash` back is a charter §8 trigger (the desk's preset given a shell);
  widening its reads past the repository, or to its dot-files, is the operator's decision too,
  taken with eyes open.
- **R58 — The phone: one token, one operator id, outbound only** (charter D20). Since plan B1a the
  token is the account's, in `<account home>/credentials/networks/telegram.json` (`0600` in a `0700`
  folder), a key file like the others (R1): readable by a workbench session's shell turn on the host
  (never by the desk, whose read check keeps it inside the repository; under compose the account's
  home is a volume the agent box does not mount), and by the host watchdog, which uses it only to
  say the account is down. Whoever holds the token can message the operator as the bot — only the
  operator, since no other chat has started it — and can read what the operator sends, by calling
  `getUpdates` or by setting a webhook of its own; the account sees either only as a 409 and
  `conflictAt` in its status (the face's `<network> conflict at …`). The account admits by the bound
  operator's user id in their private chat, so a lost or compromised phone that is still signed in
  to the operator's account can chat with the desk — have it read inside the repository, write in
  its journal and spend tokens — and pause it, and rotating the token does not stop it. The remedy
  is to end that device's session from another device (Telegram → Settings → Devices), or to
  Disconnect… Telegram in Account › Identity until then (a signed `disconnectNetwork`, since plan
  B1b); rotate the token at @BotFather only when the token itself leaked, and
  connect again. Every other sender is dropped, never answered, and counted in Not you with no
  text. A provider's authentication error can carry a masked key fragment (`****abcd`) into the
  failed line the phone gets — the face's redactor knows whole values only — as it already reaches
  the ledger and the browser. The account stores a text in its inbox before Telegram's offset moves,
  and the face moves `inbox.cursor` only once the text's post has settled — after the desk session's
  log was flushed — so a crash on either side takes the text again, and the desk answers it once,
  by its key (spec §16 H3; its edges are R94). A revoked token fails every poll (401), a mistyped
  one too (404), and the account polls on: its status, and the face's phone line, say `poll failing
  since <time>: <reason>`, redacted, until a poll answers. The account's outbox keeps 100 at most,
  each with its kind, and drops at the flush what quiet hours would hold now or what waited more
  than 12 hours. The face's own fetches — to the account on loopback for the phone, to the market
  for the desk's quotes — and the account's to `api.telegram.org` pass no egress policy: the policy
  layer shapes the model's tools and the rows' uploads (§4.3), there is no proxy policy (PLAN D10),
  and nothing but the code limits the hosts either process reaches (the account's Bot API base is
  `api.telegram.org`, or `ACCOUNT_TELEGRAM_API` only on `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`; Slack's `slack.com/api`, or
  `ACCOUNT_SLACK_API` only on `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`, and its socket only on `wss://<name>.slack.com`).
- **R59 — The desk's switch and conversation, at their edges.** `npm run desk` acts on the harness
  home its shell resolves, not the one the installed plist names; with a home set elsewhere the
  two can differ. A pause and a resume take `OFF.lock` for up to 2 s, so a resume can time out
  while the ledger's own lock is contended, with a line naming the lock; a lock left by a killed
  holder whose pid has since been reused stays until it is removed by hand, while deleting `OFF`
  still lifts the pause. A conversation that `/new` replaced stays live — the browser may hold it
  — and once its last turn ends nothing supervises it: a turn the browser opens there has no
  deadline, no fence check and no record. A cut cuts one turn: the phone's `/stop` and the
  deadline cancel the turn under way keeping the inbox, and send each text queued behind it again,
  so it is answered (`cancelKeepingQueue`; dsh's `keepInbox` alone keeps a queued text but answers
  it only when something else wakes the agent, measured in `desk-smoke`); the fence's cut keeps
  the inbox without that, so a queued text waits for the next post, which the fence refuses first;
  steering input waiting for the next step (a browser's) is kept and not sent again, as dsh's own
  stop leaves it. A phone text in flight at a restart: since spec §16 H3 a face that died (a crash,
  `kill -9`, launchd's `SIGKILL` past its exit timeout) leaves its texts in the desk session's
  durable inbox, and the next boot answers a cut phone turn with one line and wakes what was queued;
  a face stopped gracefully loses its inbox to dsh's teardown, so its dispose writes the queued
  phone texts and the phone turn under way to the ledger first (`desk-carry`), and the next boot
  posts the texts again, marked `carried over a restart`, and sends the cut turn the restart line
  (R93). A post still pending at its 30 s bound
  when the bridge goes queues the slow line, which the next boot sends late. A `deadlineFor` answer that is not finite is ignored without a line (P1 passes none;
  P3's is a constant), and `deskDeadlineMs`, which shortens every desk turn's deadline, is a test
  seam `main.ts` never passes. Two pause-switch cases are pinned only through others: `writeOff`'s
  expired-pause guard (any duration outlasts an expired pause) and the ledger of a touched `OFF`.
  A live desk
  session re-selected to another preset in the browser before its first turn passes the header
  check, which reads the preset the session was created with (low); a mismatched cold session is
  resumed under the desk's setup for a moment before the check disposes it (harmless). With a
  desk turn under way, shutdown takes up to about
  7 s more — 2 s for a cut agent to go idle, 5 s for a start, post or renew to settle — under the
  20 s launchd is commonly said to allow before SIGKILL (its documented default is
  system-defined and unmeasured, above), but counted against the 10 s R55's commands wait. A desk
  session nobody prompted from the browser gets no LLM title, its messages carrying no `user` source;
  gravit-ui lists desk sessions as it lists any (the Desk panel that filed them apart left with the
  old client; P3 ported its status to gravit-ui as Markets › Desk, `js/host/desk-view.js`, which
  lists no sessions).
- **R60 — The face runs from a tree its agent sessions can write, and launchd restarts it
  unattended** (charter D26). The face's own code — `face/src`, `face/plugins`, `face/scripts`,
  `scripts/` — lives in the workspace, which a workbench session at the repository root writes
  with no card (R9); the desk session cannot without an approved card, its sandbox fencing the
  journal. A change takes effect at the face's next start, and the LaunchAgent starts it
  unattended after a crash (`KeepAlive`, P0), so an edit nobody reviewed can go live with nobody
  watching. Nothing pins the face's code; review and the diff are the hold. The pin the desk's P2
  puts on a standing order's script producer (R63), and the one the spec's P3 puts on its filings
  producer, narrow the window only for the scripts they pin, which run on each invocation; they
  do not close it for the face itself. The market clock is the face's own code since 2026-11-01
  (R64), under this same hold.
- **R61 — The desk's roster at its edges.** `mcp__*__<raw>` admits a same-named tool from any MCP
  server, so a second server with an `earnings` tool would join the desk's roster (`desk-smoke`
  asserts one server per wildcard on its tree). And the two desk tools are per agent, given at
  `agent/created` and by the install's sweep, so a blank live session switched to `gravit-desk`
  through the `agentPresets/select` Remote gets neither — no event fires; the face client never
  calls `select`, and both tools only read. The desk guard is not per agent: it judges a call by
  the preset composed when the call runs, or by the session header, so such a session's writes,
  reads and secrets are judged all the same. A bot composition edited by hand can opt into
  `plugins/bot.js`'s `maskOnly` and so speak as Gravit, with Gravit's persona under its own mask;
  it shows in the row `bot-presets.ts` renders (`rowFor`), and nothing refuses it. And Gate 2's
  check that an order tool nothing registered is refused is asserted in Gravit's scope only: the
  global view's answer follows from the registry and is not asserted apart.
- **R62 — The desk conversation carries what it read into its later turns.** A desk turn reads
  text nobody vetted — a forwarded message, a web page, a filing — and that text stays in the
  conversation's history, with anything the turn put in its `todo_write` list, for every later turn
  of the same conversation until the phone's `/new` opens another. An instruction smuggled in once
  can steer the turns after it: this is the persistence a poisoned phone turn has, now that the
  guard denies it the instruction files, the dot-files and other agents' files. Neither the fence
  nor the guard sees history — it is what a long-lived conversation is. What holds: the desk
  contract (`dsh/profile/desk.md`) has the model treat such text as information, never as an
  instruction for later turns; the desk orders nothing (Gate 2, no order path from the phone); its
  guard holds every write and read; and `/new` leaves the history behind.
- **R63 — A standing order's script producer runs outside the sandbox with the market keys; the
  pin covers the script's bytes, not the installed packages it imports.** A firing's `scripts/<file>.py` is a child of the face process, not of a session,
  so no sandbox confines it, and its environment carries the market keys (`producerEnv`: `PATH`,
  `HOME`, `LANG`, `TZ`, `LC_*`, `APCA_*`, `ALPACA_*`, `ALPHA_*` and `GRAVIT_ROOT`; never
  `DEEPSEEK_*` or `TELEGRAM_*`, though since plan B1a the face reads no `TELEGRAM_*` at all). What holds it: the `scripts/*.py` rule (one file directly under
  `scripts/`, its real path inside it — `parseProducer`, `resolveScript`), that allow-list, `python
  -I` (no user site, no `PYTHON*` variable, no script directory on `sys.path`), and its pin: `arm`
  records the bytes' sha256, `checkFiring` checks them before the `started` (`producer-hash`, one
  line per change), and `runScriptProducer` reads them once more, refuses a mismatch unrun and runs
  a private copy of exactly those bytes from `$DSH_HOME/face/desk/run/`, so a script swapped in
  `scripts/` between the check and the exec never runs — no hash-then-exec window is left for the
  script itself. What does not hold: what the script imports. The rule since
  2026-11-01 is that nothing is imported from the tree: the repository holds no Python, and a
  future research package is installed into the producer's interpreter, never put on `sys.path`
  from the repository (`GRAVIT_ROOT` names the root for reading files; it is no import path). The
  installed package itself is not pinned: an upgrade of it changes what a pinned producer runs,
  with the market keys. More widely, the face's own code is
  writable by its sessions and takes effect at the next restart, which the LaunchAgent makes
  unattended (R60, charter D26). The private copy can still be raced by an unsandboxed process
  running as the operator: no sandboxed session can write `$DSH_HOME/face/desk/run/`, and such a
  process can read the keys anyway. A producer's process at its edges: it leads a process group of
  its own, and `SIGKILL` at its deadline reaches the whole group, so a process the script starts
  dies with it and one holding its stdout open no longer delays the report; a process that leaves
  the group (`setsid`) escapes it. An abort — the face's shutdown — cannot stop a script producer
  already running: it runs on to its own exit, or to its deadline's kill, which only a face still
  running sends. No script producer ships yet: the pre-close brief is `builtin:brief`, face code
  with nothing to pin.
- **R64 — The market clock is a rule table in the face's own code, as good as its rules.** The
  XNYS sessions come from `src/market-clock.ts` (since 2026-11-01; the Python clock and its
  pandas_market_calendars are gone): the fixed holidays with weekend observance, the Monday
  holidays, Good Friday by the Gregorian computus, Juneteenth from 2022, the 13:00 ET early closes,
  New York's offset by the US rule since 2007, and `XNYS_AD_HOC_CLOSURES`, a hand-kept table of
  one-off closures. A closure NYSE announces after the table's last edit (a day of mourning, a
  storm) is unknown until it is added: on that day an anchored order would fire into a closed
  market, and nothing fetches the exchange's notice. A rule NYSE changes (a new holiday, as
  Juneteenth was in 2022) needs an edit here. The tests check every 2026 and 2027 holiday and early
  close against a list hard-coded from the published schedule, the 2026 count (251 sessions), both
  DST changes on Sundays through 2027, and that every open falls at 09:30 New York time by Intl's
  own zone data. A failed ask - only a test's or a later clock's can fail - is asked again at most
  every 10 minutes, and meanwhile a date is answered from the newest window that still holds it,
  marked `stale`.
- **R65 — `standing.yml` and the pins, at their edges.** `standing.yml` is held by its placement
  in the harness home, outside every sandbox's writable roots, not by a check: a workbench
  session's shell turn under `DSH_PERMISSION_MODE=danger-full-access`, which drops the sandbox,
  can write it, and so can any process running as the operator; and nothing records an arming —
  the order's `armedAt` and pins are the record, and a hand edit leaves no trace but the file
  (charter D19). So can a workbench session's shell turn that the operator lets out of its
  sandbox through an approved escalation card: the card names the command, and the operator
  approving it is the only check. `arm` and `rearm` hash the files of the checkout they run from (`scripts/desk.ts`'s
  own repository), while the service's face reads its own checkout's: an order armed from a
  worktree pins that worktree's `STANDING.md`, and the service refuses it `hash` while the two
  differ — arm from the checkout the service runs (`face/README.md`). An order re-enabled after
  its anchor passed while it was disabled, or one found expired, is settled for that anchor in
  memory; across a restart in between, it can be reported missed for that day. The last
  `standing.yml` refusal and today's calendar failure are seeded from `events.jsonl` at boot, so a
  restart phones neither again — save one the pause held (`phoned: false`), which is phoned after
  the restart even if it went out before it (a duplicate, the safe side). A read error on
  `standing.yml` fails closed — even a transient `EMFILE` stops every order for that tick — and
  its line goes out once per code for the face's life, not each time it recurs (ruled in the P2
  fix wave). The ledger's failure lines are deduped in memory only.
- **R66 — The firing ledger, at its edges.** The key `<id>:<session date>` is consumed once per
  home: the `started` goes through `appendRecordOnce` under the ledger's lock, so of two faces on
  one home one runs a firing (R55). But the once-only append reads the current file alone. When
  one of the clock row's own appends rotates `firings.jsonl` (past 50 MB), the new file opens with
  today's `started`, `finished`, `interrupted`, `missed` and `refused` lines and the loaded
  orders' `expired` ones, and a firing's own appends — `producer`, `woke`, `finished` — carry the
  same, so a rotation followed by a restart reads each carried key as it ended. A rotation at
  the instant a `started` is written, by another face's append, can still split a key across two
  files. A `started` append that fails is a ledger failure — its line once, every firing stopped
  until the ledger reads again, the key's grace passing as no miss. At boot a `started` younger
  than its deadline and `FIRING_SLACK_MS` is judged only once it is that old, so a live firing on
  a second face on this home is not phoned cut off; a firing whose delivery went out and whose
  `finished` a crash then cut off is still reported `interrupted` (the order is deliver, then
  record). Earlier days are never back-filled, and an unreadable ledger stops every firing until
  it reads: the safe side.
- **R67 — The brief quotes the desk's own book, which a workbench session can write.**
  `builtin:brief` reads `desk/holdings.yml` and `desk/levels.yml` only, and quotes each near
  level's plan into an unattended turn whose text reaches the phone. A strategy's
  `strategies/<name>/levels.yml` sits in a directory the research sessions can write
  (`GRAVIT.md`'s never-edit rule is prose), so the brief does not read it (the spec's D22; the P2
  fix wave's I3): since P4 a strategy's levels reach the phone through that strategy's own report,
  which quotes them pinned (R82), and through the watch, unpinned (R84); the brief's `scope` says so. `desk/` itself is in the repository too: a
  root workbench session can write either file with no card (R9), so a planted plan of up to 300
  characters can still reach the turn; the loaders refuse control and direction characters, and
  the desk contract has the model treat quoted text as information, never as an instruction. The
  holdings are what the operator typed (charter D21) and its US prices are the Market's reads (D23). A linked
  directory above `holdings.yml` or `levels.yml` is followed: the file itself must be a regular
  file with one name, but a swap race on a directory above it remains. A brief past the 32,768
  characters a wake message quotes is cut, the tails of its near levels and refusals going
  first: its keys put every file error ahead of the long lists, though a book of many
  long-labelled holdings can still push the levels error past the cut, its holdings rows coming
  first. The snapshot asks for at most 200 symbols, one Market `explore` read each in six lanes;
  the desk's caps (60 holdings, 40 levels) keep under it today. Since P3 the watch's two blocks sit
  after the levels block, and a book at its caps already passes the cut, so there both are lost
  whole (R71).
- **R68 — The budget counts what the ledger holds.** `budget.dailyTokens` thresholds the day's
  `desk-turn` events as `events.jsonl` holds them, read before each firing and each phone post: a
  turn already under way is never cut by it, so a turn may overshoot the cap; a mid-day rotation of
  `events.jsonl` (past 50 MB) leaves the day's earlier turns in the rotated file, which nothing
  reads, so the day is undercounted and its `budget-spent` may be noted twice; a firing turn whose
  end the supervisor never reports — the watchdog's `no-turn`, or a cut turn that never unwinds —
  records no `desk-turn`, so its tokens miss the day's budget, and so, rarely, may a record the
  supervisor had queued at the instant the firing let it go; and an unreadable ledger reads as not
  spent — the budget fails open, its `error` on the status. A turn opened in the browser counts
  and is never refused. The cap is the operator's to set after the first measured week.
- **R69 — The disarmed-cycle line is not built** (ruling P2-17). The desk spec's §5.4 has a
  restart report a research cycle's goal that the restart disarmed, in the same line as the
  firings it cut off (`cycle in <channel> is disarmed; type continue in its session`); P2 did not
  build it. After a restart such a goal waits, disarmed, for the operator's next message in its
  session (R30), and nothing tells the phone.
- **R70 — The watch is polled, so an alert waits for its read.** A US crossing reaches the
  phone no sooner than the proxy's 20 s `explore` cache allows (the poll's cadence, `WATCH_US_POLL_MS`)
  plus the read, the judgement and Telegram's send; an A share's after up to 10 s
  (`WATCH_CN_POLL_MS`) plus up to five `quotes` reads of twelve pairs, each one Tencent read at
  the Account. A delayed US feed (`CBOE DELAYED`, Cboe's 15-minute quote) alerts on a print that
  old: the alert's stamp says so, and its latency (`latencyMs`, from the quote's `as_of`) shows
  it. Faster US alerts need a stream or a shorter cache, which the Market's read does not offer
  (charter D23); measured live in the desk drill's P3 half (§7.4).
- **R71 — A brief at the book's caps loses the watch's blocks whole.** The brief's `alerts` and
  `filings` blocks follow the whole levels block (a JSON key cannot sit inside it), and a book at
  its caps (60 holdings, 40 levels with long plans) already passes the 32,768 characters a wake
  message quotes, so the cut takes both blocks — counts and errors with them — before any levels
  refusal. Under the caps the cut takes the oldest filings, then the oldest alerts first (R67). The
  ledgers keep everything; `desk_state` and the Desk view still show today's alerts.
- **R72 — The previous close is the Market's own, and arrives late in New York.** A quote's
  `prev_close` is `price − change24h`, as the Market's read gives them, not a close the face
  reads; for an A share it is Tencent's previous close. A US `move_pct` key and a `gap` rule read
  only prints that carry one, and a Robinhood-priced row carries no `change24h` until Cboe's first
  trade, about 09:45 New York — so until then they are blind, a `gap` rule's 30-minute window can
  pass with no print it may judge (never said), and a level, which needs no previous close, is
  unaffected. The alert's `day:` line says `no previous close yet` when the print has none.
- **R73 — The A-share session's edges are the Market's phase and the Beijing clock.** A print is
  judged with the phase `trading` (`cn.phase`, the Market's word) inside 09:30–11:30 and
  13:00–15:00 Beijing, and the close print inside 15:00:00–15:00:30 whatever the phase. A close
  print Tencent stamps after 15:00:30 is not judged, and reaches the operator only through
  `desk_quotes` or a later brief; a phase the Market misreports at an edge moves the edge with it.
- **R74 — The XSHG table ends 2026-12-31, and extending it is a code edit.** `XSHG_CLOSURES` is
  the SSE's 2026 notices, copied (`face/src/xshg-clock.ts`); a later date is `uncovered`. Past it
  the watch polls every weekday as a 09:30–15:00 session and the Market's phase stands in for the
  calendar on whether the day trades, the bands and the close print still deciding which prints
  are judged; the phone gets one line a Beijing date, whose words now say just that (`judges A
  shares on the Beijing bands, the close print and the Market's phase for whether the day
  trades`; until the P3 final review's fix wave they named the phase alone). P4's anchors refuse
  a date past the table. When the
  SSE publishes 2027's notice, the table, `XSHG_COVERED`, the Lunhui plugin's calendar and the
  test that pins the copy move together.
- **R75 — A restart forgets what the ledger does not hold.** The watch's day is rebuilt from
  `alerts.jsonl` (`rebuildDay`, the last 36 hours): alerts, cooldowns, the hour's sends and the
  pending batch. What only memory held is lost: each key's last side and `as_of`, so after a
  restart the first judged print of a key is a first observation again — a level not past before
  the restart and past after it fires, labelled `gap`, though it crossed; a `gap` rule inside its
  30-minute window that judged a print without firing (only alerts leave records) can fire once
  more; and the repeat counts (`today.repeats`) restart at 0. `alerts.jsonl` rotates past 50 MB
  with nothing carried, so a rotation in mid-session followed by a restart rebuilds an empty day,
  and a `gap` already sent can fire a second time.
- **R76 — SEC's acceptance time is read as New York's wall clock despite its `Z`.**
  `acceptanceDateTime` ends in `Z` but carries New York's time (`edgar.ts`, ruling 9); were SEC's
  `Z` true UTC, every accepted time, the filing window's test and each alert's `accepted` would
  shift by 4–5 hours. The desk drill's P3 half checks one filing against its EDGAR index page.
- **R77 — A filings poll downloads whole documents.** Each poll reads every polled symbol's whole
  submissions JSON (up to 16 MiB each, `EDGAR_RESPONSE_MAX`; typically hundreds of KB), and the
  ticker map once per ET date, every 5 minutes from 07:00 to 20:00 ET — tens of MB a poll at the
  cap of 60 symbols, unmeasured until the drill records one poll's wall time and bytes. A filing
  recorded `suppressed: window` (accepted before 07:00 ET or on another date) starts no cooldown
  for its rule, live or rebuilt, so a pre-window 8-K cannot swallow an in-window one; two filings
  of one symbol inside the window 30 minutes apart still meet the cooldown. A symbol SEC first
  lists after its seed was empty sees its lookback filings as fresh; only a same-day one can ping.
- **R78 — The phone's ordering at its edges.** Telegram's per-chat flood limit can answer a 09:30
  burst — six alerts and a reply — with a 429; the account puts that send in its outbox, retried
  before its next poll or send, and the alert then has no message id, so its annotation arrives
  unthreaded (`replyTo` none) and late. Since spec §16 H1 an annotation runs in a desk session of
  its own and never waits on a phone turn; it waits only behind another pass's check, each bounded
  (R90). The watch's own lines (a file's load, a market blind, the
  cap) sent while the desk is paused are not sent and not retried; the alerts they accompany are
  in the ledger, recorded `suppressed: off`.
- **R79 — Two desk-enabled faces with one token both watch.** The lease (`watch.lease`) is per
  harness home: two faces on two homes, each with the desk on and the same account, each
  hold their own lease, poll the same book if they share the checkout, and send every alert twice
  (and both answer every text, R55). `FACE_DESK=0` on the second face is the hold (R55).
- **R80 — A send cut off by a shutdown is recorded undelivered, and never retried.** Once dispose
  has begun, each send of a pass not yet delivered gets a `delivered` record `{ undelivered: "the
  face shut down" }` on the send chain, with no deliver call, so the Desk view and the brief show
  it `undelivered` rather than `pending` (the P3 final review's fix wave). The send under way when
  dispose began finishes as it was and is recorded with its own result; one the 2 s bound cuts
  off has an `alert` record and no `delivered`, and stays `pending` for the rest of its day. The
  hour's count the rebuild restores counts each as sent, as the live count did.
- **R81 — Held lines across a restart, at their edges** (P4 ruling 7). A one-shot line the pause
  held is followed by a `phoned` record once its send resolves final — any answer but `paused`, a
  `deliver` that throws included, so it marks a send that ended, not proof the phone showed it — and
  the ledger's first read after a restart holds again the last three days' lines (`REHOLD_MS`) no
  `phoned` follows. At its edges: a held line can go twice across a crash between its send and its
  `phoned`; two faces on one home can both resend one, each at its own first read; a re-held
  refusal's line is built from its record, not re-checked, so a fence line can still say `Remove it.`
  after the file is gone; a rotation of `firings.jsonl` carries today's keys alone, so a held line
  older than today is lost with the rotated file, and a reported hash refusal is forgotten with it —
  yesterday's silent repeat of that refusal (`reported: false`, no line) can then rebuild a line at
  a restart; and a hash refusal the pause held and sent later is not counted phoned by the
  once-per-change dedupe, which seeds from `reported: true` alone, so after a restart the same change
  can be phoned once more. Each errs on the side of a second line.
- **R82 — A report turn can write anywhere in its strategy.** Its session is `workspace-write` with
  `strategies/<name>` as its cwd, so it can write `STANDING.md`, `levels.yml`, `status.yaml` and the
  rest, not only `reports/`. Held by the pins for its own firings — a changed `STANDING.md` or
  `levels.yml` refuses the next until `rearm` (charter D28) — and otherwise by the outside-reports
  line and git. That line is a directory diff of the strategy before and after the turn: a
  research session's edits made meanwhile are named as the firing's; a walk past 2,000 entries says
  `the listing stopped at <max> entries`, and so does a walk cut by a directory it cannot list,
  though it stopped short of the cap; and the walk skips the strategy's top-level `analysis/`, the
  Lunhui rows' (ruling 11), so a turn's write there goes unnamed.
- **R83 — An instruction file in a strategy steers every session in its channel.** The desk guard
  denies a report turn's write of the five fence names, of any dot-file and of a `CLAUDE.md` or
  `AGENTS.md`, as it does in the journal (R56). One another session plants — a research session in
  the channel has a shell — steers every session there, sessions with a shell and Gate 2's cards
  among them, until it is removed: the fence refuses that strategy's firings meanwhile with one
  line each, and a firing that finds one appeared during its turn says so once (`left <path>
  behind`).
- **R84 — What the report reads unpinned.** The watch reads every strategy's `levels.yml` unpinned
  (charter D28 recorded, not held, for it; the pre-close brief reads `desk/` only). The report
  quotes `status.yaml` unpinned, which both the strategy's research sessions and the report turn
  write. Its screen line trusts each `run.json`'s `sealed_at` and `session`, which the Lunhui rows
  write from the face but the strategy's own sessions can write too: a forged manifest can make
  the line say `ran`.
- **R85 — Each print on its own market, at its edges.** An `earlier` print has no previous close
  (ruling 1): the template has the message say `no print since` and its time. There is no A-share
  pre-open gap: at `open-90m`, 08:00 Beijing, no A share has printed that day (the call auction
  opens at 09:15), so its print is the previous session's `close`, its distance the close's and
  its `crossedSinceClose` null. The XSHG table ends 2026-12-31 (R74): A-share anchors past it are
  refused, and past it every cn print in a report reads `earlier` — only a US order holding A-share
  levels meets that.
- **R86 — The budget day is New York's** (`readBudget`). An A-share report at `open-90m` fires
  at 08:00 Beijing, 19:00 ET the evening before while New York keeps standard time, so a US day
  that spends the budget refuses the next Beijing morning's report.
- **R87 — A producer-only strategy order pins its `STANDING.md` and no `levels.yml`.** P2's `arm`
  has no `--file`, so a `--no-wake` order in `strategies/<name>` pins the strategy's `STANDING.md`
  too, and an edit to it refuses that order; it pins no `levels.yml` (`needsLevelsPin` wants a
  turn), and neither of the builtins runs there.
- **R88 — The desk file reads refuse what is not one regular file.** `readDeskFile` — the report's
  `status.yaml`, the firing's and `levelsPin`'s `levels.yml` — refuses a symlink, a FIFO and a
  hard-linked file (a link count other than 1), so an operator who hard-links a `levels.yml` gets
  a refusal; `status.yaml` is parsed from the guarded bytes, never opened twice. A linked directory
  above the file is still followed, as for the book (R67).
- **R89 — A calendar failure per market, at its edges.** A `calendar-error` event names its clock,
  not its market: at boot the seed matches an event to its market by the clock's name (`XNYS_CLOCK`,
  `builtin XNYS rules (…)`, and `XSHG_CLOCK`, `builtin XSHG table (…)`, differ today), so two clocks of
  one name would cross. The A-share market shows on
  an order's status line as a prefix (`standing <id>: market cn, <state>`), not a line or a cell
  of its own.
- **R90 — The annotation lane, at its edges** (spec §16 H1). Each pass's check is a desk session
  of its own, so every annotated pass leaves one more `gravit-desk` session in the store, none of
  which the phone's conversation or `/new` reaches. Checks run one at a time: a check waits behind
  the one before for up to 150 s of making, 150 s of turn and a minute of delivery, with no cut-off
  for staleness, so a burst of passes can land minutes late. A making that hangs past 150 s is
  answered with the not-annotated line, and the agent it later yields is let go silently, its
  dispose unbounded. The lane's dispose waits 12 s; what it cuts off goes on alone and can land after
  the conversation's dispose: a delivery under way, an agent's dispose, or a making that hangs across
  the shutdown. That making refuses with the not-annotated line rather than the shut-down one, and
  its 150 s timer keeps the process alive. A message of kind `alert` an older face left in the desk
  session's inbox is answered by the conversation as a plain turn, without the reply link.
- **R91 — A reply's context, at its edges** (spec §16 H1b). The watch resolves a replied-to message
  over the last 48 hours of `alerts.jsonl` in memory. A reply to an older message, to a message the
  watch did not send (a brief, a turn's answer), or arriving before this boot's watch has started,
  carries no context, and the operator is not told. The context is cut at 4,000 UTF-16 units with no marker; a
  cut can still split a grapheme cluster, never a surrogate pair. A record the resolver cannot read
  is skipped, and a resolver that throws drops the context with one line; the text still goes.
- **R92 — An alert a restart caught, at its edges** (spec §16 H2). A replay is held by `OFF` through
  `deliver` but ignores `MUTE`, so a muted alert caught by a restart reaches the phone late. A replay
  is never checked: its `annotate` is dropped. A crash between the lost line and its per-alert
  records repeats the line at the next boot. A `send` dated in the future (a clock set back) reads
  as young and is replayed.
- **R93 — A graceful stop carries the phone's part through the ledger, at its edges** (spec §16
  H3). `npm run service -- restart`, `stop`, a logout or any `SIGTERM` disposes the bridge first,
  then the conversation. dsh's teardown clears the desk session's inbox whatever the desk's own
  cancel keeps, and on 0.2.1-rc.5 closes the turn it aborts as `disposed` (measured on both dsh
  versions, `.superpowers/sdd/2026-11-02-desk-hardening/graceful-stop-measurement.md`; the final
  re-review's N1 and N2), so the conversation's dispose writes one `desk-carry` — the queued
  phone texts and the phone turn under way, read in the same tick as its shutdown cancels, so no
  turn claims a queued text between the two — and the next boot answers every carry no
  `desk-carried` names, oldest first: it posts the texts again under their keys and sends each cut
  turn the restart line once (a per-boot set besides the ledger), then writes one `desk-carried`
  per carry; a refusal stops it, leaving that carry and every later one for a later boot, and a
  malformed carry is skipped with one line, never stopping the boot. Its edges: a carry rotated
  out of `events.jsonl` before the boot is not read; a
  carried text loses its reply context and its Telegram message source (`{ kind: "telegram",
  carried: true }`), and its `at` only when this face had not posted it itself; a text a turn
  claims and logs while the dispose still asks which agents are busy is the carry's `cut`, read with
  the cancel; a text dsh has claimed for the open turn but not yet logged (dsh-agent-loop's
  `preStep` claims before it assembles the prompt and logs only after) is in neither the inbox nor
  the turn's name, so the conversation hears dsh-agent's `agent/inbox/claimed` on the root context
  and carries it as `queued`, to be posted again — and skipped, if it was logged after all; a boot
  whose fence check a dispose lands on wakes and carries nothing; a turn the tree wakes inside the dispose's idle wait (N2) finds the inbox the cancel
  cleared — and a turn so woken that tree dispose aborts gets the restart line through
  `cutPhoneTurn` on 0.2.1 (`disposed`) and through the resume's `interrupted` closer on 0.2.0, while
  one the desk's own shutdown cancel aborts is no cut there, which is why the snapshot and the cancel
  share a tick; a carry the pause or
  the budget refuses waits for a later boot, not for the resume or the budget's next day; and a
  carry whose `desk-carried` could not be written is answered again, its keys skipped but its cut
  line sent twice by a later boot. A `desk-carry` line is posted as the operator's words, so the
  ledger is an input with the operator's authority: the desk's own turns cannot write it (their
  sandbox is `desk/journal/` and the temp areas), but a shell-capable session on the same home can. The boot's work runs from `start()` alone: a session `start` could not open, resumed
  later by a post, is neither examined nor woken. A browser message left queued at a kill stays
  parked until something else wakes the agent. A cut turn's record has no usage, and its `t` is the
  boot's, not the turn's.
- **R94 — One text, one turn, at its edges** (spec §16 H3). A post that has not settled after 5
  minutes moves the cursor on (`inbox.cursor`; until plan B1a the offset, with an `unaccepted` record) with a log line, the phone told nothing.
  If the face then dies before that post lands, the text is lost unseen. Each such text costs its own
  5 minutes, and the order of the texts after it rests on the conversation's serial queue. The first
  keyed post after a boot reads the desk session's whole log, inside that queue. The keys seen are
  never dropped, though the session they belong to retires. A face whose context has no session
  persistence refuses every keyed text (`desk.ts` `withPersistence` finds it through `ctx.get`;
  nothing checks it at install).
- **R95 — The watchdog, at its edges** (spec §16 H4). It runs on the Mac's clock: asleep, nothing
  checks, and the desk's silence then still reads as nothing happened. It needs `npm run service --
  install` once after this round; a service installed earlier runs without it, and `status` prints
  no `watchdog:` line. It restarts once per outage: a face that stays down after its restart is
  named once and then left to launchd's `KeepAlive`. A degraded desk is never restarted. A `1` from
  launchd's own face closes an outage with `the desk answers again`; another face on the port
  (`OTHER_FACE`) during an outage neither closes it nor is counted, and nothing is said. A state file it cannot write means a silent watchdog,
  each run logging why. A reinstall boots the face out while the watchdog stays loaded, so a check in
  that window can restart a face the install is replacing. An unparsable `conflictAt` or `lastPollAt`
  reads healthy. A job unloaded during the 10 s wait reads `1` or `2`, not `3`. Since plan B1a its
  phone is the account's send (kind `watchdog`, which quiet hours never hold), and a line the account
  did not take is tried again at the next run, never queued by the face; the one line that says the
  account is down goes directly, from the token file in the account's home, tried at each run until
  the Bot API takes it. It checks the account and the market at the defaults unless `install`'s
  shell set `FACE_ACCOUNT_URL`, `FACE_MARKET_URL`, `FACE_ACCOUNT_HOME` or `BUYER_HOME` (the plist
  carries those four only); it never restarts either. An account that answers but refuses every
  send leaves the degraded and market lines unsent, one log line each run. `stop`, `uninstall`, or
  an unloaded job reads `3`, and it says nothing about it.
- **R96 — The retired bridge's files stay on disk** (plan B1a). An upgraded home keeps
  `$DSH_HOME/face/desk/telegram.offset`, `outbox.json` and `telegram.jsonl`, and its `.env` keeps
  `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` and `TELEGRAM_OPERATOR_ID`: nothing reads or writes any of them, and removing
  them is the operator's step (the token in `.env` is then a stale copy of a key, R1). A message the
  old outbox held when the face moved is never sent. `agents.ts` still scrubs `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`
  from every child the face spawns, for such an `.env`.
- **R97 — Two notices for one seat write.** Gate 2's card (§4.7) phones `Your call · … — waiting in
  Gravit` from the face, and the account's Guard card for the same write phones its own from the
  account (`cardNotice`, §3.9): the operator sees two notices, as they answer two cards. Both go as
  kind `card`, so the Cards waiting row and quiet hours hold both alike; the desk's `/pause` and
  `/mute` hold neither (they are not desk sends). A card asked before the phone client is built, or
  with the `mcp-account` row disabled, is one log line and no notice.
- **R98 — The phone's inbox is unauthenticated, behind the account's fence** (spec §5.5). The face's
  bridge trusts whatever answers `GET /api/account/identity/inbox` at the `mcp-account` row's URL,
  so a process that squats `127.0.0.1:4820` while the account is down could post texts into the desk
  conversation as the operator; such a turn still orders nothing (the desk has no order tool, Gate 2
  and D18 stand). It sits inside D10's boundary — a local process can already reach the account and
  the seat's key — and is held there. Not built: the bridge refusing a URL that is neither loopback
  nor the compose host, or pinning the bound bot seen in `/api/account/identity`. Two further edges:
  a fresh account home, or a ring that let a gap go, whose `last` is not below the cursor is passed
  over with no line; and a message the face's stricter check refuses is dropped silently, the cursor
  moving past it to `last`.
- **R99 — Slack, at its edges** (plan B2). **The two tokens** are a key file like Telegram's (R58,
  D20): whoever holds them can open the app's socket — the account sees only `conflictAt`, Slack
  spreading events across both — read the DM's history and post as the bot; the remedy is
  Disconnect… Slack, and deleting the app at api.slack.com/apps revokes both. **No threads:** Gravit answers top level in the DM, never
  in the operator's thread; a threaded text carries `replyTo: slack:<thread_ts>`, so a reply to an
  alert still finds its context, but the answer lands in the DM's main view (a map from `ts` to
  thread root would be needed, and the account keeps none). **A half-open socket:** the only
  liveness check is the 30-minute refresh (`SOCKET_REFRESH_MS`) — a socket that stops carrying
  frames without closing hears nothing for up to 30 minutes, and the next hello's backfill then
  takes what it missed, late. **Rate limits:** every hello reads `conversations.history` (and
  `conversations.replies` for each thread with a reply after the cursor, the last 24 h of history
  at most 5 pages); **a reply in an old thread while the account is down is not backfilled:** a
  reply written while no socket is open, in a thread whose parent is older than 24 h (or beyond
  those 5 pages of the last day), is never read — the backfill does not search that far for
  parents, and says so with one line only when the 5-page bound is hit; Slack's limits on those methods for a non-Marketplace app can slow a backfill,
  which then fails, backs off and runs again from the same cursor. **One workspace:** one Slack
  binding, one app, one DM; a second workspace is a second connection the account does not hold.
  **Enterprise Grid** is untested: its org-wide user ids and shared channels may not read as the
  `<team>:<user>` ids the account signs. Token rotation (`xoxe-` refresh tokens) is not built: a
  rotated token is a Disconnect… and a fresh Install app…. A workspace's owners can export DMs on
  some plans: the drill asks for a workspace where the operator is the only person, or one whose
  owners they trust. The watchdog's fallback to Slack reads the bot token only when
  `telegram.json` is absent; a present but unreadable Telegram file does not fall back, and the
  account-down line then waits for the next run.
- **R100 — The attachments, at their edges** (the dsh UI port's plan 4). A draft's files live in the
  page's memory only: a reload loses them, and a deleted conversation keeps its draft's blobs until
  the page goes. The face's search index does not index attachment names, so a message's files are
  found by its words alone. Files can be picked, pasted or dropped while a modal (a sheet, a
  drawer) covers the composer, and they join the draft under it. A folder dropped from Finder
  becomes a file record whose upload fails (`Upload failed · Retry`), to be removed by hand. A
  command's dropped receipt is recognised by dsh's message text, `File upload receipt is unknown
  for this session.` (`RECEIPT_UNKNOWN`), which a dsh bump can reword (`docs/dsh-upgrade-guide.md`
  §3.1 L1); reworded, the draft is still kept, but the files are not uploaded again on their own.
  A route change during an image's read puts the draft back unsent and says nothing. The same
  attachment in two messages shares one focus key. The thumbs' `blob:` URLs (`s.thumbs`, each a
  whole stored image) are never revoked or evicted: they hold their bytes for the page's life, a
  reload being what frees them. Whether Gravit reads a file's saved copy, and
  whether `role_pdf_page_reader` reads a page, rest on the keyed drill (§7.4), not on a test.
- **R101 — The thread, at its edges** (the dsh UI port's plan 5). Masking is display only (A2): the
  key stays in the log and in the model's context, and a copy takes the real key. Gravit's replies,
  a bot's and a job's command and output are not masked, so a key Gravit repeats shows in its
  bubble (spec §9 item 7). A URL password holding an unencoded `:` `,` `;` `(` or `)` is not masked
  (the shape fails open), and in an excerpt a key the `…` cuts before its prefix is whole (`gh…`,
  `sk…`) is not masked. A room member's Trace draws Gravit's `dispatch` unmasked, though it often
  quotes the operator's prompt. Earlier pages live in the page's memory until a reload or until a
  turn starts with the reader at the tail; while the reader reads up they stay, and one earlier
  call adds at most 40 pages (2,000 messages), so a long read-up window is drawn whole by every
  render while a turn streams (one `innerHTML` of every loaded message, its masking memoized but its
  markup and layout not). An operator image above the reader that loads
  after a prepend's keep shifts the place by its height (nothing reserves a thumb's size); Safari's
  momentum scroll can carry past the kept place. A send still pending, with no seq, puts its turn's
  mark at the end of the thread. A tool message split across an earlier page and the window drops
  the earlier page's call data (harmless while no tool call is drawn, A1). The open job's `pre` is moved
