  back into the page by every render (its text kept, but laid out again where it is re-inserted);
  folding the Finished fold while its job is open reopens it on the next render; a re-opened
  follow re-sends the whole retained output after every reconnect, the page skipping what it holds.
  Jobs vanish when the face restarts (the host's jobs live in its memory). At rc.5 a second
  `job/kill` of a settled job answers `already-finished`, not `job/not-found`.
- **R102 — The words, the sizes and the keys, at their edges** (the dsh UI port's plan 6). The
  language (plan 7's), the sizes and the fonts are per browser (`gravit-ui.prefs`): another browser
  keeps its own, and the phone's messages are untouched. A line held in state — the status line, a
  sheet's `said`, a field's `error`, a seat line or receipt, a stored report or edit error, a Run's
  conversation title (kept in dsh, the search index and `moduleRuns`) — keeps the table it was
  written in; under plan 7's switch it changes at the next line, not at the switch. The guard's
  scanner cannot see a lone lowercase word in a plain string (`'killed'`, `'failed'`: it reads like
  a status value), a capitalized word after punctuation or a hyphenated one; the probe catches them
  only in the corpus' states, so a branch the corpus never draws can still hold one, and a word the
  fixtures' own prose holds (`Paper`, `closed`, `filled`) is known to the probe wherever it is drawn.
  The Account's codes drawn as words — an open order's `pending`, `limit`, `open`, a limit's
  `payees` scope and its `ok` status — are the Account's content, not the table's (the controller's
  ruling). `P&L` stays outside the table (a value holds no `&` before a letter). Some sentences are
  still lists joined in code order (`orderWords`, the limit clauses, `Missing:`, `May send:`, the
  routes, Devices, the desk's lines, the trade fill, a module chip's `<module>: <words>`), and
  `sheet.earn.locked` and `markets.chart.sessions` read `1 days` and `The last 1 sessions` as before.
  The key bindings are the browser's to allow: until the browser drill marks one `bound: false`,
  every row is listed.

   closed for the box, not for the host loop).
26. **A peer check behind the widened `Host` fences** (R51): admit a non-loopback peer at the
   Account only from the compose network's peer (or with a shared token), and gate the face's
   `/data` on the cookie when `FACE_BIND` widens the bind. One middleware condition each; it changes
   the door's admission, so it waits for its own small design.
27. **The composed-answer drill.** The keyed drill (`face/README.md` "The composed-answer
   drill") on the operator's face: a live `cn-market` run that ends in a composed answer, the notes
   folded, the slider moving the cursor, the times in China time, then plan 3's half — a ladder
   name's drawer and its limit line, Escape, a follow-up, `Open run ›` — not yet run. Plan 3 (the
   stock drawer, clickable stock names, the drawn choices, the `yesterday` and `signals` blocks and
   the footer's `Open run ›`) is built. R52 is the residual a pinned answer would close.

## Appendix A — Environment variable index

| Variable | Layer | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `FACE_ACCOUNT_SEAT_DIR`, `FACE_ACCOUNT_URL` | `account-seat.ts`, `seat.ts`, `account-proxy.ts`, `phone.ts`, `scripts/watchdog.ts` | the Account package the seat runs from (default the repo's `account/`) and the service the seat, the seat box, the proxy, the desk's phone and the watchdog reach (§4.6) |
| `FACE_MARKET_DIR`, `FACE_MARKET_URL` | `market-row.ts`, `market-proxy.ts`; `lib/market-fetch.mjs` (the Lunhui freezes) | the market package `market:mcp` runs from (default the repo's `market/`) and the market the `mcp-market` row, the market proxy, the desk's quotes and the Lunhui freezes read, default `http://127.0.0.1:4821`; the proxy follows the row as composed, the freezes this variable alone (§4.6) |
| `MARKET_URL` | `market/src/mcp.ts` (the `mcp-market` row's `env`) | the market `market:mcp` asks, default `http://127.0.0.1:4821` (§3.10) |
| `FACE_BIND` | `overlay.ts`, `main.ts`, `docker-entrypoint.sh` | the face webserver's bind, a concrete address; the container's own (`hostname -i`) in the compose agent box only (§4.3, §4.6) |
| `PORTFOLIO_BIND`, `PORTFOLIO_HOSTS` | `account/src/portfolio/server.ts` | the Account's listener and its admitted extra `Host` values, compose's Account box only (§3.9) |
| `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` | dsh credential seam | the LLM and `web_search` |
| `DSH_HOME` | dsh, face | harness home |
| `DSH_PERMISSION_MODE` | dsh | sandbox preset; `danger-full-access` ⇒ approval policy `never` |
| `DSH_TELEMETRY_DISABLED` | face boot | any non-empty value disables telemetry; composed after the operator layers, it still wins over an operator's re-enable of the row the policy layer disables |
| `FACE_PORT`, `FACE_PROFILE` | face | port, profile name |
| `MARKET_AKSHARE_BIN` | the market (`live/akshare.ts`, §3.10) | the AKShare sidecar's executable, default `~/.local/bin/akshare-mcp`; the market image sets `/usr/local/bin/akshare-mcp` |
| `MARKET_BIND`, `MARKET_HOSTS` | `market/src/server.ts` | the market's listener and its admitted extra `Host` values, compose's market box only (§3.10) |
| `PORTFOLIO_MARKET_URL` | `account/src/portfolio/server.ts`, `account-check.ts` | the market the Account reads, default `http://127.0.0.1:4821` (§3.10) |
| `IFIND_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `IFIND_REFRESH_TOKEN` | the market (`cn-ifind.ts`, §3.10) | the Lunhui boards stand-in's iFinD credential, held by the market alone |
| `FACE_SMOKE` | face tests | enables the 30 smoke files (35 real boots) |
| `FASTMCP_LOG_LEVEL` | the market's AKShare sidecar (a FastMCP server; one of the names its child inherits) | `WARNING` silences FastMCP's INFO noise |
| `FACE_PYTHON` | face (`desk.ts`) | the interpreter a standing order's `.py` script producer runs under, `-I`, default `python3`; none ships, and the market clock needs none |
| `FACE_DESK` | face (`main.ts`) | `0` mounts none of the desk's rows (no ledger events, no sleep watch, no desk conversation, no phone bridge, no Gate 2 card notice); `/data/desk/status` and the Pause route still answer |
| `FACE_DESK_MODEL` | face (`main.ts`, `resolveDeskRoute`) | the desk session's model route, default `deepseek-official/deepseek-flash`; an unusable one falls back to the tree's default selection, Gravit's, with one line |
| `ACCOUNT_TELEGRAM_API` | the account (`identity/bot-api.ts`) | the Bot API base for tests and smokes, honoured only as `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`; default `https://api.telegram.org` (§3.9, §4.6) |
| `ACCOUNT_SLACK_API` | the account (`identity/slack-api.ts`) and the watchdog | the Slack Web API base for tests and smokes, honoured only as `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` (or that and `/api`); default `https://slack.com/api` (§3.9, §4.6) |
| `FACE_ACCOUNT_HOME`, `BUYER_HOME` | `scripts/watchdog.ts`; `BUYER_HOME` the account's own home too | the account's home whose Telegram token file the watchdog reads, only to say the account is down; default `~/.buyer-agent-demo` (§4.6). No `TELEGRAM_*` name is read anywhere since plan B1a |
| `ALPHA_EDGAR_USER_AGENT` | face (`desk.ts`, for the watch's filings) | the contact email SEC asks for, the EDGAR requests' `User-Agent`; unset, no filing is fetched (§4.6) |

The Python package's variables — the two APCA keys and `APCA_API_BASE_URL`, `ALPHA_DATA_SOURCE`,
`ALPHA_PIT_ROOT`, `ALPHA_DATA_FEED`, `ALPHA_DATA_COMPOSITE*`, `ALPHA_UNIVERSE_SCREEN`, the three
`ALPHA_*_USER_AGENT`, the order flag — and the producers' interpreter variable are read nowhere
since 2026-10-24, but for `ALPHA_EDGAR_USER_AGENT`, which the desk's watch reads again since P3; `agents.ts` keeps the two APCA names on its scrub list (§4.6).
